items.title: fix(extract): keep file and declaration IDs distinct (#4854)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4854. A file and a declaration inside it no longer share an id.

The file id is the extensionless stem, a declaration id is `make_id(stem, name)`, and the parse-time file id is `make_id(path)`. When a declaration's normalized name equals the file extension, both recipes land on one string, and `add_node` silently keeps the first:

```text
a.js   class Js

before
  file id     make_id("a.js")      -> a_js
  class id    make_id("a", "Js")   -> a_js      same string
  add_node(class)                  -> a_js in seen_ids, return
  add_edge(file, class, contains)  -> a_js -> a_js
  flags on class_nid               -> file becomes _callable_class
  method id   make_id(a_js, run)   -> a_js_run   owned by the file

after
  registry.resolve(a_js, "Js", "type")
    a_js is reserved by the file
    -> a_js_b692bab43393
  decl_node adds the class under the salted id
    -> a_js -> a_js_b692bab43393 contains
    -> a_js_b692bab43393 -> a_js_b692bab43393_run method
```

Two invariants are enforced:

```text
unique    an id is assigned only after an availability check against the
          file id, the taken node ids, and the ids assigned to declarations
stable    the same declaration resolves to its assigned id on a re-walk
          (reopened classes, cfg twins), and unaffected files keep their ids
referenced a reference to the declaration uses the declared id, not a
          per-file id derived from the referring file
```

The registry keys ownership by the id the declaration would have used, so `Foo` and `_Foo`, or `Base` in two namespaces, stay distinct. A lookup by name only answers when one declaration in the file spells it.

Cross-file references needed a second change. `ensure_named_node` is per file, so a reference in `b.ts` to `Ts` in `a.ts` was minted from `b.ts`'s stem, which is `b.ts`'s own file id:

```diff
 b.ts   import { Ts } from "./a";  @Ts class Other {}

 before
-  Other --references--> b.ts        (the referring file)
   no edge to the class

 after
+  Other --references--> Ts (a.ts)
   corpus map: (resolved path, normalized name) -> declared id
   import fact selects the module, path-keyed, so two modules may declare Ts
```

## Evidence

The test commit is red on the base tree. The implementation commits flip it green, one concern at a time:

| commit | new test file |
|---|---|
| `1517f89e` tests only, base code | 61 failed, 9 passed |
| `bcea646b` registry and mint sites | 2 failed, 68 passed (`Other -> b.ts` remains) |
| `6755a5a7` corpus map | 1 failed, 69 passed (schema pin) |
| `9290d9fc` schema 30 | 70 passed, 1 skipped |

The cases that failed on the experiment branch and now pass:

```text
class Js {} + export const $b692bab43393 = 1     before: const dropped
                                                after:  both nodes, distinct ids

a.ts export class Ts
b.ts @Ts class Other                            before: Other -> references -> b.ts
                                                after:  Other -> references -> Ts (a.ts)

a1.ts, a2.ts both export Ts
b.ts imports a1 and @Ts                         after:  binds a1's Ts, not a2's
```

Full suite, no env var:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly
9036 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed, 2398 warnings in 556.48s

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_file_id_collision_4854.py
70 passed, 1 skipped   (twice in a row, cold and warm)
```

The 71 parametrized cases cover JS, TS, Python, Java, PHP, Ruby, C++, C headers, Rust, Go, C#, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, and Julia. One skip: C++ namespace declarations are not modeled by the extractor, confirmed by the control name.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a node id is unique in the corpus, a declaration's id is stable across runs, and every reference to that declaration uses it. The tests assert behaviour (labels, source files, edges, build labels), not the helper.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (bug fix).
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented the **limitations** below.

## How was this tested?

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_file_id_collision_4854.py
  70 passed, 1 skipped

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_extract.py tests/test_build.py \
    tests/test_cache.py tests/test_dedup.py tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py \
    tests/test_file_node_id_spec.py
  624 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly
  9036 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed in 556.48s
```

The targeted extraction, build, cache, dedup, and existing id-collision tests ran after the fix. The full suite ran on the final tree with no environment variables set.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. A revert restores the previous ids for the colliding declarations only; unaffected files keep the same ids before and after. The one persisted change is the AST cache schema, and reverting the code makes the schema-30 entries miss and re-extract, which is safe.

**Blast Radius:** narrow, but corpus-wide in code paths. The behaviour change applies to every language that mints declaration ids through the engine, plus Rust, Go, and Julia. It only fires when a declaration name normalizes to the file extension (`Js` in `.js`, `Ts` in `.ts`, `Java` in `.java`, and so on), so ordinary files produce byte-identical ids. `build()` keeps the file and the declaration for each fixture; no self-contains edges remain.

**Schema:** `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` is 30 (base 29). Cached per-file results under 29 carry the dropped declaration, so they are ignored and re-extracted. An existing `graph.json` built before this change keeps the missing class until a full rebuild: `graphify update` only re-extracts changed files, so delete `graphify-out/` or pass a fresh `--out` once after upgrading.

**Limitations**

- Cross-file references: decorator and inheritance are covered. `new Ts()` and TS type annotations do not emit a cross-file reference edge in this extractor today, so no test claims them.
- Standalone extractors: rust, go, and julia use the registry at their choke points. Apex, Bash, Dart, DM, Elixir, Erlang, Fortran, Markdown, Objective-C, OCaml, Pascal/Pascal Forms, PowerShell, R, Robot, Solidity, SQL, VB.NET, Verilog, Zig, and the YAML/JSON/Terraform config extractors still mint from the file stem and are not covered here. The zoo does not test them.
- C++ namespace declarations are not modeled, which is why the zoo skips that kind.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no fragments touched.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). The registry is per-file and ordered by the walk; no env switch.
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages. (No trailer in the commit messages.)

items.title: test(extract): cover --out semantic cache reuse and root pairing (#4831)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds regression coverage for #4831. No behaviour change: one line in `cli.py` makes an existing pair of roots explicit, everything else is tests.

The bug was a root mix-up. `extract <dir> --out <other>` passed `root=out_root` to both semantic cache calls. `save_semantic_cache` resolved the model's corpus-relative `source_file` against the output root, so `is_file()` failed for every group and nothing was written. The manifest join failed the same way, so no doc got a `semantic_hash` and run 2 re-extracted the whole docs corpus. The code fixes landed upstream in 0.9.17 (manifest stamping) and 0.9.20 (`root=target, cache_root=out_root`).

Two coverage gaps were left behind:

```text
                                                      existing suite
save path writes entries under --out                  covered, indirectly (#2927)
check path reads what the save wrote                  uncovered
a new caller omits cache_root                         uncovered
two runs with --out spend nothing on run 2            uncovered
```

The two additions map to the reporter's shapes:

```text
run 1                              run 2
3 docs dispatched                  no source change:       0 dispatched
3 entries under --out              doc rows removed:       0 dispatched, 3 cache hits
corpus stays clean                 both runs:              every doc stamped
```

and to the call sites:

```diff
 _check_semantic_cache(sem_paths_file, root=target, cache_root=out_root)
 _save_semantic_cache(nodes, root=target, cache_root=out_root, ...)
-check_semantic_cache(files, root, mode=cache_mode, ...)
+check_semantic_cache(files, root=root, cache_root=root, mode=cache_mode, ...)
```

### Commits

```text
3559d763  test(extract): assert --out reuses the semantic cache across runs (#4831)
d76d11cf  test(cache): pin both roots on every semantic cache call site (#4831)
```

## Evidence

Mutate the historical call shape back into `cli.py` (`root=out_root`, `cache_root` dropped) and run this branch:

| mutation | existing suite | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| save call, both roots dropped | 1 failure, incidental (#2927) | 3 failures |
| check call only | **0 failures** (56 green) | 2 failures |
| a new caller omits `cache_root` | 0 failures (35 green) | guard fails |

The check-side row is the gap: nothing in the suite consumed a cache entry the manifest had not already stamped, so the read path was never exercised under `--out`.

```text
tests/test_extract_out_semantic_cache.py   2 passed
tests/test_semantic_cache_call_sites.py    3 passed
full suite                                8971 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed (8m35s)
```

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a path that names a source file resolves against the corpus root, the cache lives under the output root, and every call site states both. The runtime tests prove the composite behaviour; the static guard proves the pairing at call sites that runtime tests never reach.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary (tests, plus one keyword pair that changes no behaviour).
- [x] Added a **regression test** or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Nothing persisted changes shape. No cache key, manifest key, schema, or file format is touched, so a revert restores the exact previous test count and behaviour.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. This is test-only apart from one explicit keyword pair.

- `cache-check` passes the corpus as both roots. It has no `--out`, so the call is byte-identical in effect; the keywords make the two roles visible.
- `save_semantic_cache` and `check_semantic_cache` keep their signatures. The 32 call sites inside generated skill snippets (single root, no `--out`) stay valid.
- The guard walks `graphify/**/*.py`. It fails if a fourth caller appears without both keywords, which is the point.
- The tests stub `extract_corpus_parallel`, so they add no network use and no tokens to CI.

**Limitations**

- The guard does not scan the generated skill markdown, where a single root is legitimate. It covers production Python only.
- The CLI tests drive `main()` in process with a stubbed backend. They do not exercise `claude-cli` or provider-specific paths.
- Not tested on Windows. The tests use `tmp_path` and the same path rules as the rest of the suite.

## How was this tested?

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_extract_out_semantic_cache.py tests/test_semantic_cache_call_sites.py -q
  -> 5 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q -p no:randomly
  -> 8971 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed in 515.35s

# mutation checks (temporary edit, then reverted)
save call  root=out_root                    -> 3 failed
check call root=out_root                    -> 2 failed
new module calling save_semantic_cache(root=) -> guard failed, runtime suite green
```

items.title: fix(csharp): bind classic extension-method calls to their declaration (#4828)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4828.

`value.Mask()` to a classic `this`-parameter extension produced no `calls` edge. `graphify explain ".Mask()"` listed zero callers, so a widely used helper looked dead. In the reporter's ~40k-node corpus one helper had 9 call sites and 0 callers, and the corpus declares 185 distinct extension method names.

The resolver implemented one dispatch rule. C# has two:

```text
nominal    caller ──calls──▶ member of receiver_type ∪ inherits*(receiver_type)
extension  caller ──calls──▶ `this`-parameter method on a static class,
                             receiver passed as argument 0
```

`_resolve_csharp_member_calls` implements the first. An extension is declared on a sibling static class, so the lookup found nothing and the call was dropped. Two facts were also missing before any pass could join them: `_csharp_method_signature` detected the `this` modifier but used it only to compute `min_arity`, and `_csharp_receiver_type_name` rejected every lowercase type, so `string` and `int` receivers were never typed.

This PR records the join key and adds the second dispatch arm:

```diff
 method node (.cs)
+  extension: true
+  extended_type: "Widget"        # simple name of the `this` parameter's type
+  extended_type_arity: 0
+  extended_is_type_param: true   # `this T`
 raw_call
+  receiver_type: "string"        # primitives are typed now (`this string`)
+  ──▶ csharp_extension_calls resolver (after the nominal pass)
```

Binding rules, all fail-closed:

| rule | why |
|---|---|
| receiver type is declared in the corpus and its base chain is fully resolved | an out-of-corpus base may declare an instance member of that name, and that member wins |
| receiver type declares no instance member of that name | instance dispatch beats extension dispatch |
| declaring namespace is visible at the call site, innermost level first | a file-level `using` belongs to the compilation unit, so an inner-namespace extension wins |
| extended type is the receiver type, a resolved base, or an implemented interface | C# applicability |
| declaration accepts the call's argument count (`min_arity`/`arity`, receiver consumes one parameter) | overload choice, reusing #4584 |
| exactly one survivor | a tie is ambiguous and binds nothing |

Out-of-corpus receivers (`string`, `int`, third-party) and untyped chained receivers (`v.ToString().Mask()`) cannot have their instance members enumerated. They need two conservative proofs instead: the member name is not one a BCL type owns, and no regular method in the corpus spells it. Such edges are INFERRED 0.75. A receiver typed by the extractor's declaration table scores 0.85.

### Six commits

```text
83227a76  fix(csharp): record extension-method facts and primitive receiver types
cc81da11  feat(csharp): bind extension calls on typed receivers
44812501  feat(csharp): bind extension calls on primitive and third-party receivers
b94e90e8  feat(csharp): bind extension calls on chained receivers
fb7ccabd  test(csharp): score candidates against the production BCL deny-list
be14c4c1  fix(csharp): use the 0.75 discrete tier for guarded extension edges
```

Stage 1 is provably sound on its own. Stages 2 and 3 only add recall, and each is a separate commit so it can be reverted without touching the others. Reverting the whole branch restores the previous graph output, because the pass only appends edges.

## Evidence

The reporter's corpus, before and after:

```text
before
  Connections (1):
    <-- StringExtensions [method] [EXTRACTED] Ext.cs:L3

after
  Connections (3):
    <-- StringExtensions [method] [EXTRACTED] Ext.cs:L3
    <-- .A() [calls] [INFERRED] Svc.cs:L3
    <-- .B() [calls] [INFERRED] Svc.cs:L4
```

The "after" block matches the issue's expected output, including the chained `v.ToString().Mask()` line.

Each rule was scored against fixtures before it landed. 15 fixtures with ground truth decidable from the C# spec, 10 candidate strategies, measured on the nominal graph:

| strategy | recall | false edges |
|---|---|---|
| scope + assignability + poison (stage 1) | 15/22 | 0 |
| + guarded out-of-corpus receivers (stage 2) | 20/22 | 0 |
| + untyped receivers (stage 3) | 21/22 | 0 |
| out-of-corpus receivers without the deny-list | 21/22 | 1 |
| the reporter's local patch | 18/22 | 2 |
| bare-name fallback | 15/22 | 4 |

`test_strategy_matrix` pins every trade in that table. No scope check binds an unimported extension. No poison check binds through an unknown base. No deny-list binds `PropertyInfo.GetValue`. The bare-name fallback reproduces the #1609 god-node edge.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant is that a `calls` edge exists only when the graph can prove which declaration the compiler would choose. Every new rule is a C# resolution rule, and every uncertain input resolves to "no edge" rather than a guess.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary (the two extractor changes are the minimum facts the binding pass needs; the pass is additive).
- [x] Added a **regression test** (9 metadata tests, 57 production-truth tests, and the 10-strategy decision record).
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No file-format change. The AST cache schema moves 29 → 30 so cached `.cs` extractions re-run once; stale cache entries cannot bind because they lack the new metadata. Reverting the branch restores the old edges exactly, since nothing is retargeted or removed.

**Blast Radius:** moderate. This changes which callers a C# graph reports.

- New edges are `calls` / INFERRED only.
- The pass runs after the nominal pass and skips any `(caller, target)` pair that already exists, so `WidgetExtensions.Paint(w)` keeps its EXTRACTED edge.
- A wrong edge needs the name proofs to agree on the wrong declaration, or an instance member the corpus cannot see. The 0.75 tier marks edges that rest on name proofs rather than a typed receiver.
- Communities, reports, and `explain` output for C# corpora will gain callers that were previously missing.
- `--force` and explicit `changed_paths` paths are unaffected; the resolver is additive.

**Limitations**

- The BCL deny-list is a heuristic. An extension whose name matches a BCL member does not bind through an out-of-corpus receiver, and neither does one whose name a regular method in the corpus already uses. `string.ToInt32()` next to an unrelated `Conv.ToInt32()` is pinned as a known miss.
- Generic extended types compare by simple name. The receiver table strips generic arguments, so `this Box<int>` is not told apart from a `Box<string>` receiver.
- Chained receivers use the untyped rung. No return-type inference is added.
- A field chain (`x.F.M()`) is skipped: it needs `F`'s declared type, not `x`'s.
- Call sites in `.razor`/`.cshtml` keep the pre-existing gap; the nominal C# member resolver is `.cs`-only too.

## How was this tested?

```text
tests/test_csharp_extension_metadata.py     9 passed
tests/test_csharp_extension_resolution.py  57 passed
tests/test_csharp_extension_calls.py      169 passed, 96 skipped
full suite (tests/)                      9201 passed, 113 skipped, 1 xfailed
```

`test_csharp_extension_metadata.py` pins the declaration facts: extended type, generic arity, qualified `this App.Widget`, `this T`, `this object`, primitive receiver typing, and that a `string` receiver is not parked as a cross-repo candidate.

`test_csharp_extension_resolution.py` runs the real pipeline against every fixture. `expect` edges must exist, `forbid` edges must not, from stage 1 onward. The stage list is explicit, so a later commit can add recall but not a false edge.

`test_csharp_extension_calls.py` is the executable decision record. It extracts each fixture with the production extension resolver removed from the registry, so candidate numbers stay comparable across stages, then asserts the matrix and eight discriminators: scope, scope level, assignability, poison, out-of-corpus rung, deny-list, untyped rung, and metadata versus signature parsing. The 96 skips are parametrized cases a candidate is not required to reach.

Also run:

```text
graphify update .   -> 23,376 nodes, 48,940 edges
```

Not tested: Windows.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no skill fragments touched.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). The new metadata is read from the AST; the resolver consumes graph facts only.
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages. (No trailer in the commit messages.)

items.title: fix(skill): stop an --update re-read from stamping a doc whose chunk failed (#4811)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

labels.name: needs:title
labels.description: PR title should follow the conventional-commit format

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4811. An `--update` marks a changed doc as done when its chunk failed, so the doc is never re-queued and the graph keeps its pre-edit nodes.

The sequence: the merge block reads this run's extraction from `graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json`, stamps the manifest from it (#2015/#1948), then overwrites the same file with the whole merged graph so Steps 4-8 can read it. From that moment the file no longer means "what this run produced" — it is mostly old nodes from `graph.json`, with nothing on disk saying which is which. Anything that re-reads it as this run's output stamps the doc:

- a second run of the merge block in the same update (e.g. after a later step fails);
- core Step 9, which agents run after an update (#837).

The fix writes a snapshot of this run's extraction, plus the partial set B3.5 wrote, before the merge overwrites the working file. The merge block's manifest save and Step 9 both stamp from that snapshot. The partial set travels with the payload, so the #4807/#4814 exclusion still holds after the merge block deletes `.graphify_partial.txt`.

Three commits, each independently revertable:

1. `test(skill): pin the #4811 stamped-failed-doc gap` — 12 scenarios over the real rendered blocks, red on the current runbook.
2. `fix(skill): snapshot this run's extraction before the update merge` — the writer, the lifecycle, and the merge-block save. Turns the merge-rerun scenarios green.
3. `fix(skill): stamp Step 9 from this run's extraction snapshot` — the second reader.

**Stacked on #4832** (`fix/4814-partial-list-lifecycle`, currently open). That PR adds the run-start delete hooks this change extends, and its list-consumption line is the reason the partial set has to travel inside the snapshot. Until #4832 merges, this PR's diff includes its three commits.

**Design choice.** I measured eight candidate designs against the same 12-scenario matrix (each driven through the real rendered blocks and scored with the real `detect_incremental`):

```text
policy                     S1   S2   S3   S4   S5   S6   S7   S8   S9  S10  S11  S12   score
baseline                    X    X    X    X   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok    X   7/12
snapshot at merge, raw, list kept
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
snapshot at merge, self-contained  <- chosen
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
snapshot at merge, no start delete
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok    X   ok   ok   ok    X   ok  10/12
stamp from .graphify_semantic.json, list kept
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
stamp from .graphify_semantic.json, shipped list lifecycle
                           ok   ok    X    X   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  10/12
snapshot gated by a per-run id
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
snapshot at the producer (Part C)
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
```

S1/S2 = failed chunk then merge re-run / Step 9. S3/S4 = partly read doc. S5/S6 = success controls. S7 = failed update then a clean full build. S8 code-only. S9 deletion-only. S10 full-build failed-chunk control. S11 second update after a failure. S12 precision.

Why the chosen design over the others:

- The two smallest fixes (semantic-only, and raw snapshot + keep the list) both require reverting #4832's "consume and remove the list" line. The self-contained snapshot leaves that PR's list lifecycle untouched, so the two changes do not conflict.
- S7 and S11 are why the snapshot needs delete-at-start: without it, a snapshot from a failed update poisons a later successful full build and a later successful update.
- The run-id design scores the same but adds a persistent file plus a filter every reader must apply — the cost #4832 measured and rejected for the partial list.
- The producer design scores the same but edits the shared core Part C block (all 13 hosts, full builds included) and still needs a merge-side writer for the deletion-only path.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a file is stamped only when a value that describes **this run** says it produced output, and that value cannot be rewritten before every reader has read it. Step 9 and the merge block now read the same immutable snapshot; the snapshot is written once per run, before the merge, and cleared at every run start.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

The issue's reproduction, before and after:

```text
before (at 2af27a8e)
  $ python merge_rerun_repro.py rerun
  after a second merge, next --update queues: []
  $ python merge_rerun_repro.py step9
  after Step 9, next --update queues: []

after
  $ python merge_rerun_repro.py rerun

```

After:

```text

after the full build, next --update queues: []
```

items.title: fix(watch): record a contended incremental request instead of dropping it (#4800)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4800, stacked on #4801. That PR gives `graphify update` a change set derived
from the manifest. A request built that way names no paths, and this PR is what
happens when such a request loses the per-repo lock.

`_rebuild_code` asks for the lock before it does anything. If another rebuild holds
it, each request kind records what it could not do so the holder can run it later:

```python
if not block_on_lock:
    if incremental and changed_paths is None:
        pass                                # writes NOTHING
    elif changed_paths is None:
        _queue_pending_full(out)            # "re-extract everything"
    elif changed_paths:
        _queue_pending(out, changed_paths)  # "re-extract these files"
```

The derived kind has no path list to append and cannot use `.pending_full`: the drain
runs after the lock it just won, so a full marker would upgrade its own incremental
pass. So it recorded nothing, printed "nothing to queue", and returned `False`, which
is the same answer a caller gets when its change set *was* recorded and will run.

The review bot on #4801 flags this at `graphify/watch.py:1979`, rated high. This PR
closes that finding.

```diff
 _rebuild_code(..., incremental=True, block_on_lock=False)
   if incremental and changed_paths is None:
-    pass
+    _queue_pending_incremental(out)     # a third marker, written before the attempt
+    queued = True

   # inside the lock, whichever process holds it
+  queued_incremental = _drain_pending_incremental(out)
+  incremental_effective = incremental or queued_incremental
-  if queued_full:      full = True
-  elif changed_paths is None:  full = not incremental
+  if queued_full:      full = True     # a full request still wins
+  elif changed_paths is None:  full = not incremental_effective
   else:                full = False
```

An explicit `changed_paths` still wins, and `.pending_full` still wins over
everything. The late-arrival loop drains the third marker too and breaks only when
all three records are empty.

### Three commits

```text
a82abc60  test(watch): pin the lock-queue contract for the existing request kinds
acb92bf5  fix(watch): record a contended incremental request instead of dropping it
9ce7e721  docs(watch): describe the three queue request kinds
```

The first is pure coverage of the contract that already holds for the other two kinds
(`.pending_full` / `.pending_changes` semantics, and a caller that wins the lock not
upgrading itself). It passes on the base branch. The second adds the marker, the
wiring and the tests for it, in one commit, so a revert removes the behaviour and its
tests together. The third updates comments that described two kinds.

### The contract the tests pin

`tests/test_update_lock_contention.py`, six tests, real lock and real queue files, no
monkeypatching. Contention is created by holding the lock in-process; `flock` is per
open file description, so a second open in the same process conflicts:

```text
I1  a contended incremental request leaves a record a drain can act on
    ...and `.pending_incremental` is written on contention, drained once, then absent
I2  a caller that WINS the lock runs the pass it asked for, never a full one
    driven by a record it left itself
I3  the record drives the work through the winner's drain
I4  `.pending_full` / `.pending_changes` keep their meaning, and a queued full
    marker still upgrades a blocking incremental caller
```

I3 is the one worth reading. The call that ends up doing the work asks for the
*default* pass, which is a full one, so a single re-extracted file can only come from
the winner's own drain honouring the marker. Calling `_rebuild_code(incremental=True)`
again and calling that "honoured" would be the test re-asking, which proves nothing
about the queue.

No sleeps. Content changes carry an explicit `os.utime` bump, so nothing depends on
filesystem timestamp granularity.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A request that loses the lock must either leave something the holder can act on, or
tell its caller it was not served. It must not return the same `False` that means
"queued and will run".

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. One new marker file under `graphify-out/` and the drain that reads
it. Reverting the middle commit removes the behaviour and its tests together.

**Blast Radius:** narrow, and limited to builds that lose the lock:

- A build that wins the lock behaves exactly as before, except that a marker left by
  another process is now honoured: the winner runs an incremental pass rather than a
  full one when no explicit paths and no full marker are present.
- `.pending_full` still wins over everything, and an explicit `changed_paths` still
  wins over the derived set.
- The marker is written before the lock attempt, as the other two records are. The
  write-before-lock order is deliberate and unchanged: reversing it broke
  `tests/test_watch.py::test_rebuild_code_empty_change_set_does_not_claim_queued`
  (#4274) in an earlier attempt at this area.
- A stale marker left by a crash asks for one extra derived pass. That pass is a
  content diff, so it is cheap and it cannot miss work.

**Limitations**

- **This is design completion, not an incident fix.** No non-blocking incremental
  caller exists today: `graphify update` blocks on the lock, and the watcher and the
  hooks pass explicit paths, so they use `.pending_changes`. The hole opens the day
  something calls `_rebuild_code(incremental=True)` without blocking, which is a
  reasonable thing to add later.
- **The winner's pass becomes incremental when a marker is queued,** including when
  the winner's own request was a full one. That is the intended semantics (a queued
  incremental request has to be honoured), and it is what I3 pins. A full request
  still wins if `.pending_full` is also present.
- **An older graphify ignores the marker.** It does not know the file, so it behaves
  as it does today: the request is dropped. Nothing breaks.
- **One test needed an adaptation for the 0.9.96 gate.**
  `test_i4_a_queued_full_marker_still_upgrades_a_blocking_incremental_caller` queues a
  marker and expects a full pass, but the gate runs before the drain, so an untouched
  tree returns at the gate and never reaches the queue. It now carries one change
  first, the same way `test_default_is_the_full_path` in #4801 does. The assertion is
  unchanged.

## How was this tested?

Red on the base branch, for the intended reason:

```text
E  AssertionError: a contended incremental request was dropped: it left no pending
   record and its caller got an indistinguishable result (outcome=False, pending=[])
FAILED tests/test_update_lock_contention.py::test_i1_contended_incremental_request_is_not_silently_dropped
```

Green with the fix, including the mutation check. Removing the marker write from
commit 2 puts both I1 tests back to red, which is how I know they are not vacuous:

```text
MUTATION, marker write removed -> 2 failed (I1 and the marker lifecycle)
restored                        -> 6 passed
```

```text
tests/test_update_lock_contention.py       -> 6 passed
tests/test_update_incremental.py           -> 17 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q              -> 8895 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed in 411.72s
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/ tests/test_update_lock_contention.py
                                           -> All checks passed
```

8895 is #4801's 8889 plus the six tests here. The suite ran with `PYTHONPATH` set to
the repo, so the tests that shell out via `sys.executable -m graphify` load this tree
rather than the installed package.

Diffstat against the base branch:

```text
 graphify/watch.py                    |  66 +++++++++--
 tests/test_update_lock_contention.py | 219 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 273 insertions(+), 12 deletions(-)
```

Not tested: Windows. The marker uses the same `Path.touch()` / `unlink()` pattern as
the two existing records.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no skill fragments touched.)

items.title: perf(update): re-extract only the files whose content changed (#4800)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

labels.name: needs:title
labels.description: PR title should follow the conventional-commit format

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4800. `graphify update` pays for the whole corpus however little changed.
0.9.96 shipped the zero-change half (#4748): an untouched tree returns at the gate in
1.96 s. Change one file and the run costs 68.15 s again, because the gate can only
answer "all unchanged" or "not all unchanged", and nothing derives *which* files
differ.

Seven stages run, and only the first two read source text:

```text
scan ──> extract ──> build ──> cluster ──> analyze ──> report ──> export
disk     parse       graph     communities  findings     md/html
```

Everything downstream works on the graph, so a two-file edit paid for all seven
stages. This PR gives `update` a change set:

```diff
 _rebuild_code(watch_path, incremental=True)
   detect(watch_path)
+  changed_paths = manifest diff of the scan
+                  rows whose ast_hash moved, plus rows whose file is gone
   if changed_paths is not None:
     extract only those
     preserve every other file's nodes
     hand the unchanged corpus's AST nodes to extract() as resolution context
-  else: extract the whole corpus        <- what `update` always did
   extract -> build -> cluster -> analyze -> report -> export
```

On the issue's corpus (1,059 scanned files, one process per run): 68.15 s and
1,071 MB becomes 48.72 s and 537 MB. The stages after extraction still work over
every node, which is why this is 19 seconds and not 66. That is called out under
Limitations rather than buried.

The manifest already stores a content hash per file, and `_rebuild_code` has taken
`changed_paths` since the hook work. The only caller that ever passed one was git:
`post-commit` diffs HEAD and forwards the touched paths. `update` passed nothing,
which the function documents as "the full code corpus". So the missing piece was a
change set that does not depend on git. It is written with paths relative to the
scan root, so a copied checkout carries a usable baseline.

### The rule the change set is built on

A false "changed" costs time. A false "unchanged" ships a graph that describes code
the reader no longer has. Every uncertain answer therefore resolves to "changed":

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| has this file changed? | content hash, never mtime alone. A checkout or `rsync --times` moves mtime with identical bytes; a same-second rewrite leaves it put |
| no row for it? | changed. Nothing describes it, so it was not in the last build |
| manifest missing, unreadable, or naming another tree? | full path. Unknown is not "nothing changed" |
| file gone from disk? | changed, and it must reach the deleted branch, or its nodes survive and the shrink guard refuses the write |

### Five commits

```text
34333812  refactor(detect): expose the changed set for a root
5c02c991  feat(watch): derive changed_paths from the manifest in _rebuild_code (#4740)
78be63ab  feat(cli): use the incremental path for update (#4740)
2de3b0d0  fix(watch): keep cross-file resolution edges for the changed set (#4740)
0ea45d78  test(watch): make the default-path assertion robust to the no-change gate (#4740)
```

The split is deliberate. The refactor is behaviour-neutral and provable as such.
The capability is default-off, so the watcher and the post-checkout hook are
untouched. The CLI flag is its own commit, so reverting it returns `update` to
full-corpus while the capability stays.

The commit subjects say `#4740`, the umbrella issue this work started under. This PR
fixes #4800, its scoped successor. #4748 already landed the gate this branch sits on.

Two of the commits are correctness fixes, and the new caller is what exposed them.
Deriving a change set means only the changed files are parsed, so a call from a
changed file into an unchanged one can lose its edge (#2406/#3763). v8 answers that
by passing the unchanged corpus's AST nodes as resolution context. Commit `2de3b0d0`
fixes the case where that context came back empty: the membership test anchored
stored paths via `identity()`, which resolves against the tree recorded in
`graphify-out/.graphify_root`, while the set it was compared against was built with
`absolute_identity(..., project_root)`. On a copied checkout the marker still names
the original tree, so every stored node read as corpus-absent. Two lines, same
anchoring on both sides.

### The stacked PR

```text
fix/4800-incremental-lock-drop   records a contended incremental request instead of dropping it
```

`_rebuild_code` can lose the per-repo lock. The other two request kinds record what
they could not do, in `.pending_full` and `.pending_changes`. A manifest-derived
request names no paths, so before that PR it records nothing and returns the same
`False` that a queued request returns. That PR adds `.pending_incremental`.

It is latent today: every non-blocking caller passes explicit paths, and `update`
blocks on the lock. So this PR is complete on its own for the CLI path, and the stack
closes the hole for a future non-blocking incremental caller. I would rather say that
than let a reviewer find it.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (the reported symptom is cost)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [x] Refactor (the first commit only)
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A partial rebuild is sound only if its key covers every input that reaches the graph,
and the cost of being wrong is asymmetric: over-reporting costs time, under-reporting
ships a stale graph.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No schema, cache-key or file-format change. Reverting the CLI
commit alone returns `update` to full-corpus rebuilds.

**Blast Radius:** moderate, because this decides what gets re-extracted:

- The change set is content-addressed, so a false "unchanged" needs identical bytes
  plus a matching manifest row. Everything else falls back to the full path.
- A new file has no row and therefore always re-extracts.
- A deleted file is carried into the change set so its nodes are evicted and the
  shrink guard can attribute the loss.
- `incremental` defaults to off, so the watcher, the post-checkout hook and every
  existing caller keep the full path.
- The first commit is a pure refactor. `detect_incremental` calls the factored
  helpers with the same arguments; I checked the output matches the inline version on
  a corpus with an edit, a delete and an add, for both `kind="ast"` and
  `kind="semantic"`.
- `--force` still means a full rebuild. An explicit `changed_paths` still wins over
  the derived set.
- The gate still runs first, so a tree it can skip costs what it costs today (1.96 s
  here). The change set is only computed when the gate declines.

**Limitations**

- **Extraction is only part of the run.** Build, cluster, analyze, report and export
  still work over every node, so 68 s becomes 49 s rather than seconds. On this
  corpus the JS/TS resolution pass re-parses the TypeScript files too, because those
  suffixes bypass the AST cache on purpose. That remaining half is the rest of #4800.
- **An incremental rebuild is not byte-identical to a full one on a large corpus.**
  On 1,059 files it keeps one sourceless `any` node and seven edges that a full
  rebuild drops. This is not introduced here: v8 with an explicit `changed_paths`
  produces the same node and edges. It is pre-existing `changed_paths` behaviour that
  this PR makes reachable from the CLI.
- **A source that never extracts re-queues on every run** by design (#2543), so a
  corpus containing one can never reach the pure-skip case. This repository has one
  (`worked/rsl-siege-manager/graph.json`), which is why `graphify update .` here still
  re-extracts a handful of files.
- **On a copied checkout, deletions and renames are not evicted.**
  `graphify-out/.graphify_root` still names the original tree, so stored source paths
  resolve there and the fail-closed sweep reads the removed file as alive-out-of-scan
  and preserves it. The full path behaves identically, so this predates the PR; it is
  why this branch's deletion test uses a same-directory tree.
- **No incremental rebuild for the semantic path.** This covers `graphify update`
  (AST) only. `graphify extract` already had its own incremental mode.
- The change set is not persisted, so it is recomputed per run. It costs one manifest
  read against a scan that already happened.

## How was this tested?

`tests/test_update_incremental.py` is new and has 17 tests. Fifteen drive the real
`_rebuild_code` with a spy on `extract()`: an unchanged copied checkout, two edited
files reduced to the changed subset, an mtime bump with identical bytes, an added
file, a deleted file and the eviction that follows, the default path, `--force`, an
explicit `changed_paths`, a missing manifest, an unreadable manifest, a manifest
anchored elsewhere, incremental output equal to a full rebuild on the same tree, the
lock path, the non-blocking queue behaviour, and a cross-file call edge surviving an
incremental update both in place and on a copied checkout. Two run the real CLI as a
subprocess: `update` end to end, and `update --force`.

The assertion in `test_default_is_the_full_path` is the one that had to change to
coexist with the 0.9.96 gate, and a test that passes in both worlds can be vacuous,
so I checked it. The corpus now carries one change before the second run, which is
sound either way: a correct no-change gate cannot skip a tree that changed. Mutating
the derivation guard in a scratch copy to fire even when `incremental` is unset makes
it fail, with and without the gate:

```text
E  AssertionError: assert [['a.py']] == [['a.py', 'b.py', 'c.py', 'uses.py']]
```

Gates, all with `PYTHONPATH` set to the repo so `sys.executable -m graphify` children
load this tree rather than the installed package:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q          -> 8889 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed in 412.62s
tests/test_update_incremental.py       -> 17 passed
tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_progress_final_line_uses_consistent_denominator
                                       -> 1 passed
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/ tests/test_update_incremental.py
                                       -> All checks passed
```

Wall time and peak RSS for `graphify update`, one process per run, on 1,059 scanned
files (583 code), the same tree and the same two-file edit in both rows:

| | wall | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| current v8 (`dac06345`) | 68.15 s | 1,071 MB |
| this branch | 48.72 s | 537 MB |

The unchanged case is unchanged by this PR, because the gate answers it first:
1.96 s and 46 MB.

Not tested: Windows. The change set uses paths from `detect()` and the manifest's
existing anchoring rules, and nothing here adds new path construction.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no skill fragments touched.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). (Extraction is untouched. The change set is a content-hash comparison against the manifest, and mtime is only used to decide whether to hash.)
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages. (No trailer in the commit messages.)

items.title: perf(update): skip extraction when no relevant inputs changed (#4740)

labels.name: contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4740. `graphify update` had exactly one no-change exit, and it sat at the far end of the pipeline: detect → extract → build → cluster → compare topology. A run where nothing changed still paid for all of it. On this repo that is 36 s and 1.0 GB of RSS.

This moves the decision to the front, before extraction. `detect()` is not moved or duplicated; the gate classifies the result `_rebuild_code` already computed.

```diff
 _rebuild_code(watch_path, ...)
   detect(watch_path)
   code_files = detected["files"]["code"]
+  if changed_paths is None and not force:
+    if _inputs_unchanged(...) and _build_state_matches(...):
+      print("No relevant changes; graphify-out left untouched.")
+      return True
   extract(...)
   build_from_json(...)
   cluster(...)
-  compare topology   <- was the only no-change exit
```

The work is in the skip key. A skip is sound only if the key covers every input that reaches the graph, and the failure modes are asymmetric: a wrong "changed" costs time, a wrong "unchanged" ships a stale graph. So the key is:

```text
scanned files      every detected bucket, compared by content (ast_hash), not mtime
                   (detect_incremental's existing loop, shared)
in-scope path set  digest of the scanned paths plus the resolution inputs
                   (catches adds, deletes, renames and ignore-rule edits)
resolution inputs  tsconfig*/jsconfig/package.json, already ordinary scan input,
                   and package-lock/yarn.lock/pnpm-lock, which detect() skips by
                   name and now records separately so they can be stamped
extractor          v{version}-s{schema}-g{grammar}, the AST cache namespace
                   (a graph an older extractor wrote is not one this one wrote)
build config       scan root, follow_symlinks, no_cluster, gitignore, --exclude,
                   .graphifyrc digest
output shape       GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT, GRAPHIFY_AMBIGUOUS_SCALE
outputs            graph.json size + mtime_ns, graph.html presence, .graph.html.stale
was full           the last rebuild passed changed_paths=None
```

Most of that list is not theoretical. The first full-suite run failed 11 existing tests, and every one was a second rebuild on an unchanged tree that still had work to do: healing a graph an older version wrote, honouring a `.gitignore` eviction the incremental path deliberately skips (#2495), a subdir invocation after a root one, a pending HTML re-render. I grew the key until each passed again. No existing test was changed.

```diff
 graphify/detect.py
~  detect_incremental's classify loop -> classify_manifest_files(file_buckets, manifest, *, kind, unstamped_is_changed=True)
+  called from detect_incremental (behaviour unchanged) and from the gate
+  detect() records the resolution inputs it skips by name in detected["resolution_inputs"]
 graphify/watch.py
+  _inputs_unchanged, _scan_digest, _extractor_epoch, _current_build_state
+  _graph_json_is_complete, _write_build_state, _build_state_matches
+  graphify-out/.graphify_build_state.json
+  _ast_manifest_files() stamps a resolution_inputs bucket
 tests/test_update_no_change_gate.py
+  new, 19 tests
```

### The stamp only describes outputs that are fully on disk

A stamp is a promise that the next run may skip, so it is only allowed to exist when the outputs it names are complete. `_write_build_state` used to read graph.json's size and mtime from `stat()` without looking at the bytes. The atomic replace exists so a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated graph.json (#2689), but its non-atomic fallback can land part of the bytes and report success. Forcing that:

```text
run2 returned True
graph.json now 40 bytes; parses: False (Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 38)
stamp records size=40 | on disk 40 | match=True
_build_state_matches says: True
run3 skipped: True              <- truncated graph served forever
```

The writer now refuses to stamp unless graph.json is a whole JSON object and no `.graph.html.stale` marker is pending. Both refusals fail closed, so the next run takes the full path and reports the problem instead of skipping over it:

```text
stamp records size=1246 | on disk 40 | match=False
_build_state_matches says: False
run3 skipped: False
```

Before finding that, I tried the failure points a reviewer would expect, each with a topology-changing edit so the run had real work: `cluster`, the graph publish, the report write, `save_manifest`, and the HTML reconcile. None of them produced a skip on the next run, and the graph was never stale. Every stamp site is already the last statement before its `return True`, so anything written afterwards would only cause a mismatch. The `--no-cluster` `same_graph` case is safe for the same reason: graph.json is not rewritten, and the stamp stats it at stamp time, so the recorded size and mtime always describe what is on disk.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (performance; the report is a cost bug)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A skip happens only when the key covers every input that reaches the graph, and a stamp exists only when the outputs it names are complete. Anything that cannot be proven takes the full path.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. One new JSON file under `graphify-out/` and a set of comparisons. No graph schema, cache-key or file-format change, and deleting the stamp reverts behaviour to a full run.

**Blast Radius:** moderate, because the gate decides whether a rebuild happens at all:

- A missing, unreadable or mismatched stamp falls back to the full path, so the worst case is the old cost rather than a wrong graph.
- `detect()` gains a `resolution_inputs` key and the manifest a matching bucket, so lock files are hashed on every rebuild. That is the cost this PR adds, bounded by how many lock files the corpus has.
- `classify_manifest_files()` defaults to the old `detect_incremental` semantics: a row-less or blank-hash file still re-queues on the incremental path, and only the gate treats it as unchanged.
- An explicit `changed_paths` and `--force` both bypass the gate.
- `_write_build_state` can now decline to write. A declined stamp is not an error; the next run simply rebuilds.

**Limitations**

- A **copied** `graphify-out` does not skip. The stamp is a new file, so a checkout that copies `graph.json`/`manifest.json`/`cache/` (the issue's runs 1–3) has no stamp and takes the full path. The steady-state rerun is what this makes cheap, which is why it only partly addresses #4740. The incremental patch path is a later PR.
- A source whose extraction previously failed, and whose content is then fixed with no other change, is picked up on the next rebuild instead of by the gate. Its row is blanked by design (#2543), and closing that needs a per-file stamp of unstamped sources.
- The completeness check reads the first and last non-whitespace byte of graph.json rather than parsing it. A full `json.load` would answer more, but the cap is 512 MiB and the rebuild is still holding its own copy of the graph, so a second parse can add about a gigabyte of peak RSS. Mid-file corruption moves mtime, which the stat comparison already catches.
- A retained `.graph.html.stale` marker means the `--no-cluster` path cannot stamp, since that path never touches HTML. It takes the full path until a clustered run consumes the marker.
- A new input that affects the output (another env knob, another resolution file) means extending `_current_build_state()`. Nothing enforces that.
- Hooks and the watcher go through the same gate.

## How was this tested?

`tests/test_update_no_change_gate.py` drives the real `_rebuild_code` and spies on `extract()`. It covers the unchanged tree, a new file, a deleted file, an edited `tsconfig.json`, an edited `package.json`, an edited lock file, an mtime bump with identical bytes, an explicit `changed_paths`, `--force`, a missing manifest, a scanned file with no manifest row, the scan digest, a rebuild that fails at each of three write points, a partially published graph.json, and both writer refusals.

Against pristine v8 (`92741d16`) the whole file gives **8 failed, 11 passed**. The 11 that pass include every "the full path is still taken" guard, so they are the proof this PR did not change existing behaviour. The 8 failures are the skip itself, the two digest and row-tolerance tests, and the three stamp refusals.

Against the pre-hardening stamp (`79c812d0`), the 6 tests added for it give **3 failed, 3 passed**. The 3 failures are its contracts: a partial publish, a truncated graph, a pending marker. The 3 `never_finishes` cases pass either way; they pin the ordering so a later refactor cannot move a stamp in front of a write.

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q                                    -> 8745 passed, 15 skipped, 1 xfailed in 420.12s
tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_progress_final_line_uses_consistent_denominator
                                                                 -> 1 passed
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/ tests/test_update_no_change_gate.py
                                                                 -> All checks passed
.venv/bin/python -m pyright graphify/watch.py graphify/detect.py  -> 29 errors, 3 warnings
   identical to the pre-change count on the same two files; no new errors
```

Wall time and peak RSS for `graphify update .` on this repo, 605 tracked code files and a 22.8k node / 47.7k edge graph, with the tree untouched between runs:

| run | wall | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| before, no change | 36.1 s | 1,007,716 KB |
| after, no change | 1.4–2.1 s | 53,260 KB |
| after, `--force` | 37.7 s | 1,008,724 KB |

One flake to flag: `tests/test_language_override_lifecycle.py::test_watch_root_config_lifecycle_rebuilds_and_refreshes_event_mapping[delete]` failed once with a missing `graph.json` earlier on this branch, then passed in isolation, as a whole file, and in the full-suite runs since. It drives the real watcher through a monkeypatched `time.sleep`, so it is timing-sensitive.

Not tested: Windows. The digest uses `os.path.abspath` and the same anchoring rules the manifest already relies on.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no skill fragments touched.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). (The two env knobs the gate reads already changed the output before this PR; reading them only makes the gate more conservative, and extraction itself is untouched.)
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included. (The stamp records a scan root path and file digests, not source text.)
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages. (No trailer in the commit messages.)

items.title: fix(extract): report AST cache hit rate over the file total, not uncached set (#4740)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4740. `graphify update` reported its AST cache progress against the uncached set, so the last line always read `N/N uncached files (100%)` and looked like a 100% hit rate. #4740 read it as "the copied cache missed almost every file"; the real rate was never printed anywhere.

That line counts progress through the work the run has to do, so its denominator is the work, not the corpus. This adds a separate line whose denominator is the file total, and leaves the existing progress lines alone.

**Before** (warm run across 100 `.py` + 20 `.ts`, cache already warmed, v8 `92741d16`):

```text
  AST extraction: 20/20 uncached files (100%) [12 workers]
```

20 of the 120 files were re-extracted, and the only line shown says 100%.

**After:**

```text
cold:  AST cache: 0/120 files served from cache (0%); 120 to extract
warm:  AST cache: 100/120 files served from cache (83%); 20 to extract
       AST extraction: 20/20 uncached files (100%) [12 workers]
```

```diff
 graphify/extract.py
+  _PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 100    hoisted to module scope, shared by all three sites
   extract()
+    cache_hits / no_extractor counters in the Phase 1 cache loop
+    print(f"  AST cache: {cache_hits}/{total} files served from cache "
+          f"({cache_hits * 100 // total}%); {len(uncached_work)} to extract"
+          + f"; {no_extractor} without an extractor")
+    gated on total >= _PROGRESS_INTERVAL, like the progress lines
   _extract_parallel / _extract_sequential
-    _PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 100    dropped, both read the module constant now
 tests/test_extract.py
+  test_extract_reports_ast_cache_hit_rate_over_file_total
```

No existing test changes. `tests/test_extract.py:5660` pins the `100/100 uncached files (100%)` format and still passes unmodified.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The cache summary reports against the files the run was asked to extract, so its denominator cannot shrink to the uncached set. The progress lines keep counting the uncached work, and their format stays pinned by `tests/test_extract.py:5660`.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Two counters, one `print`, one test. No schema, cache or file-format change, no persisted state, nothing to migrate back.

**Blast Radius:** narrow, and limited to stdout:
- The line prints on the runs that already print progress, meaning any `extract()` call asked to extract `_PROGRESS_INTERVAL` (100) files or more. Small batches, which is what `watch`, the hooks and the MCP server pass on a rebuild, stay quiet. Anything parsing that stdout strictly will see one extra line on the large runs. The gate came out of review: the first version printed on every call, so a one-file watch rebuild logged a 0% rate that is trivially true and carries no information.
- The counts come from the existing Phase 1 loop. Extraction, caching and the graph are untouched.
- Files with no extractor were invisible in every printed total before this. They now show as a suffix, so the 5 `.ets` files in the existing 105-file test are accounted for instead of silently absent.

**Limitations**

- The `uncached files` lines are unchanged. A reader still sees `20/20 uncached files (100%)`; the new line is what supplies the correct denominator. I left them because their format is asserted by an existing test, and rewriting them is outside this fix.
- On a TS-heavy repo the rate will read low or zero, because the JS/TS suffixes bypass the AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`). That is the second half of #4740 and this PR does not touch it.
- The `; N without an extractor` suffix is not asserted by a test. The path is exercised, since the existing 105-file test's `.ets` files have no extractor, but nothing pins the suffix text.
- Nothing prints when the path list is empty, or when it holds fewer than `_PROGRESS_INTERVAL` (100) files.
- Once warm `update` runs pass only the changed batch (the incremental path in #4740's other half), this line goes quiet on the runs someone might use to check whether the cache helped. If that visibility is wanted, it belongs behind a flag or an environment variable rather than unconditional stdout.

## How was this tested?

New `tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_reports_ast_cache_hit_rate_over_file_total` drives the real `extract()` over 100 `.py` + 5 `.ts` and reads captured stdout, no mocking. The corpus is sized past 100 files on purpose: the final progress line only prints when `total_files >= 100` (`extract.py:9263`), so a smaller corpus cannot show the two lines side by side. It covers three runs:

- cold, cacheable-only corpus -> `0/100`, `100 to extract`
- warm, same corpus -> `100/100`, `0 to extract`
- mixed, after warming -> `100/105`, `5 to extract`, while asserting the progress line still reads `5/5 uncached files (100%)` and that `105/105 uncached files` never appears

The gate was measured directly, in a scratch checkout, against the real `extract()` and through `_rebuild_code(changed_paths=[one file])`:

```text
    1 file  -> no line
   99 files -> no line
  100 files -> prints
  605 files -> prints
one-file watch rebuild -> no line, only the usual watch message

tests/test_extract.py with the gate     -> 373 passed, 1 xfailed
tests/test_extract.py without the gate  -> 373 passed, 1 xfailed
```

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly \
  tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_reports_ast_cache_hit_rate_over_file_total \
  tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_progress_final_line_uses_consistent_denominator
  -> 2 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
  -> 8727 passed, 15 skipped, 1 xfailed, 2225 warnings in 402.12s (0:06:42)
```

Both Before/After blocks come from real `graphify update` runs on the same corpus, with the fix stashed and then applied.

Environment note, not fixed here: the full suite needs `tests/test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py` to install `graphifyy` through `uv`, so it hangs without network. The step-1 script tries `uv tool run` / `uv tool install` before it ever reads the `graphify` shebang. With `graphify` on PATH and an offline `uv` that fails fast, that file's 30 tests pass in 8s.

Not tested: Windows. The change is a `print` of integers.

- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages. (No trailer in the commit message.)

items.title: fix(uv-lock): keep uv.lock on the 3.11+ branch, pin pillow 13.x (#4693)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4693. On Python 3.10 the `svg`, `all` and `leiden` extras could never get a patched pillow: every open advisory against pillow 12.3.0 is first fixed in 13.0.0, and 13.0.0 requires Python 3.11, and the lockfile pinned 12.3.0 for every Python.

There are two changes:

- `[tool.uv] environments = ["python_full_version >= '3.11'"]` drops the 3.10 branch from the lock. A dependency scan of `uv.lock` no longer reports the advisories, because the lock simply has no 3.10 branch to scan.
- `uv lock --upgrade-package pillow` pins pillow 13.0.0. The relock also cleared preexisting lock drift: the committed lock still read editable 0.9.84 while `pyproject.toml` was 0.9.95 (scipy, contourpy, importlib-metadata come along).

```text
> pip-audit on the lock export for all extras
before: pillow 12.3.0   -> 37 advisories (12 x Critical, 25 x High)   first fixed: 13.0.0
after:  pillow 13.0.0   -> 0 advisories
```

The 3.10 leg of the CI test matrix goes with the lock: `uv sync --all-extras --frozen` installs straight from `uv.lock`, and the lock now covers only 3.11+. That leg failed exactly that way on this PR's first CI run. `requires-python` stays `>=3.10`.

### Existing tests this PR changes

None. No test reads the pillow pin or the `[tool.uv]` section.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Lock-driven installs resolve a patched pillow, or fail loudly on Python 3.10 instead of silently installing an unpatched one. Lock-unaware installs keep working on 3.10.

- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Two files plus a workflow matrix entry, and the lockfile is regenerated on the next `uv lock` anyway.

**Blast Radius:** narrow.
- A 3.11+, all-extras install gets pillow 13.0.0. Before this PR it kept getting 12.3.0 — the lock predated 13.0.0 and uv preserves pinned versions, so even 3.11 users are being unstuck here.
- A 3.10 `uv sync` / `uv run` / `uv tool install` now errors with the lockfile's supported-environments message instead of installing pillow 12.3.0. That failure names the constraint.
- A plain `pip install graphifyy[svg,all,leiden]` on 3.10 ignores `uv.lock`, still resolves and still installs pillow 12.3.0. That residual is what raising `requires-python` to >=3.11 (the issue's second option) would close; it's a follow-up, not part of this PR.

**Limitations**

- Python 3.10 users of the `svg`, `all` or `leiden` extras installed without the lock still run unpatched pillow. This PR changes the lock only.
- CI no longer tests Python 3.10 on the lock path. Without the matrix leg nothing guards against a 3.10-regressing `pyproject.toml` change; it would surface as an install failure for bare-pip users, not in CI.

items.title: fix: recover chained TS decorators and report the lossy parse region (#4711)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4711. A TypeScript decorator whose expression is a call chain (`@(Link().toMany())`) contributed no `references` edge to the graph, and the partial-parse warning pointed at a line that was not the one costing extraction.

tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2 cannot parse a member access on a call in decorator position. `@Link().toMany()` fails on one line, without parentheses, and with the dot moved to the next line, so no formatting change avoids it. The parser recovers by wrapping `Link().` in an ERROR and parsing `toMany()` as a sibling inside the parentheses. `_ts_decorator_name` returned `None` for every `parenthesized_expression`, so the whole decorator was skipped.

The warning also reported the first ERROR in document order. In `continent.entity.ts` that is line 14, a single-line recovery that keeps every symbol; the multiline region at line 33 is the one that lost edges.

```diff
 graphify/extractors/engine.py
+  _ts_decorator_target_name()
+    unwrap a parenthesized decorator
+    name the outermost call the parser recovered
+    name nothing for a recovered non-call expression (`@(A, B)`)
+
+  _first_multiline_error_line()
+    line of the earliest ERROR that spans more than one line

 graphify/extract.py
-  first_error_line
+  lossy_error_line, falling back to first_error_line
+  "error region at line N" instead of "first error at line N"
```

**Before** (v8, `continent.entity.ts` from the issue):

```text
warning:  ... continent.entity.ts (first error at line 14, 6 symbol(s) extracted)
decorator edges: column, entity, primarykey
```

**After:**

```text
warning:  ... continent.entity.ts (error region at line 33, 8 symbol(s) extracted)
decorator edges: column, tomany, toone, entity, primarykey
```

The two new edges add their stub targets, which is where the two extra nodes come from.

The 7-line `x.ts` from the issue goes from no decorator edge to:

```text
x_c -> tomany [references, context=decorator]
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A decorator's `references` edge targets the outermost call of its expression, whether or not the expression is parenthesized. A recovered expression that is not a call (an invalid `@(A, B)`) gets no name rather than a guessed one. The warning line names the region the warning gate selects on: the earliest multiline ERROR, or the first error when the file yielded nothing but its file node.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No cache schema change. Cached per-file results without `lossy_error_line` keep the old first-error line until they are re-extracted; the graph itself is unchanged by that key.

**Blast Radius:** TS/JS decorator edges and the partial-parse warning text.

Parenthesized decorators in every language now resolve a name where they previously resolved none. Plain decorators (`@Component`, `@ng.Component()`, `@Injectable`) take the same path as before, and the 320 TS/JS tests pass. The warning wording changed from `first error at line N` to `error region at line N`, which is user-visible; four existing expectations were updated with it. The full-suite failure set is identical to v8.

**Limitations**

- **Grammar:** the parse error remains. tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2 is the newest release on PyPI, and TSX and JS grammars fail on the same construct. No source rewrite tried (paren stripping, double parens, computed access, sequence, optional chain, line continuation) parses.
- **Unparenthesized chains:** `@Link().toMany()` still attributes only `Link`, because the parser ends the decorator at `@Link()` and parses the rest as a separate expression.
- **One target per decorator:** only the outermost call is named, so `Link` gets no edge from `@(Link().toMany())`.
- **Repeated targets:** two decorators with the same target collapse into one edge, since edges are deduplicated by endpoints and relation.
- **Warning:** it still says "may be partially extracted" even when every symbol survived; the parser cannot tell whether the lost part was a decorator edge or a symbol.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_ts_decorator_chains.py` run `extract()` on small TS files: the two recovered shapes, the clean identifier-receiver shape, the invalid-sequence guard, and the warning line for a file with an earlier single-line error.

```text
       test_partial_extraction_warning.py          -> 320 passed
pytest -q -p no:randomly (full suite, serial)      -> v8:      39 failed, 7988 passed, 361 skipped

                                                      (failure sets identical)
```

|---|---|---|
| `x.ts` | no decorator edge | `x_c -> tomany` |
| `continent.entity.ts` | 3 decorator edges, warning at line 14 | 5 decorator edges, warning at line 33 |

items.title: fix: resolve affected <path> for disambiguated file labels (#4698)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4698. `graphify affected <path>` answered `No unique node match for <path>` for a file whose basename is shared with another file and that has a second node on `L1`, for example a module docstring.

A path query matches every node in the file, so resolution ends in `_prefer_file_node`. Three of its passes pick the file node:

1. the label equals the query basename and sits on `L1`
2. the file node is the only node on `L1`
3. the label equals the basename

#2032 relabels colliding basenames to their shortest unique path suffix (`alpha/hooks.py`), which retires passes 1 and 3. The rationale pass creates one node per docstring at the docstring's own line, so a docstring on line 1 puts a second node on `L1` and retires pass 2. A one-line top-level definition does the same. Either precondition alone is harmless. Both together resolve to `None`.

The fact the resolver needs is already in the graph: a file node's label is a path form of its own `source_file`. `_is_file_node_label` encodes exactly that and `build`/`analyze` already use it.

```diff
 graphify/affected.py
   _prefer_file_node()
     pass 1: label equals the basename and is on L1
+    pass 2: label names this node's own source_file
+            (_is_file_node_label, imported lazily from graphify.build)
+            checked before the "only node on L1" fallback
     pass 3: only node on L1
     pass 4: label equals the basename
```

No graph schema change and no re-extraction. The relabelled node is already in `graph.json`; only the lookup changes.

**Before** (v8, the issue's repro):

```text
$ graphify affected app/alpha/hooks.py
No unique node match for app/alpha/hooks.py
$ echo $?
0
```

**After:**

```text
$ graphify affected app/alpha/hooks.py
Affected nodes for alpha/hooks.py
```
