items.title: fix(rust): scope a `use` to the crate it names (#4699)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4699. A Rust `use` could bind to a same-named definition in another crate. On `tokio-rs/axum` @ `86aa615`, `examples/customize-extractor-error/src/custom_extractor.rs` says `use serde_json::Value`, and both its import and a `Value` reference bound to a variant in `axum-core/src/response/into_response_parts.rs`. The graph showed a cross-crate dependency the source never had.

Three causes, all in the Rust extractor and the corpus rewire:

1. `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` bound a sourceless stub to the only node with that label anywhere in the corpus. The crate the `use` names was not part of the decision.
2. The extractor recorded the imported name (`_rust_use_name`) only for paths rooted in this crate, so an external `use` carried no scope.
3. A scoped binding and a label-only guess both reported `EXTRACTED`.

```diff
 extractors/rust.py
   use binding
+    record the first path segment on the stub (`_rust_use_roots`)
+    record a bare `pub use` as a re-export (`_rust_pub_use`)

 extract.py
-  _rewire_unique_stub_nodes(nodes, edges)
+  _rewire_unique_stub_nodes(nodes, edges, root)
+    resolve each .rs file's crate from the nearest Cargo.toml
     bind a stub to a unique same-label definition
+    consider only candidates in a crate the `use` names
+    follow `pub use` re-exports across crates
+    leave the stub unbound when the named crate is outside the scan
+    mark a rewire with no resolving `use` as INFERRED

 cargo_introspect.py
+  package_name(manifest)   # reuses the module's TOML loader
```

**Before** (v8, the reported file):

```text
imports_from  custom_extractor.rs  ->  Value @ axum-core/.../into_response_parts.rs
references    handler()            ->  Value @ axum-core/.../into_response_parts.rs
```

**After:**

```text
imports_from  custom_extractor.rs  ->  Value  (a local sourceless stub)
references    handler()            ->  Value  (a local sourceless stub)
```

The re-export handling keeps edges the scoping would otherwise drop. `axum-extra/src/extract/cached.rs` (`use axum::extract::FromRequestParts`) and `axum/src/extract/connect_info.rs` (`use super::{.., FromRequestParts}`) still reach `axum-core/src/extract/mod.rs`, and a `use axum_core::..` edge stays `EXTRACTED`.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A Rust name binds only inside a crate its `use` names. A crate outside the scan binds to nothing. A cross-crate re-export counts as the named crate. A binding made by label alone is `INFERRED`.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. The per-file AST payload gained two markers, so the cache schema moves from 22 to 24 and cached `.rs` extractions re-run on the next build. A revert brings back the label-only binding on the next build. No migration, no config change.

**Blast Radius:** Rust cross-file resolution.

On `tokio-rs/axum` @ `86aa615` (302 `.rs` files):

| | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | 4036 | 4141 |
| edges | 10326 | 10326 |
| cross-crate `imports_from` | 125 | 163 |
| cross-crate `references` | 122 | 168 |
| bug-signature edges (target label is an external `use` of the source file) | 22 | 13 |
| confidence | 10195 EXTRACTED / 131 INFERRED | 9828 EXTRACTED / 498 INFERRED |
| import cycles | 20 | 20 |
| time (median of 3) | 2.05 s | 1.97 s |

The node count rises because a scoped stub that binds to nothing stays as a sourceless node instead of being dropped. Cross-crate edges rise because a name with several same-named definitions can now resolve to the one in the crate it names instead of staying ambiguous. Bug-signature edges drop from 22 to 13. The 20 cycles do not change; the reported `Value` edge was not part of one.

- **Other languages:** scoping only applies when `origin_file` ends in `.rs`, so no other extractor changes. The full-suite failure set is identical to v8.
- **Saved graphs:** the cache bump forces a re-extraction, so an existing `graph.json` keeps its old Rust edges until the next build. A rebuild produces the scoped result.
- **Determinism:** crate resolution reads only paths and `Cargo.toml` files, with no environment or ordering input.

**Limitations**

- **No manifest:** a file with no `Cargo.toml` above it keeps v8's label-only binding and is marked `INFERRED`. Scoping needs a crate.
- **Glob re-exports:** `pub use core::*;` is not followed; only a named `pub use` is.
- **Renamed dependencies:** `foo = { package = "bar" }` in `Cargo.toml` is not mapped, so `use foo::..` stays unbound.
- **Macros:** a re-export produced by a macro is invisible to the extractor.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_rust_crate_use_scope.py` run `extract()` on small Cargo projects and compare node ids, edge targets, and confidence. None of them calls a private helper.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| an external `use` plus an annotation does not reach a local crate (enum variant) | fail | pass |
| an external `use` plus an annotation does not reach a local crate (struct) | fail | pass |
| a grouped external `use` does not reach a local crate | fail | pass |
| an annotation with no `use` does not reach a local crate | fail | pass |
| `use a::Value` reaches `a`, not a namesake in `c` | fail | pass |
| `use osiris_types::Config` does not reach `server`'s `Config` | fail | pass |
| `use osiris_types::Config` reaches `osiris-types` when both define it | fail | pass |
| a `use` of a re-exporting crate reaches the defining crate, not an unrelated namesake | fail | pass |
| `pub(crate) use` does not leak out of its crate | fail | pass |
| a manifest-less binding is `INFERRED`, not `EXTRACTED` | fail | pass |
| guard: external `use` with no reference, `std`, `crate::`, same-name types without a `use` | pass | pass |
| guard: `use super::Item` through a re-export reaches the defining crate | pass | pass |
| guard: a scanned-crate `use` keeps `EXTRACTED` | pass | pass |

```text

```

items.title: fix: drop inline comments from pnpm workspace globs and skip globs pathlib rejects (#4681)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4681. An inline YAML comment after a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` glob stayed in the glob, so the workspace package was never found and imports of it stayed unresolved. On Python 3.12 a `**` glob with a comment also made `Path.glob` raise, and the error escaped `extract()`, so the whole run failed with no graph.

```yaml
packages:
  - "services/runner/stg/**" # staging runner infrastructure
```

`_pnpm_workspace_globs` read that line as `services/runner/stg/**" # staging runner infrastructure`.

- **3.12:** `ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component`. Exit 1, and the Python files in the run are lost too.
- **3.13:** no crash, but the glob matches nothing. A plain `pk/*` with a comment fails the same way on every version.
- **Absolute globs:** `Path.glob` raises `NotImplementedError` on every version, from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or from `package.json` `"workspaces"`.

This PR fixes both parts in `resolution.py`:

```diff
 _pnpm_workspace_globs
   for each "- value" line under packages:
-    strip quotes from both ends
+    if quoted: take the text up to the closing quote (skip the item if there is none)
+    else: cut at the first `#` that follows whitespace
     skip empty and `!` values

 _load_workspace_packages
   for each glob
-    root.glob(pattern)
+    try root.glob(pattern)
+    except ValueError, NotImplementedError: warn and skip this glob
```

`"a#b/*"` and unquoted `a#b/*` stay as written, because YAML only starts a comment at a `#` after whitespace.

**Before** (v8, the issue's repro plus a package `@x/svc` under `services/runner/stg/`):

```text
3.12: warning: skipped .../libs/consumer.ts (ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component)
      [graphify extract] AST extraction failed: ...   exit 1, no graph.json
3.13: exit 0, 19 nodes, 14 edges, consumer.ts imports_from ref_x_svc (unresolved)
```

**After:**

```text
3.12: exit 0, 18 nodes, 16 edges, consumer.ts imports_from svc/index.ts
3.13: exit 0, 18 nodes, 16 edges, consumer.ts imports_from svc/index.ts
```

These are the same counts v8 gives for the repro with the comment removed.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A workspace glob means what pnpm reads from the YAML, and one glob that `Path.glob` can't use never stops the extraction of the rest of the repository.

- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.

- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No ids or cache formats change. JS/TS files skip the AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`), so no schema bump is needed.

**Blast Radius:** JS/TS workspace import resolution. Only lines under `packages:` that hold a comment, or a quote left open, read differently. A glob that used to crash the run is now skipped.

**Limitations**

- **Warning count:** the cache that holds the workspace packages is per process, so the warning prints once per bad glob in each worker. 60 TS files on 3.12 printed it 26 times.
- **Existing graphs:** `graphify extract` in a folder already built with v8 keeps the old result, because the manifest skips unchanged files. `graphify update .` or a fresh folder picks up the fix. The same holds today for any edit of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

- **Absolute globs** are skipped, not resolved.

items.title: fix: fold SQL table stubs across files and bind schema-qualified names (#4653)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4653. A SQL table got one node per file that read it. A schema-qualified read like `dbo.Customers` never bound to the `CREATE TABLE` in another file, and a plain read like `Invoices` bound to a Python class of the same name.

There were three causes, all in the cross-file pass in `extract()`:

1. Stubs with the same id and no `source_file` are salted apart by `origin_file` in `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids`. So each file gets its own `dbo.Orders`.
2. `_is_type_like_definition` rejects any label with a `.`. A SQL table is `schema.name`, so `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` never binds `dbo.Customers` to its definition.
3. `.sql` is not in `_LANG_FAMILY_BY_EXT`, so the cross-language guard treats SQL as unknown and lets the Python class win.

This PR fixes all three in that pass. It doesn't touch the SQL extractor:

```diff
 _LANG_FAMILY_BY_EXT
+  ".sql": "sql"

 _is_type_like_definition(node)
-  dotted label -> not a definition
+  dotted label -> not a definition, unless the node comes from a .sql file

 _rewire_unique_stub_nodes
   remap each stub to its unique definition
+  for each stub from a .sql file
+    drop the remap if the definition is in another language
+    if it binds to nothing, group it by _norm_ident(label)
+  fold each group into its smallest id (so file order doesn't matter)
```

**Before** (v8, the issue's repro):

```text
dbo.ActiveCustomers  reads_from  dbo_customers                      (a stub, not the table)
dbo.LateOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.OpenOrders       reads_from  views_open_orders_sql_dbo_orders   (a second dbo.Orders)
dbo.Recent           reads_from  app_models_invoices                (the Python class)
```

**After:**

```text
dbo.ActiveCustomers  reads_from  tables_customers_dbo_customers     (the CREATE TABLE)
dbo.LateOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.OpenOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders   (one dbo.Orders)
dbo.Recent           reads_from  invoices                           (a SQL stub)
```

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Each SQL table is one node across the project. A read binds to the `CREATE TABLE` when exactly one file defines it, and never to a definition in another language.

**Door:** two-way. Per-file extraction doesn't change, so the AST cache needs no bump. A revert brings back the per-file stubs on the next build.

**Blast Radius:** SQL nodes, and any edge between SQL and another language. On `microsoft/sql-server-samples` `wide-world-importers/wwi-ssdt` (336 `.sql` files):

items.title: fix(sql): end the statement at GO batch separators (#4651)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

labels.name: needs:title
labels.description: PR title should follow the conventional-commit format

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4651. In a T-SQL script, a `GO` line with no `;` before it hid every statement after it. Those tables and views got no node, and their edges were lost or attached to the wrong node.

`GO` is a command for sqlcmd and SSMS, not SQL. tree-sitter-sql reads it as an identifier, so the statement doesn't end there, and the parser puts `GO` and the rest of the file in one ERROR node.

This PR ends the statement at each `GO` line before parsing:

```diff
 extract_sql
   source = file bytes
+  for each GO [n] line found on the masked text (comments and strings blanked)
+    skip it if a `,` comes right before it, or a `,` or `)` right after it (a column named go)
+    replace `GO` with `;` plus spaces (same length, so byte offsets and line numbers don't move)
   tree = parser.parse(source)
```

A keyword before the line doesn't make it a column. `SET NOCOUNT ON` / `GO` is a real separator, and SSMS writes one before every object.

**Before** (v8):

```sql
SET NOCOUNT ON
GO
CREATE TABLE dbo.Customers (Id INT PRIMARY KEY)
GO
```

items.title: fix(sql): strip T-SQL brackets and add reads_from/writes_to edges for procedures (#4635)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4635. On a T-SQL project the SQL graph was close to empty:

1. Bracket names were mangled. `[dbo].[Country]` got the label `dbo].[Country`, and it never matched `dbo.Country`.
2. Stored procedures had no `reads_from` edges, in any dialect.
3. `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`MERGE` made no edge.

Both come from the grammar. tree-sitter-sql 0.3.11 has no T-SQL bracket identifiers: the outer `[` and `]` become ERROR tokens, and the name it keeps is `dbo].[Country`. It also has no `create_procedure` node at all, so the `create_procedure` branch in `sql.py` never runs. Even `CREATE PROCEDURE p AS SELECT a FROM t1;` lands in an ERROR node. The regex recovery then adds the procedure node, and nothing adds its edges. Without `;` between statements, the grammar also merges the body, so the tree has no `insert` or `update` node to read.

So this PR reads procedure bodies as text, not from the tree:

```diff
 extract_sql
   labels and lookup keys
+    strip [ ] from each name part: [dbo].[Orders] -> dbo.Orders, [a]]b] -> a]b
   routine recovery (_ROUTINE_RECOVERY_RX, when the parse has errors)
     add routine node
+    body = after its name, up to the next CREATE/ALTER line, a GO line, or EOF
+    scan the body on the masked text (comments and strings blanked)
+      FROM / JOIN                                          -> reads_from
+      INSERT [INTO] / UPDATE / DELETE [FROM] / MERGE [INTO] / SELECT ... INTO -> writes_to
+      UPDATE o ... FROM dbo.Orders o                        -> alias resolves to dbo.Orders
+      skip CTE names, @variables, #temp/##temp, table-valued function calls
+    one edge per (routine, relation, table)
```

Ids don't change: `_make_id` already dropped the brackets, so only labels and in-file matching were wrong. Double-quoted names (`"dbo"."V"`) keep their labels. Routines the tree parses cleanly (PostgreSQL `$$` functions) keep their tree-based edges and aren't scanned a second time.

**Before** (the issue's repro, v8, `graphify update .`):

```text
dbo].[Country reads_from dbo].[tbl_Country
(3 procedures: contains only)
```

**After:**

```text
dbo.Country               reads_from  dbo.tbl_Country
dbo.GetOrderTotal()       reads_from  dbo.Orders
dbo.GetOrderTotal()       reads_from  dbo.Payments
dbo.GetOrderTotalPlain()  reads_from  dbo.Orders
dbo.GetOrderTotalPlain()  reads_from  dbo.Payments
dbo.AddPayment()          writes_to   dbo.Orders
dbo.AddPayment()          writes_to   dbo.Payments
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

`writes_to` is a new relation. Nothing outside `sql.py` lists relation names, so it needs no registration.

## Verification & Invariants

A procedure has a `reads_from` edge to each table it reads and a `writes_to` edge to each table it writes, and none to aliases, variables, temp tables, CTEs, or names in comments and strings. A name gets the same label and key with or without brackets.

- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Ids are unchanged. `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes 20 -> 21 so cached `.sql` extractions re-run, and a revert re-runs them again. #4572 and #4573 also take 21, so whichever lands second needs 22.

**Blast Radius:** SQL only. On `microsoft/sql-server-samples` `wide-world-importers/wwi-ssdt` (336 `.sql` files):

| | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | 739 | 1011 |
| non-`contains` edges | 146 | 465 |
| time (median of 3) | 5.7 s | 5.8 s |

- **Removed:** no v8 edge. The edges that show as removed in a text diff are the same edges with bracket-free labels.
- **Added:** 190 `reads_from` and 129 `writes_to`. All 319 were checked against the source: 314 have the keyword right before the table name, and 5 are `UPDATE sih ... FROM Warehouse.StockItemHoldings AS sih` alias updates.
- **False positives:** none among the 61 distinct targets. 13 are `sys.*` catalog views, which are real references. 36 edges sit on routines that only exist because of the mask's known multi-line-string hole (`Configuration_*InMemory.sql` build procedures inside multi-line `N'...'` strings).
- **Existing tests:** 10 assertions in `test_multilang.py` change their expected routine label to the bracket-free form (`[dbo].[usp_Real]()` -> `dbo.usp_Real()`). `test_sql_tsql_bracketed_procedure_is_recovered` now filters to routine nodes, since the procedure's tables now appear as stubs.

**Limitations**

- **One node per file for undefined tables.** A table no file defines, referenced from N files, becomes N stub nodes. In the repro that's three `dbo.Orders` nodes. v8 does the same. Answering "what writes to `dbo.Orders`" across a project needs that fixed. Filed as #<stub-issue>.
- **`GO` without `;`** still swallows the next statement in the tree, so a second `CREATE TABLE` after `GO` is lost. Filed as #<go-issue>.
- When a procedure both reads and writes a table, `graph.json` keeps one edge per pair, so only `writes_to` shows. `extract()` returns both.
- `MERGE ... USING src` records no read. `TRUNCATE` and `EXEC` aren't modelled. `BULK INSERT dbo.T` counts as a write.
- A `CREATE`/`ALTER` at the start of a line inside a body (`CREATE INDEX ... ON #t`) ends the body early. `CREATE TABLE #t` and `CREATE TABLE @t` don't.
- Trigger and index labels keep their brackets.
- The `create_procedure` and `fb_proc_or_trigger` branches are dead on this grammar. They're left as they are.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_sql_tsql_procedures.py` run `extract()` or `extract_sql()` on small files, including the issue's four, and assert `(source, relation, target)` triples. None calls a private helper.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| T1: `[dbo].[Orders]` and `dbo.Orders` in one file are one table | fail | pass |
| T2: no half-stripped labels; labels are `dbo.Orders`, `dbo.AddPayment()`; `[a]]b]` -> `a]b`; `"dbo"."V"` kept | fail | pass |
| T3: each repro procedure reads its tables | fail | pass |
| T4: plain `CREATE PROCEDURE p AS SELECT ...`, with `(x INT)`, with `@x INT ... BEGIN END` | fail | pass |
| T5: `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`, `SELECT ... INTO` give `writes_to`; `DELETE FROM` isn't a read | fail | pass |
| T9: `UPDATE o ... FROM dbo.Orders o` writes `dbo.Orders` | fail | pass |
| T10: `#work`, `##shared`, `@ids` are skipped | fail | pass |
| T11: `GO`-separated procedures keep their own tables; comments and strings are ignored | fail | pass |
| guards: aliases, columns, variables, CTEs, two procedures in one file, top-level statements, function and view reads, one edge per triple | pass | pass |

On v8 the guards pass because v8 makes no procedure edges. They catch a fix that attaches too much.

```text
pytest tests/test_sql_tsql_procedures.py (tests on v8)    -> 25 failed, 8 passed
pytest tests/test_sql_tsql_procedures.py (this branch)    -> 33 passed
pytest test_multilang.py test_pg_introspect.py test_extract.py -> 448 passed
pytest -q -p no:randomly (full suite, --basetemp=/var/tmp) -> 8504 passed, 14 skipped
ruff check (changed files)                                 -> All checks passed
```

The cache bump was checked on the repro: a v8 run writes the cache, then this branch with the schema forced back to 20 serves the old labels and the single edge. At 21 it re-extracts and gives the 7 edges above.

items.title: fix(js): resolve ns.fn() calls through namespace imports (#4619)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4619. A call through a namespace import made no `calls` edge:

```ts
import * as ops from './ops'
export function dispatch(n: number) { return ops.submit(n) }   // no dispatch -> submit
```

It failed in both call paths:

- The symbol-resolution pass (`resolution.py`) never recorded `import * as ops`, and kept only bare-identifier callees, so `ops.submit` was dropped. #3517 fixed aliased named imports here and left namespace imports for later.
- The per-file engine saw the member call, then looked `submit` up by bare name in the caller's own file. When that file has its own `submit`, the call bound to it, so the edge pointed at the wrong function. Otherwise the call was parked, and the cross-file loop skips every member call.

The engine now knows which import binds each receiver. The resolution pass resolves `fn` against the module's real exports:

```diff
 engine: member call ns.fn()
+  if ns is bound by `import * as ns from './m'` (corpus file, not shadowed in the caller)
+    skip the same-file bare-name lookup
+    stamp the raw call with (m, "*")
 resolution pass
+  record `import * as ns` as an import fact with imported name "*"
+  turn each stamped call into a use fact `ns.fn`
+  fn = the one export of m named fn (re-export chains, `export { a as b }`, `export * as ns`)
+  no export of that name -> no edge
```

The lookup uses the export table that named imports already use (`exported_candidates`), so it handles renames the same way. Unlike `resolve_exported_origin`, it doesn't fall back to "a symbol with that name exists in the file", so `ns.privateFn()` makes no edge.

**Before** (the issue's repro, v8):

```text
calls dispatch() -> helper()
```

**After:**

```text
calls dispatch() -> helper()
calls dispatch() -> submit()
calls dispatch() -> reveal()
calls direct()   -> submit()
```

I chose this after writing the tests first and running four candidates against them:

| | A: resolution pass only | B: engine + new resolver | C: A + class methods + engine guard | D: engine binding + export table (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| issue repro (T1) | 4/4 | 4/4 | 4/4 | 4/4 |
| class methods, nested functions, `.tsx`, `.mjs` (T2) | 3/5 | 5/5 | 4/5 | 5/5 |
| through barrels (T3) | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| `export { a as b }`: `x.b()` edge, `x.a()` none | pass | fail | pass | pass |
| no edge to an unexported function | fail | fail | fail | pass |
| no edge to a same-named function in the caller's file | fail | pass | pass | pass |
| shadowing, external package, `import type` (T4) | pass | pass | pass | pass |

B rebuilt the export table from graph labels. That lost the renamed name and treated every `contains` child as an export.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A call `ns.fn()` through `import * as ns from './m'` has a `calls` edge to the function `m` exports as `fn`, and to nothing else.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No id changes and no schema bump: JS/TS files skip the per-file AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`), so the next extract gives the new edges, and a revert gives v8 output again.

**Blast Radius:** small. Only JS/TS graphs change, and only around namespace imports. On a 2876-file TypeScript project, 12 edges were added and 7 removed out of 15567, and I checked each against the source:

- **Removed:** 7 calls like `ops.add()` inside a class method `add()`, which v8 bound to the class's own `.add()`.
- **Added:** those 7 calls, plus `ops.list()` and `ops.wakeNow()`, now point at `service/ops.ts`. 3 more are calls inside `it(...)` callbacks, through an `export *` barrel.

Extraction took 37.7 s, against 38.6 s on v8 (median of 3).

**Limitations**

- A top-level `ns.fn()` statement, outside any function, still makes no edge, the same as a bare call. `test_ts_import_require.py` pins the edges of that case.
- `ops.a.b()` and `const f = ops.submit; f()` still make no edge. `new ops.K()` and `const { submit } = ops; submit()` now do. All four are `xfail(strict=False)`, because their wanted behaviour isn't decided.
- Only relative imports resolve, the same as other JS imports here (`_resolve_js_module_path`). `tsconfig` path aliases and Vue/Svelte callers are untested.
- The `"*"` import fact goes into the shared alias table. `"*"` is never an export name, so a bare `ops()` resolves to nothing.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_js_exported_fn_call_resolution.py`, next to the #3346 tests. Each one runs `extract()` on a small project and asserts `(caller, callee, callee file)` edges. None of them calls a private helper.

| T3b: renamed re-export | fail | pass |
| T4: no edge to a same-named function in the caller's file | fail: binds to it | pass |
| T4: name not exported, local and parameter shadow, `react`, `import type` | pass | pass |
| T4b: no edge to an unexported function | pass | pass |
| T5: chain, const alias, `new`, destructure | 3 xfail, 1 xpass | 2 xfail, 2 xpass |
| T6: named, aliased (#3346) and default imports, `imports_from` edges | pass | pass |

On v8 the tests that pass do so because v8 makes no namespace edges at all. They guard against binding by name.

items.title: fix(vbnet): resolve calls through typed fields, Me.field and With blocks (#4588)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4588. Stacked on #4573, so only the last two commits are new: 467f15ba (tests) and 25d072bc (fix).

The VB resolver dropped calls made through a field, through `Me.field`, and inside `With` blocks:

```vb
Private _repo As Repository        ' F1-F5
_repo.Save()                       ' no edge
Me._repo.Save()                    ' no edge
With _repo
    .Load()                        ' no edge
End With
```

Fields had no declared type, so a field receiver hid the call and nothing replaced it.

```diff
 resolve(call)
   locals / parameters
+  field of the caller's type (all partial files), then VB bases nearest first
+    declared type known and unique -> member of that type, INFERRED 0.85
+    untyped / external / ambiguous -> no edge (still hides a same-named type)
   type or Module named by the receiver

 walk(method body)
+  With target stack: `.M()` -> call on the innermost target
+    name / Me.name -> resolved like name.M()
+    New T()        -> typed receiver T
+    anything else  -> no edge
```

- Only `As T` and `As New T()` give a field a type. `Private x = New T()` is `Object` to the compiler, because Option Infer doesn't apply to fields.
- The field's type is resolved with the declaring file's namespace and imports.
- `Me.f`, `MyClass.f` and `OwnType.f` resolve like `f`.
- A typed local or field of an interface type binds to the interface member, as the compiler does.
- VB→C# edges keep the `_vbnet_resolved` marker from #4573.
- `watch.py` forwards `declared_type` and `imports`. `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 21 → 22.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a VB `calls` edge points only at the method the compiler would bind. When the receiver's type isn't known for sure, there's no edge, never a guess.

I checked each case against the VB compiler (dotnet SDK 8.0, 30 cases). A local, a parameter or a `Shadows` field hides a field. A field hides a type of the same name. Nested `With` uses the innermost target. Lambdas see the `With` target. An untyped field is `Object` (BC30209 under Strict On).

Persisted state: field and property nodes gain `metadata.owner`, `declared_type`, `namespace` and `imports`. The schema bump re-extracts cached VB files. The change is two-way: reverting it and bumping the schema again restores the old graph.

Known gap: a call whose receiver is a field declared in another partial file or a base class can still bind to a type with the same name in the calling file (same-file shortcut). #4573 behaves the same way, and it takes a field named exactly like a type.

items.title: fix(vbnet): resolve cross-file calls to Module members, typed locals and C# statics (#4570)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4570. In a VB.NET project, `calls` edges appeared only when the caller and the callee were in the same file.

For each invocation, `extract_vbnet` picks the type that owns the target. An unqualified call or a `Me` call gets the caller's own type. A qualified call is looked up in `owner_by_short`, which only holds types declared in that file. Anything else (a Module in another file, a local variable, a C# type) got `target_owner = None` and was dropped: no edge and no raw call, so no resolver could see it. The only VB resolver, `resolve_vbnet_partial_calls`, matches `(owner, name, arity)` for `Partial` types. The shared name pass skips VB calls because they are marked as member calls.

| Call in `Caller.vb` | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `LogIt("x")`, a Module Sub in another file | raw call with owner `Caller`, no edge | `LogIt` in `Helpers.vb`, EXTRACTED |
| `Helpers.LogIt("x")`, Module in another file | dropped | EXTRACTED |
| `Dim w As New Worker()` then `w.Save()` | dropped | `Worker.Save`, INFERRED |
| `CsRules.IsLocked(1)`, a C# static | dropped | EXTRACTED |
| `.Save()` inside `With w` | **wrong edge** to the caller's own `Save` | no edge |
| `handler(1)`, `handler` a local `Action(Of Integer)` | **wrong edge** to a `handler` method | no edge |

The extractor now emits a raw call for every invocation, with the written receiver, its kind (`none`, `me`, `mybase`, `name`, `local`), the declared type of a local or parameter, the caller's namespace, the file's `Imports` and the caller's nested types. The raw calls keep `is_member_call`, so the shared name pass still never sees them. `resolve_vbnet_calls` replaces the partial-type resolver (the old name stays as an alias and as the registry name) and follows VB's lookup order:

```text
resolve(call)
  unqualified / Me
    nearest of own type, then in-corpus bases, that declares the name -> it decides, at any arity
    a field, property or event with the name -> no edge
    else Modules in scope (same, enclosing, global or imported namespace) with that member
      exactly one Module, exactly one arity match -> edge, else none
  MyBase                -> the base chain only
  local / parameter     -> its declared type, then member lookup          (INFERRED)
  Type.M() / Module.M() -> a field or nested type of that name hides it
                           else the type unique in scope, VB or C#, then member lookup
  a VB target must accept the arity; a C# target must be the only method of that name
  a caller whose base chain leaves the corpus -> INFERRED, context external_base_may_hide
```

Only a unique match makes an edge. Nothing falls back to a name match across the corpus.

I checked every rule against the compiler before writing it. I used dotnet SDK 8.0 in a container, offline, with small VB projects that print which method ran:

| Case | Compiler |
|---|---|
| unqualified call, Module in another file, same namespace | binds the Module |
| Module in another namespace, no `Imports` | BC30451 |
| with `Imports`, or Module in an enclosing namespace | binds the Module |
| caller's class or its base declares `LogIt` (any arity) | binds the class method, or BC30455 |
| two Modules declare `LogIt`, even at different arities | BC30562 |
| field, property, delegate field or nested type with the name | hides the Module |
| two `Helpers` in namespaces the caller doesn't import | BC30451 |
| `As New Worker()`, `As Worker = New Worker()`, `Dim w = New Worker()` | `Worker.Save` |
| `CsRules.IsLocked(1)` and `csrules.islocked(1)` from VB | the C# method |
| `.Save()` in `With w` | `w.Save` |
| `handler(1)`, `handler` a local delegate | the delegate |

`watch.py` now forwards `owner`, `full_name`, `accepted_arities` and `namespace` to the context nodes of unchanged files (#2406). Without them, an unchanged `Helpers.vb` reached the resolver with no owner. This has two side effects: the existing partial-type resolver now works on incremental rebuilds too, and `_resolve_csharp_qualified_calls` binds the same as a full build on an incremental rebuild. With `Svc` in both `Alpha` and `Beta` and a caller with `using Beta`, v8 bound an incremental rebuild to `Alpha.Svc.Save`, and now binds `Beta.Svc.Save`. Only the VB resolver and that C# resolver read `metadata.namespace`.

`_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes from 17 to 18. #4567 and #4572 bump the same line from 17 to 18, so whichever lands later needs 19.

**Before** (the issue's repro, `extract --code-only --force`):

```text
A_SameFileSelf -> B_Target()   EXTRACTED
.G_CsToVb      -> LogIt()      EXTRACTED
```

**After:**

```text
A_SameFileSelf      -> B_Target()    EXTRACTED
C_UnqualifiedModule -> LogIt()       EXTRACTED  call
D_QualifiedModule   -> LogIt()       EXTRACTED  call
E_TypedLocal        -> Save()        INFERRED   call
F_CsStatic          -> .IsLocked()   EXTRACTED  call
.G_CsToVb           -> LogIt()       EXTRACTED  call
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A VB.NET call gets a `calls` edge exactly when the VB compiler's lookup gives one target in the corpus, and never to a target the compiler would not pick.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. New raw-call fields, a resolver, four metadata keys forwarded in `watch.py`, and a cache schema bump. No id, graph format or manifest change. Reverting restores v8 output after one re-extract.

**Blast Radius:** moderate. VB.NET graphs gain many `calls` edges, so `affected`, `path`, `explain`, god nodes and communities change for VB projects. Two kinds of wrong v8 edges go away (`With` blocks, local delegates). C# changes only on incremental rebuilds, where it now matches a full build. Bumping `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` invalidates the whole AST cache, so the first forced run after upgrading re-extracts every code file once.

**Limitations**

- A receiver typed by a field (`Private _w As Worker`, then `_w.Save()`) is not tracked. Recorded as a strict xfail.
- The target of a `With` block is not tracked, so `.Save()` gets no edge rather than `w.Save`. Recorded as a strict xfail.
- Project-level `Imports` and `RootNamespace` from the `.vbproj` are not visible. This can only miss a Module, never pick a wrong one, because the compiler sees a superset of what graphify sees. Exception: in a corpus with several projects that don't reference each other, a Module from an unreferenced project can be bound.
- `Shared` versus instance members are not modeled.
- A C# target with overloads gets no edge from VB, because C# method nodes carry no arity.
- Found while testing, separate bugs, recorded as strict xfails: the C# member resolver ignores arity when calling an overloaded VB Module (it bound the two-argument overload of `LogIt`), and nested VB types are not extracted at all.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_vbnet_extractor.py`, built on `extract()` with real files under `tmp_path`. They find nodes by label and file name, not by id. Each expected result comes from the compiler cases above.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| unqualified call reaches a Module Sub in another file | fail | pass |
| module-qualified call reaches a Module in another file | fail | pass |
| local typed `As New T()` / `As T = New T()` (×2) | fail | pass |
| VB call reaches a C# static | fail | pass |
| `LogIt` / `logit` / `LOGIT` all bind the Module | fail | pass |
| incremental rebuild of only the caller keeps the edge (#2406) | fail | pass |
| external base: unqualified and qualified Module call is INFERRED (×2) | fail | pass |
| `.Save()` in a `With` block is not a call on the caller's own `Save` | fail: wrong edge | pass |
| a local delegate call is not a call of a same-named method | fail: wrong edge | pass |
| schema-17 cache entry is not served | fail | pass |
| inferred local `Dim w = New Worker()` | fail | pass |
| parameter typed `As Worker` | fail | pass |
| Module through `Imports`, Module in an enclosing namespace | fail | pass |
| edge confidence for each form (×4) | fail | pass |
| inherited method reached | fail | pass |
| lowercase VB call reaches a C# method | fail | pass |
| own method wins; inherited method is never replaced by a Module | pass | pass |
| class method hides the Module at any arity | pass | pass |
| two Modules with the same name give no edge (×2) | pass | pass |
| `As Object` receiver binds to nothing | pass | pass |
| never binds a same-named Python function | pass | pass |
| same-file and `Partial` calls keep their edges and context | pass | pass |
| C# → VB Module call keeps its edge | pass | pass |
| Module in a namespace that isn't imported is out of scope | pass | pass |
| unqualified call never binds an unrelated class's method (VB, C#) | pass | pass |
| field or nested class named like the Module hides it (×2) | pass | pass |
| two `Helpers` in namespaces not imported give no edge | pass | pass |
| property, field or delegate field named like the Sub hides it (×3) | pass | pass |
| field-typed receiver | xfail | xfail (limitation) |
| `With` block target | xfail | xfail (limitation) |
| C# call to an overloaded VB Module picks by arity | xfail | xfail (separate bug) |
| nested class named like the Module is the target | xfail | xfail (separate bug) |

Most of the guards pass on v8 only because v8 binds no cross-file VB calls at all. They protect the new resolver. The three property/field guards failed on an earlier version of this branch, before the member check was added. The cache test fails with the schema set back to 17.

```text
pytest tests/test_vbnet_extractor.py -q (new tests, on v8 86c57be8)   -> 22 failed, 26 passed, 4 xfailed
pytest tests/test_vbnet_extractor.py -q (this branch)                 -> 48 passed, 4 xfailed
pytest -q (full suite, --basetemp=/var/tmp)                           -> 8432 passed, 14 skipped, 4 xfailed
ruff check graphify/ tests/test_vbnet_extractor.py                    -> All checks passed
```

One full-suite run had a single failure in `test_pr10_watch_overrides.py::test_ignored_root_configuration_still_rebuilds_the_graph[True]`, a PHP watcher test. It passed on the next full run and 8 out of 8 times alone, on both v8 and this branch.

items.title: fix(json_config): link a package.json dependency's manifest entry to its ref node (#4569)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4569. Each package.json dependency produced two nodes labelled `react` with no edge between them:

- the manifest entry `<stem>_dependencies_react` (type code, carries the version-range line), reached through `dependencies --contains-->`;
- the ref node `ref_react` (type concept), reached through `package.json --imports-->`. Code imports (`import React from "react"`) resolve here.

5711e9d2 (#1764 follow-up) moved the `imports` edge from `key_nid` to `file_nid` so it would stop reading as `react --imports--> react`. That edge was the only link between the two nodes. On v8 the manifest entry is 4 hops from the code that imports the package, the two land in different communities, `explain react` exits 3 ("Ambiguous: 'react' matches 2 nodes in package.json"), and `affected react` prints "No unique node match".

The manifest entry now has a `declares` edge to the ref node and is labelled `name@range`:

```diff
 elif parent_key in _DEP_KEYS and val_text.strip():
     dep_nid = _make_id("ref", key)
     add_node(dep_nid, key, line, file_type="concept")
     add_edge(file_nid, dep_nid, "imports", line, context="import")
+    add_edge(key_nid, dep_nid, "declares", line)
+    version = one line of val_text, capped at 40 chars ("...")
+    relabel key_nid to f"{key}@{version}"   # only if its source_location is this line
```

The ref node keeps the bare name that imports resolve to, so the two nodes no longer share a label: no `react -> react` edge, and `react` resolves to one node. A blank range (`"   "`) now behaves like `""`: bare label, no ref, no edge. `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes from 17 to 18.

The relabel checks `source_location` because a key node id carries only the immediate parent key. In a v2 lockfile, `dependencies.semver` under two `node_modules/*` entries mints one node; `add_node` keeps the first, so relabelling every pair would put the later range on the first line (4 of 44 relabelled nodes on a 340-package lockfile).

**Before** (the issue's package.json):

```text
dependencies --contains--> react [code]
package.json --contains--> dependencies
package.json --contains--> name
package.json --imports--> react [concept]
```

**After:**

```text
dependencies --contains--> react@^19.0.0 [code]
package.json --contains--> dependencies
package.json --contains--> name
package.json --imports--> react [concept]
react@^19.0.0 --declares--> react [concept]
```

I chose this after writing tests for the wanted behaviour and running four candidates against them:

| | A: `declares` edge | A2: `references` edge | B: no key node | C: edge + `name@range` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| entry connected to importing code | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| no edge between same-label nodes (#1764) | no | no | yes | yes |
| `explain` / `affected` resolve `react` | no | no | yes | yes |
| unimported devDependency not flagged isolated | yes | yes | no | yes |
| existing tests pass | yes | yes | no (`test_extract_json_nested_contains`) | yes |

A2 also makes `affected` list the manifest line as a consumer, since `references` is in `DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS`. `declares` is not, and nothing in graphify whitelists relation names.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A package.json dependency's manifest entry is connected to the code that imports the package, and no edge joins two nodes with the same label.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. One edge and one relabel in the `_DEP_KEYS` branch, plus a cache schema bump. No id changes. Reverting restores v8 output after one re-extract.

**Blast Radius:** moderate. Every manifest entry under a dependency block changes label (`react` becomes `react@^19.0.0`), and anything keyed on that label sees the new text. The ref node keeps `react`, so searching for the package still finds it. Bumping `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` invalidates the whole AST cache, so the first forced run after upgrading re-extracts every code file once.

**Limitations**

- A v2 `package-lock.json` already takes this path on v8 (its top-level `dependencies` key makes it config JSON). Its nested entries get the new label and edge too: 99 `declares` edges on a 340-package lockfile. v3 lockfiles are skipped as data JSON. I did not change `_is_config_json`.
- npm reads `""` and `"   "` as `*`. graphify has never linked `""`, unchanged here; `"   "` used to mint `ref_react` and an `imports` edge and now matches `""`.
- A small community named after its hub can now carry a range, e.g. `left-pad@workspace:*`.
- Obsidian note names drop the caret (`react@19.0.0.md`); the existing numeric-suffix dedup handles collisions.
- With two package.json files, each manifest's ref id is file-qualified (`a_package_json_ref_react`) while code imports a separate `ref_react`, so in a monorepo the manifest and the code still don't connect. Separate bug, recorded as a strict xfail.
- The issue says the `@types/*` key nodes show as isolated. On v8 they are already exempt (#4205); the flagged node is the ref node, which this PR now connects.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_extract.py`, next to the existing json_config tests. The build-level tests run `extract` + `build_from_json` on a package.json and a `.tsx` that imports `react`. The manifest entry is found by structure (`contains` from the dependency block), not by label, so a relabel can't pass them on its own.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| entry within 2 hops of the importing code | fail: 4 hops | pass |
| every dependency block (×4) | fail | pass |
| stale cache entry not served (fails with schema 17) | fail | pass |
| one node labelled with the bare name | fail: 2 | pass |
| `explain` / `affected` resolve the package name | fail: ambiguous | pass |
| unimported devDependency not reported isolated | fail | pass |
| label carries a one-line capped range (×8) | fail | pass |
| blank range: bare name, no ref, no edge | fail | pass |
| key shared by two sibling blocks labelled with the range on its own line | fail | pass |
| no same-label `imports`, no self-loop | pass | pass |
| no edge of any relation between same-label nodes | pass | pass |
| `utils` dependency stays a namespaced `ref_` | pass | pass |
| declaring line recorded | pass | pass |
| two manifests keep their own lines | pass | pass |
| non-dependency keys unchanged | pass | pass |
| ref node keeps the bare name | pass | pass |
| empty range unchanged | pass | pass |
| non-string values unchanged | pass | pass |
| two-manifest corpus reaches its entry | xfail | xfail (strict) |

The ones that pass on v8 guard #1764, J-4 and existing output.

items.title: fix(hooks): try python before python3 under Git for Windows so the Store alias never runs (#4563)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4563. When the hook's interpreter probes 1 to 4 all miss, its last resort tried `python3` before `python`. On Windows 10/11, `python3` is usually the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps`, because python.org's installer ships `python.exe` but no `python3.exe`. Running the alias opens a console window for about 1.1 s and exits 9009. The hook then falls through to the real `python`, so it works, but every commit, checkout and merge flashes a window and blocks before the detached rebuild starts.

The last resort is reached when the pinned interpreter, `.graphify_python`, the launcher and the uv-tools scan all miss: a removed venv, graphify moved to another env, or a GUI client with a minimal PATH.

Under Git for Windows the last resort now tries `python` first. The Windows check is the one `hooks.py` already uses for its pipe-handle handling.

```diff
 # Last resort: try python3 / python (works for system/venv installs on PATH).
+# Under Git for Windows `python3` is usually the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias
+# ... Try `python` first there (#4563).
 if [ -z "$GRAPHIFY_PYTHON" ]; then
-    if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && python3 -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
-        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="python3"
-    elif command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1 && python -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
-        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="python"
+    if [ -n "${WINDIR:-}" ] || [ -n "${MSYSTEM:-}" ]; then
+        _GFY_FIRST="python"; _GFY_SECOND="python3"
+    else
+        _GFY_FIRST="python3"; _GFY_SECOND="python"
+    fi
+    if command -v "$_GFY_FIRST" >/dev/null 2>&1 && "$_GFY_FIRST" -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
+        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="$_GFY_FIRST"
+    elif command -v "$_GFY_SECOND" >/dev/null 2>&1 && "$_GFY_SECOND" -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
+        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="$_GFY_SECOND"
     else
```

Probes 1 to 4, the probe command, the interpreter names, the "could not locate a Python" message and `exit 0` are unchanged. All four generated hooks splice in the same `_PYTHON_DETECT`, so one edit covers post-commit, post-checkout, post-merge and post-rewrite.

I did not take the issue's second suggestion, skipping a `python3` under `*/WindowsApps/*`. A real Store Python also lives there, so skipping it would remove the last resort for Store-Python users.

**Before** (v8 probe block, a fake `WindowsApps/python3` that logs, sleeps 1 s and exits 9009, ahead of a real `python`):

```text
calls:  python3 (stub), python
chose:  python          1.07 s
```

**After** (`MSYSTEM=MINGW64`):

```text
calls:  python
chose:  python
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Under Git for Windows, the hook never runs `python3` while `python` can import graphify. Everywhere else the probe order is unchanged.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. A probe-order change inside a generated hook script. No schema, cache or file-format change. Existing installs pick it up on the next `graphify hook install`.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Only the last-resort branch changes, and only when `WINDIR` or `MSYSTEM` is set. Linux and macOS keep `python3` then `python`. If `WINDIR` or `MSYSTEM` leaks into a non-Windows shell (for example WSL with `WSLENV`), the only effect is that `python` is tried before `python3`.

**Limitations**

- Not run on Windows. The behavioural tests use `sh`-script fakes and skip on `nt`. The reporter's measurements (about 1.1 s, exit 9009, one `AppInstallerPythonRedirector.exe` per call) are the Windows evidence.
- Hooks already installed keep the old order until `graphify hook install` is run again.
- If `python` is itself a Store stub (no real Python on PATH), it still runs once before the warning.
- If `python` lacks graphify, `python3` is still probed after it.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_hooks.py`. They run the emitted `_PYTHON_DETECT` under a real `sh`, with a temp `HOME` so probes 1 to 4 miss, and only two fake directories on PATH: `WindowsApps/python3` and `bin/python`. Each fake logs its call.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_windows_never_runs_the_store_python3_alias_when_python_works` [msystem] | fail: calls `python3, python` | pass: calls `python` |
| `test_windows_never_runs_the_store_python3_alias_when_python_works` [windir] | fail: same | pass |
| `test_windows_falls_back_to_python3_when_python_lacks_graphify` | fail: calls `python3` | pass: calls `python, python3`, picks `python3` |
| `test_outside_windows_python3_is_still_tried_first` | pass | pass |
| `test_windows_with_no_working_python_still_fails_loudly_and_exits_zero` | pass | pass |
| `test_every_hook_embeds_the_probe_chain_unchanged` (4 hooks) | pass | pass |

The ones that pass on v8 guard existing behaviour: the Linux/macOS order, the warning path, and that every hook carries the tested block.

The same block also ran under `dash` (`debian:stable-slim`) and BusyBox ash (`alpine:3.20`) with podman. Both parse it, and both give the same call order as above, with and without `MSYSTEM`.

```text
pytest tests/test_hooks.py -q (new tests, on v8 86c57be8)          -> 3 failed, 6 passed
pytest tests/test_hooks.py -q (this branch)                        -> 181 passed
pytest -q (full suite, --basetemp=/var/tmp)                        -> 8401 passed, 14 skipped
ruff check graphify/hooks.py tests/test_hooks.py                   -> All checks passed
```

items.title: fix(rust): name a use rooted at a sibling mod so it reaches its declaration (#4564)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4564. A Rust `use` rooted at a child module declared beside it, such as `pub use item::Invoice;` next to `mod item;`, left its `imports_from` edge dangling. Build then minted an `external` stub `invoice`, and `affected` and `explain` tied on it.

The #4439 fix lends `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` a temporary node for every edge that carries `_rust_use_name`. `name_use` sets that only when the path's first segment is `crate`, `self` or `super`, so that `use serde::Serialize` never lands on a corpus `Serialize` (5faa05c8). `item::Invoice` starts with `item`, which looks the same as `serde::` to that check, so it got no lent node.

Rust settles which one a first segment means. A `mod` declared in the same scope shadows a crate of the same name, and only a leading `::` reaches the crate. Checked with `cargo check` on rustc 1.95.0, using a stand-in `serde` crate:

| Code | Result |
|---|---|
| `mod serde { … }` + `use serde::Serialize;`, same scope | E0432 |
| `mod serde;` (file module) + `use serde::Serialize;` | E0432 |
| `mod serde` + `use ::serde::Serialize;` | compiles, reaches the crate |
| top-level `mod serde` + `mod tests { use serde::Serialize; }` | compiles, reaches the crate |

So the rule is exact: a first segment that names a sibling `mod_item` is this crate's, unless the path starts with `::`.

```diff
 use_declaration
+  scope_mods = names of mod_item siblings of this use     # either order; an inline mod is its own scope
   name_use(written, path)
-    if first segment in (crate, self, super)
+    if first segment in (crate, self, super)
+       or (first segment in scope_mods and path does not start with "::")
       edge._rust_use_name = written
```

`_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes from 17 to 18, so a cached 0.9.92 result without the name is not served.

**Before** (the issue's four files, `extract --code-only --cargo --force`, `cluster-only`):

```text
graph.json   NODE invoice  type=external  source_file=''
             EDGE src_model -> invoice
affected Invoice   No unique node match for Invoice                      (exit 0)
explain Invoice    Ambiguous: 'Invoice' matches 2 nodes in different files.   (exit 3)
```

**After:**

```text
graph.json   EDGE src_model -> src_model_item_invoice    (no external node)
affected Invoice   Affected nodes for Invoice …
explain Invoice    Node: Invoice  ID: src_model_item_invoice  Source: src/model/item.rs L1
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A Rust `use` reaches its declaration whenever Rust resolves the path inside this crate. A path Rust resolves to another crate never lands on a corpus declaration.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. One extra condition in `name_use` and a cache schema bump. No graph format, id or manifest change. Reverting restores v8 behaviour. The schema bump costs one re-extract of cached Rust files on the next forced run.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Only Rust `use` edges rooted at a sibling `mod` change, and only from a dangling stub to the real declaration. `use` paths rooted at `crate`, `self`, `super`, `::` or an outside crate behave as on v8. Bumping `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` invalidates the whole AST cache, not only Rust entries, so the first forced run after upgrading re-extracts every code file once.

**Limitations**

- An incremental `graphify extract` (no `--force`) skips a file whose content hash matches `manifest.json` before it reads the AST cache (`detect_incremental`). The schema bump never reaches those files, so an existing graph keeps the stub until `--force` or an edit to the file. The same is true of every schema bump, #4439's included, because the manifest does not record the extractor version or schema.
- `_make_id("Invoice as Bill")` puts the alias in the raw target id (`invoice_as_bill`), for `crate::`, `self::` and bare paths alike. The rewire hides it whenever it resolves the edge. Not changed here.
- A `use` inside a fn body gets no edge (the extractor does not visit fn bodies), and `r#item` paths are not matched. Both are unchanged from v8.
- In `pub use item::{self as items, Invoice};`, `Invoice` lands, but the `self as items` binding names a module, which has no declaration node, so it stays a stub as on v8.

## How was this tested?

15 new tests in `tests/test_rust_use_trees.py`, next to the #4439 tests:

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_a_use_rooted_at_a_child_mod_lands_on_the_declaration` [plain, use_first, pub_crate, rename, self_alias_group] | 5 fail | pass |
| `test_the_issue_repro_builds_without_an_external_stub` (build level) | fail | pass |
| `test_a_group_and_a_nested_path_from_a_child_mod_land_on_the_declarations` | fail | pass |
| `test_a_use_of_a_mod_declared_inline_lands_on_the_declaration` | fail | pass |
| `test_a_use_rooted_at_a_local_mod_named_like_a_crate_lands_on_the_local_declaration` | fail | pass |
| `test_a_cache_entry_from_before_child_mod_names_is_not_served` | fail | pass |
| `test_a_use_of_another_crate_still_does_not_land_on_a_same_named_declaration` [leading_colons, inner_scope, outside_crate] | pass | pass |
| `test_a_second_import_of_the_same_item_does_not_change_the_result` | pass | pass |
| `test_two_types_with_one_name_stay_two_nodes_and_are_not_swapped` | pass | pass |

The five that pass on v8 guard the serde concern, the second-import case that can hide this bug in larger repos, and two distinct `Invoice` types that must not be cross-linked. The cache test fails on this branch with the schema set back to 17 (`assert ['invoice'] == ['src_model_item_invoice']`) and passes with 18.

```text
pytest tests/test_rust_use_trees.py -q (new tests, on v8 86c57be8)    -> 10 failed, 5 passed
pytest tests/test_rust_*.py -q (this branch)                          -> 98 passed
pytest -q (full suite, --basetemp=/var/tmp)                           -> 8407 passed, 14 skipped
ruff check graphify/extractors/rust.py graphify/cache.py tests/test_rust_use_trees.py -> All checks passed
```

A separate session that did not write the fix also ran 20 end-to-end cases (`extract`, `cluster-only`, `affected`, `explain`) against v8 and this branch, with `cargo check` as ground truth for each. Fixed: the issue's repro, the `use` before the `mod`, a group, a nested path, an inline `mod`, `pub(crate) use` and `as Bill`. Unchanged and never landing on a corpus `Serialize`: `use ::serde::Serialize;`, `use ::serde::{Serialize};` (the group binding reaches `name_use` as `::serde::Serialize`), the `mod tests` inner scope and a plain `use serde::Serialize;`.

items.title: fix(extract): let the model acknowledge empty files so they don't arm the shrink guard (#4547)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4547. A file the model read and found empty (a `robots.txt`, an HTML shell, a short compose file) failed `graphify extract` on every run, the same way a file the model skipped does.

A file sent for semantic extraction counts as covered only if a returned node has it as `source_file`. Zero nodes puts it in `uncovered_files`, which sets `_extraction_incomplete`. That turns off `force`, so any run where the graph shrinks is refused and exits non-zero. The response format has only `nodes`, `edges` and `hyperedges`, so the model has no way to say "read it, nothing here." A retry sends the same file and gets the same answer.

A file the model read and found empty also failed a second way. A chunk holding only that file got an empty response, which `_response_is_hollow` treats as hollow. It was retried at 2 s and 8 s, then marked partial, which also arms the guard.

What changes, per file sent:

| Model's response for the file | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | covered | covered |
| no nodes, listed with `entities: 0` | uncovered, guard armed | `empty_files`, guard not armed |
| no nodes, not listed | uncovered | uncovered |
| no nodes, listed with `entities > 0` | uncovered | uncovered |
| no `files` key at all | uncovered | uncovered |
| in a truncated or hollow chunk | partial | partial, whatever it says |

```diff
 _EXTRACTION_SYSTEM schema
-{"nodes":[...],"edges":[...],"hyperedges":[...],"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0}
+{"nodes":[...],"edges":[...],"hyperedges":[...],"files":[{"path":"relative/path","entities":0}],...}

 _extract_with_adaptive_retry
   result = extract_files_direct(chunk)
+  _take_acks(result)        # keep 0-entity acks for paths in THIS chunk -> _empty_files
+                            # acks name only some files and no items -> hollow, normal retry

 _response_is_hollow
-  return not nodes and not edges and not hyperedges
+  no items and every acknowledged file has entities == 0 -> not hollow

 extract_corpus_parallel
-  uncovered = dispatched - covered
+  empty_files = (dispatched - covered) & acked_empty - partial
+  uncovered   = dispatched - covered - empty_files
```

The CLI also writes the full uncovered list to `graphify-out/uncovered_files.txt`, with paths relative to the corpus root, and removes a stale copy at the start of the next extract. Before this, the warning named five files and "+N more", and the rest were only in memory. The llm.py warning no longer says a re-run will retry the files. They are re-sent every run, but with the same `--token-budget` the model usually skips the same ones.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Only a file the model left out, or one from a truncated or hollow chunk, arms the shrink guard. A file the model read and acknowledged as empty does not.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. `files` is optional and is read only by the coverage check. It is popped before anything reaches the cache or `graph.json`. A response without it behaves exactly as on v8. Reverting the commit restores the old behaviour, and no stored data needs migrating.

**Blast Radius:** moderate. Every semantic extraction prompt gains the `files` rule, so each response gets slightly longer (one short entry per file). Runs that failed only because of empty files now write the graph. The guard now trusts a model's 0 for a file that comes back with no nodes.

**Limitations**

- If the model writes nodes for some files and falsely lists the others as `entities: 0`, those files won't arm the guard. The case in #4547 (files never mentioned) is still caught.
- If a large document is split into slices and one slice acknowledges 0 while another slice is never mentioned, the file counts as empty.
- `references/extraction-spec.md` has no `files` rule, so skill-driven extraction is unchanged.
- Empty files are still re-sent on every run. #2927 deliberately keeps zero-node results out of the semantic cache, and I left that rule alone. Caching an acknowledged 0 can be a follow-up if wanted.

## How was this tested?

New file `tests/test_empty_file_ack.py`, 11 tests. They patch out the model call and the hollow-retry sleep, so they make no network calls and run in about a second.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| acknowledged-empty file is not uncovered | fail | pass |
| chunk with only an empty file succeeds, no retry | fail | pass |
| files-only response is not hollow; empty and junk `files` still are | fail | pass |
| `extract` keeps `force=True` when an empty file is acknowledged | fail | pass |
| `uncovered_files.txt` holds every path, removed on a clean run | fail | pass |
| unacknowledged file stays uncovered | pass | pass |
| no `files` key behaves as before | pass | pass |
| `entities > 0` with no node stays uncovered | pass | pass |
| ack for a path outside the chunk is ignored | pass | pass |
| truncated chunk that acknowledges stays partial | pass | pass |
| files-only response that misses a file is still hollow | pass | pass |

The six that pass on v8 guard the existing behaviour.

```text
pytest tests/test_empty_file_ack.py -q (this branch)                        -> 11 passed
pytest tests/test_empty_file_ack.py tests/test_chunking.py \

pytest -q (full suite, --basetemp=/var/tmp)                                  -> 8403 passed, 14 skipped
ruff check graphify/llm.py graphify/cli.py tests/test_empty_file_ack.py     -> All checks passed
```

items.title: fix: keep a wiki page relabelled only by case (#4508)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
Fixes #4508. A community relabelled only by case keeps its wiki article on case-insensitive filesystems. ## Summary On APFS (macOS) and NTFS (Windows), `groups.md` and `Groups.md` are one file. When a community's label changes from `groups` to `Groups`, the export writes into the existing entry, and the entry keeps its old case. The end-of-run orphan sweep compared names case-sensitively, so it deleted the page the run had just written. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Before B1["write Groups.md
(lands in groups.md)"] --> B2{"sweep: 'groups.md' in produced?"} B2 -- "no (case differs)" --> B3["unlink groups.md
index.md links to missing file"] end subgraph After A1["write Groups.md
(lands in groups.md)"] --> A2{"sweep: same device+inode
as a produced page?"} A2 -- yes --> A3["keep, rename to Groups.md"] A2 -- no --> A4["unlink stale page"] end ``` The sweep now matches files by identity (device and inode) instead of by name. A page this run wrote is kept, and its entry is renamed to the produced case. A stale page that is a separate file is still removed. Case-folding the names was the other option in the issue. It was rejected because on Linux `groups.md` and `Groups.md` are two real files, so folding would keep a stale page. Changed: `graphify/wiki.py` (the sweep block plus a `_file_id` helper, 21 lines added, 1 removed). New: `tests/test_wiki_case_only_relabel.py` (2 tests). ## Evidence - **Before:** `to_wiki` relabel `groups` → `Groups` on upstream `v8`: `['Groups.md', 'index.md', 'other.md']`, but `Groups.md` is not a readable file. `index.md` links to it. The test `test_case_only_relabel_keeps_article_on_case_insensitive_fs` fails with `AssertionError` on `Groups.md` `is_file()`. - **After:** same run on this branch: `Groups.md` is readable and `index.md` links to it. Test passes. ```text upstream v8 test_case_only_relabel_keeps_article_on_case_insensitive_fs FAILED test_case_only_relabel_drops_old_page_on_case_sensitive_fs passed this branch test_case_only_relabel_keeps_article_on_case_insensitive_fs passed test_case_only_relabel_drops_old_page_on_case_sensitive_fs passed wiki suites (test_wiki, link_filename_parity, idempotent_writes, path_length) 70 passed, 3 skipped full suite (tests/) 8394 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed ruff check graphify/wiki.py + new test All checks passed ``` The case-insensitive test simulates APFS and NTFS with a symlink, because the test machine runs Linux. The test helper `_case_insensitive_write` documents this. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way. The change touches only the orphan sweep. No file format, schema or cache key changes. Reverting restores the name-based sweep. **Blast radius:** wiki export (`to_wiki`). It runs on every `graphify` export that writes a wiki. Output is unchanged unless a case-only relabel happens. The sweep now calls `stat` on each `*.md` in the wiki folder, which is one extra call per page. A stat failure on a dangling symlink still removes the link as before. ## What does this PR do? Fixes #4508. On a case-insensitive filesystem, a relabel that changes only case used to delete the new article and leave `index.md` pointing at it. The sweep now keeps any page this run wrote, even when its on-disk name has the old case, and renames the entry to the new case. - Single-case runs are unchanged. Each produced page still gets one file. - A stale page that is a different file is still removed on every platform. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Documentation - [x] Tests or CI - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Security fix ## Verification & Invariants Invariant: after an export, every page `index.md` links to exists, and the sweep never deletes a page the run wrote. - [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide. - [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant. - [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary. - [x] Added a **regression test** that fails on upstream `v8` and passes here. - [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation. - [x] Documented **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. ## How was this tested? ```text PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/wt-4508 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp=/var/tmp/... -q tests/test_wiki_case_only_relabel.py -> 2 passed (this branch); 1 failed, 1 passed (upstream v8) full suite: 8394 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed ``` ## Limitations - Not run on a real APFS or NTFS volume. The test simulates one with a symlink. - Windows `st_ino` values were not checked on Python 3.14. On Windows the sweep relies on device and inode numbers that Python reports for each file. - `to_obsidian` has a similar case-only collision (#2650). This PR does not change it. ## Graphify-specific checklist - [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts. N/A: no skill fragments changed. - [x] AST/structural extraction is deterministic. N/A: wiki export only. - [x] I reviewed security implications: no shell or Python interpolation added. - [x] No API keys or local-only graph data are included. - [ ] I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages. N/A: no AI attribution in the commits.

items.title: fix: same-named files from two repos are not one file in explain and path (#4512)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4512.

In a merged multi-repo graph, two nodes can share a label and a repo-relative `source_file`, for example `web/dup.py` and `ml/dup.py`. Both appear as `dup.py`. The same-file check used the bare `source_file`, so the two nodes counted as one file. `explain` and `path` then refused with "matches 2 nodes in dup.py", listed bare `L1` lines, and gave a hint that could not tell the candidates apart.

This PR makes a file the pair (repo, source_file). The refusal names each candidate's file with its repo, and when the same path exists in more than one repo, the hint says so and asks for the full node id.

```text
_rivals_across_files(tier)
  before: key = source_file           -> web/dup.py and ml/dup.py collapse to "dup.py"
  after:  key = (repo, source_file)   -> two files, cross-file branch

_ambiguity_message(...)
  repos differ        -> list "web/dup.py", "ml/dup.py"
  same path, 2 repos  -> hint: "the same path exists in more than one repo ..."
  otherwise           -> unchanged
```

- A repo is shown in the refusal only when the candidates span more than one repo.
- Single-repo graphs (no `repo` attribute) keep the old wording.
- Same-file duplicates keep the old same-file branch.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A same-named file from two repos is never silently merged into one file. A single-repo graph gives the same refusal text as before.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added **regression tests** that fail on the code before this change.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Only the wording of one refusal and the file key used to detect ambiguity change. No schema, cache or file-format change. Reverting restores the old wording.

**Blast Radius:** ambiguity refusals in merged graphs. `_resolve_single_node` is shared, so `explain`, `path`, and the `get_node` and `get_neighbors` tools all show the new wording. `query` and `--seed` are not changed here. Single-repo output is unchanged.

**Limitations**

- `query` and `--seed` still answer silently for same-named files from two repos. That is tracked by the #4511 fix, which is a separate PR.
- Repo-qualified paths such as `web/dup.py::Config` do not resolve. The refusal does not suggest them; it gives the node id.
- A graph where some nodes have a `repo` attribute and others do not is not covered by tests.

## How was this tested?

Repro: two repos, each with `dup.py` defining `Config`, merged with `graphify merge-graphs`.

```text
after
```
