items.title: fix(hooks): rebuild after cherry-pick, rebase and pull --rebase (#4490)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

labels.name: needs:title
labels.description: PR title should follow the conventional-commit format

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4490. After a clean `git cherry-pick`, a `git rebase` or a `git pull --rebase`, the hooks never launched a rebuild, so `graph.json` described the old code until the next plain commit.

There are two causes:
- **Cherry-pick.** `post-commit` exited on `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, which git leaves on disk while the hook runs. This is the same trap as `MERGE_HEAD` in #4463.
- **Rebase.** `post-commit` and `post-checkout` skip while `rebase-merge/` exists, and no hook rebuilt at the end.

**Before** (the issue's repro, v8 `10130e79`):

```text
git cherry-pick side   -> 0 rebuilds
git rebase main        -> 0 rebuilds
git commit (control)   -> 1 rebuild
```

**After:**

```text
git cherry-pick side   -> 1 rebuild
git rebase main        -> 1 rebuild
git commit (control)   -> 1 rebuild
```

```text
post-commit:
  drop the CHERRY_PICK_HEAD exit
  if sequencer/todo exists and its first line is the commit just made:
    more than one step left  -> skip (mid range pick or revert)
    last step                -> CHANGED = diff sequencer/head..HEAD   (one rebuild covers the range)
  else: a stale sequencer/ (left by git reset --hard) is ignored -> normal HEAD~1 rebuild

post-rewrite (new hook):
  $1 = rebase -> launch an unscoped rebuild, like post-merge
  $1 = amend  -> exit (post-commit already rebuilt)
  no rebase-merge check: rebase-merge/ is still on disk when post-rewrite runs
```

Why only the last step rebuilds: if `graphify-out/graph.json` is tracked, a rebuild between picks rewrites it, and git then refuses a later pick that touches it (`Your local changes ... would be overwritten by merge: graphify-out/graph.json`). Just dropping the `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` check hit exactly that.

```diff
 graphify/hooks.py
   _HOOK_SCRIPT (post-commit)
-    [ -f "$GIT_DIR/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" ] && exit 0
+    sequencer/todo check: skip mid-sequence, last step diffs from sequencer/head,
+    stale sequencer/ ignored
+  _REWRITE_SCRIPT (new), _REWRITE_HOOK_MARKER / _END
   install / uninstall / status
+    post-rewrite, same append/preserve handling as the other hooks
 graphify/__main__.py
   hook install help line names post-rewrite
```

### Existing tests this PR changes

| Test | Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_hooks_reuse_git_dir_from_env` | every script in `_HOOK_SCRIPTS` must contain `GIT_DIR=${GIT_DIR:-` | required only when the script reads `$GIT_DIR` | the new post-rewrite hook never reads `$GIT_DIR`; adding an unused line would be dead code |
| `_HOOK_SCRIPTS` parametrize list | 3 hooks | adds `post-rewrite` | the nohup, detach, worker-cap and quote-safety tests now cover the new hook too |

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Every git operation that changes the tree launches one rebuild when it finishes, and no hook rebuilds in the middle of a pick, revert or rebase sequence.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Shell hook scripts and one new hook file. No schema, cache or file-format change.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. This changes when the hooks launch a rebuild, not what a rebuild does:
- A clean cherry-pick, a rebase and `pull --rebase` now rebuild once.
- A range pick or revert rebuilds once at the end. A revert range used to rebuild after every step, with the same final graph.
- Plain commits, amends, checkouts and merges behave as before.
- `graphify hook install` now also writes `.git/hooks/post-rewrite`, appending to a user's existing one like the other hooks. `GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1` turns it off.

**Limitations**

- `--skip` on the last pick and `--quit` still leave the graph stale, as on v8. git runs no hook when a sequence ends that way.
- If you edit the commit message while resolving a pick, or revert a `Revert "..."` commit, the todo line no longer matches HEAD. That step is then treated as a stale sequencer and rebuilds mid-sequence. It never skips a rebuild. This comes from reading the logic, not a test.
- Hooks already installed keep the old behaviour until `graphify hook install` is run again.
- This PR doesn't touch `post-merge`. #4476 fixes that, and the two merge cleanly in either order. Merged together, the hook tests give 184 passed.

## How was this tested?

New `tests/test_hooks_rewrite.py` runs real git operations against the installed hooks and counts rebuild launches. Four of its tests run a real build and check the graph contents. Against v8's hooks it gives 8 failed and 4 passed. The 4 that pass are behaviours v8 already gets right: the plain-commit control, amend, the tracked-graph sequence, and the abandoned pick. They're there to prove this PR doesn't break those cases.

- `test_single_cherry_pick_rebuilds_once`, `test_range_cherry_pick_rebuilds_once`, `test_rebase_rebuilds_once`, `test_pull_rebase_rebuilds_once`, `test_conflicted_rebase_continues_and_rebuilds_once`

items.title: fix(hooks): drop MERGE_HEAD guard from post-merge so real merges rebuild (#4463)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4463. The post-merge hook never rebuilt after a merge that makes a merge commit (`--no-ff`, diverged branches, `git pull`). Only fast-forward merges rebuilt.

`_MERGE_SCRIPT` exits early if `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists. On git 2.54, MERGE_HEAD is still on disk while post-merge runs, and git deletes it after the hook returns. A fast-forward never writes it, which is why those merges still worked. I reproduced this on Linux with git 2.54.0, so it isn't specific to Windows.

What the hook sees while it runs:

| Merge | MERGE_HEAD during post-merge | v8 hook |
|---|---|---|
| fast-forward | absent | rebuilds |
| `--no-ff` | present | exits |
| diverged branches | present | exits |
| `git pull` (diverged) | present | exits |

So the #2418 cleanup (removing symbols the union merge driver brings back) never ran on a real merge.

**Before** (`sh -x` on the installed hook, `git merge --no-ff feat`):

```text
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-merge ']'
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-apply ']'
+ '[' -f .git/MERGE_HEAD ']'
+ exit 0
```

**After:**

```text
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-merge ']'
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-apply ']'
+ '[' -f .git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD ']'
...
[graphify] Merge completed - launching background rebuild (log: ...)
```

```diff
 _MERGE_SCRIPT
-# This hook only fires after a merge completed cleanly, so MERGE_HEAD is
-# already gone by the time it runs -- ...
+# git leaves MERGE_HEAD on disk while post-merge runs and deletes it only
+# after the hook returns, so it must not be checked here (#4463). ...
 [ -d "$GIT_DIR/rebase-merge" ] && exit 0
 [ -d "$GIT_DIR/rebase-apply" ] && exit 0
-[ -f "$GIT_DIR/MERGE_HEAD" ] && exit 0
 [ -f "$GIT_DIR/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" ] && exit 0
```

Git only runs post-merge after a successful merge, so the check never protected anything there. The same check in post-commit and post-checkout is unchanged. There it keeps those hooks quiet while a conflicted merge is being resolved.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Every merge that changes the tree triggers one post-merge rebuild. Hooks still stay quiet mid rebase or cherry-pick.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. One line removed from a generated hook script, no schema, cache or file-format change. Existing installs pick it up on the next `graphify hook install`.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Only the post-merge hook changes. After this, every `--no-ff`, diverged or `git pull` merge launches one detached background rebuild, which is what the hook was written to do. Users who merge often will see that rebuild run where it silently didn't before. `GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1` still turns it off.

**Limitations**

- Hooks already installed keep the old guard until the user re-runs `graphify hook install`.
- If an older git deletes MERGE_HEAD before running post-merge, the new test passes there even without the fix. I haven't checked which git versions behave that way.

## How was this tested?

Added `test_post_merge_hook_runs_after_a_real_merge`. It installs the hooks in a temp repo, runs `git merge --no-ff`, and checks that the hook prints the launch line. It fails on v8 and passes with the fix.

```text
.venv/bin/ruff check graphify/hooks.py tests/test_hooks.py                             -> All checks passed
```

I didn't run the full suite. The change is confined to the post-merge hook script.

items.title: fix(skill): drop backticks bash ran inside Part C and the update merge (#4461)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4461.

Four comment lines inside double-quoted `-c "..."` blocks had backticks. Bash expands backticks inside double quotes, so it ran the text before Python started. This PR drops the backticks, keeps the words, and adds a test that fails on any backtick inside such a block.

### Summary

```diff
 # Part C, in core/core.md:317, core/aider.md:378, core/devin.md:442 (15 generated skills)
-# `graphify update` deleted it along with the re-extracted code file it
+# graphify update deleted it along with the re-extracted code file it

 # --update merge block, in references/shared/update.md:110 (all 14 skills/<host>/references/update.md)
-# Do NOT add `changed` here: with root= passed, prune_set relativizes to the same base
+# Do NOT add changed here: with root= passed, prune_set relativizes to the same base
```

The skills run Python as `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "..."`. With `graphify` on PATH, bash ran a full `graphify update` in the middle of Part C and pasted its output into the Python source. The first output line landed in the comment. The next lines were pasted into the code, and Part C failed with `SyntaxError`. `.graphify_extract.json` was never written. Without `graphify` on PATH the only sign was `command not found` on stderr, so nobody noticed.

Two commits:
1. `test(skill): no command runs from backticks in -c "..." blocks`: `tests/test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py`. On its own it fails 58 cases (29 per check).
2. `fix(skill): drop backticks bash ran inside Part C and the update merge (#4461)`: the 4 fragment lines, the regenerated files, and one `gen.py` line.

### Evidence

- **Test before and after:** unfixed v8 58 failed, 105 passed. After the fix 163 passed. The 58 are 29 files per check: 15 monoliths plus 14 `references/update.md`.
- **Real graphify on PATH** (Part C copied verbatim from `graphify/skill.md:377-417`, a project with a previous build and one edited file, venv `graphify` first on PATH):

  ```text
  before (v8 fe085ced)
    exit 1   SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?
             at "[graphify watch] 3 file(s) not classified ..." (graphify's own stdout)
    graph.json rewritten by the unrequested update (sha prefix e4df2084c90f7f07 -> 70d4be72e1eab745)
    .graphify_extract.json: not written

  after (this branch)
    exit 0   stdout: Merged: 1 nodes, 0 edges (1 AST + 0 semantic)   stderr: empty
    graph.json unchanged (sha prefix fa4465c9b74a2269 before and after)
    .graphify_extract.json: written (237 bytes)
  ```
- **Other cases, v8:** a fake `graphify` printing 3 lines gives exit 1 and `SyntaxError`; one printing 1 line works, because the line lands inside the comment; no `graphify` on PATH gives exit 0 with `command not found`. A fake `changed` printing 3 lines in the `--update` merge block gives exit 1 and `SyntaxError`, with `graph.json` and `manifest.json` untouched.
- The `# Save scan root so \`graphify update\` ...` lines in Step 1, `shell/posix.md` and `shell/powershell.md` are plain shell comments outside quotes. Checked: a fake `graphify` was not called.

### Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Comment text only, in four fragment lines. No stored format changes, and reverting is one commit.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Comments inside Python source the skills hand to the interpreter. Nothing in `graphify/*.py` changes.

- **Cache and ids:** no change. The semantic cache key comes from `prompt_fingerprint`, which hashes the file the skill passes as `prompt_file`, `references/extraction-spec.md` (`cache.py`). That file is not in this diff. aider and devin pass no prompt. No node ids, graph format or manifest change.
- **Generated files:** 60, all regenerated with `--bless` and never hand-edited: 16 monoliths and 14 `references/update.md`, plus their 30 `tools/skillgen/expected/` copies. `skill-windows.md` is one of the 16. Its text changes, but it was never affected, because its Part C sits in a single-quoted PowerShell here-string (`@'`).
- **`gen.py`:** one line. `_is_semantic_origin_stamp_fix_line` matched the Part C comment with its backticks, so the round-trip audit would reject the new text. It now matches the text without backticks. The old string is not needed: the pinned v8 baselines for aider and devin hold neither form, and `--monolith-roundtrip` passes.
- **Open PRs, checked with `git merge-tree --write-tree` against each branch's head, then the new test run on the merged tree:**

  | PR | text merge | new test on merged tree |
  |---|---|---|
  | #4313 | clean | 163 passed |
  | #4344 | clean | 163 passed |
  | #4353 | clean | 163 passed |
  | #4371 | clean | 163 passed |
  | #4434 (at 75218d94) | clean | 163 passed |
  | #4452 | clean | 163 passed |
  | #4456 | clean | 163 passed |

  - #4344 and #4353 spell the opener `"$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)" -c "`. The test accepts both spellings, so it runs on their merged trees as well.
  - #4434 added a comment with backticks inside a `-c` block (`core.md:208`). Its branch now drops them too (75218d94), so the new test passes whichever lands first.
  - #4456 can later drop the PATH filtering at `tests/test_code_only_update_all_hosts.py:156-160`, which exists because of this bug. Not changed here.

### Not covered

- The runtime check runs only `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "..."` statements in fenced bash blocks (quoted or not). Other shapes, such as `"$PYTHON" -c "..."`, are not run; the static check still scans them.
- `$VAR` expansion inside the double quotes is not a command, so neither check looks at it.
- The static check looks for backticks only. It does not look for `$(...)` inside the quotes; the runtime check does, through the shell trace, for the statements it runs.
- The windows monolith's Part C is a PowerShell here-string, so the runtime check does not run it. The static check skips `@'...'@` here-strings on purpose. The runtime test skips on win32.
- The test reads the generated files. It does not render them again.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: no command runs while bash expands a skill's double-quoted `-c "..."` block, so the Python source Part C and the update merge hand to the interpreter is exactly what the skill text says.

- `tests/test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py` checks it two ways over `graphify/skill*.md` and `graphify/skills/**` (128 files). Static: no backtick inside any double-quoted `-c` block, with PowerShell `@'...'@` here-strings skipped. Runtime: each `-c "..."` statement of the 29 files that hold Part C or the `--update` merge is run under bash with a stub interpreter, with a fake `graphify` and a fake `changed` first on PATH. The shell is traced, and `PATH` holds only the fakes, `cat` and the stub, so a backtick naming any other command is a trace line the test rejects.
- It has scanner unit tests and two runtime controls, so it cannot pass with nothing in it: a backticked `graphify update` is caught through the fake, and a backticked unknown command is caught through the trace. A guard test fails if the Part C and update files are not found.
- Generated or persisted state this invalidates: none. `--bless` rewrites 30 `expected/` files (the other 104 are content-identical).

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

Run from `/var/tmp` with `PYTHONPATH` set to the worktree and the repo venv's Python, so the code under test is this branch. `graphify.__file__` was checked to be inside the worktree.

```text
python -m pytest tests/test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py -q --basetemp=... -p no:cacheprovider
  unfixed v8 (test file only):  58 failed, 105 passed
  both commits:                 163 passed

python -m tools.skillgen --bless              -> blessed 134 artifact(s) into expected/.
python -m tools.skillgen
python -m tools.skillgen --check              -> check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.
python -m tools.skillgen --monolith-roundtrip -> monolith-roundtrip OK: each monolith matches v8 modulo the enum unification.

python -m pytest tests/test_skillgen.py tests/test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py -q
  96 passed
python -m pytest <the 65 .py test files that mention "skill"> tests/test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py -q
  2363 passed, 3 skipped

python -m pytest -q --basetemp=... -p no:cacheprovider
  8160 passed, 14 skipped, 2043 warnings in 504.73s (0:08:24)

ruff check .
  All checks passed!
pyright tests/test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py tools/skillgen/gen.py
  0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations
```

Not run: `pyright` on the whole repo.

items.title: fix(skill): aider and devin code-only --update reach the merge (#4447)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4447: this fixes the aider and devin skills only. The 14 generated hosts are fixed by #4313, and this PR does not touch that file (`tools/skillgen/fragments/references/shared/update.md`) or any generated `references/update.md`.

**Merge order:** independent of #4313. Either can land first, and they touch different files. #4313 fixes the 14 generated skills, this PR fixes aider and devin. Once both are in, I'll add the 14 skills to this PR's test so all 16 are covered.

### Summary

On a code-only `--update` the aider and devin runbooks said "run only Step 3A, then go straight to merge". Part A writes `.graphify_ast.json`, the merge reads `.graphify_extract.json`, and nothing wrote it. Part C would write it, but it reads `.graphify_semantic.json` unconditionally, and in these two files the Part B fast path is prose only.

```text
aider / devin skill, code-only path

 --update, "If code_only is True"
-  run only Step 3A, go straight to merge
+  Step 3A (AST) -> Part B fast path -> Part C -> merge

 Part B, "Fast path:"
+  block writes an empty .graphify_semantic.json     (Part C reads it unconditionally)

 only-deletions guard (aider only)
-  writes graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json        (the aider merge reads ./.graphify_extract.json)
+  writes .graphify_extract.json

 commit 2 (separate bug)
 --update section
+  block writes .graphify_detect.json from .graphify_incremental.json
   (Part A reads it, Step 9 deletes it, nothing in the section wrote it again)
```

Three commits:
1. `fix(skill): aider and devin code-only runs reach the merge (#4447)`: the paragraph, the fast-path block, aider's guard path, the test, and the `gen.py` audit entry for these lines.
2. `fix(skill): aider and devin --update populate .graphify_detect.json`: a separate bug found while testing. Fixes #4455. Without it Part A fails first after any full build. It can be dropped without affecting commit 1.
3. `test(skill): keep graphify off PATH and satisfy pyright in the update test`: bash runs the backticked text in Part C's comment when `graphify` is on PATH, which broke the test in CI. The test keeps `graphify` off PATH for the blocks it runs, and three Optional values are narrowed for pyright. The test checks the same things.

Plain first-time code-only builds on aider and devin also failed. The full-build text says "skip Part B entirely and go straight to Part C", and Part C then raised `FileNotFoundError` for the semantic file. The fast-path block fixes that when the agent runs it. The literal "skip Part B" sequence without the block still fails. Project with two `.py` files, detect, Part A, Part C:

```text
unfixed (v8 fe085ced)
  aider  [Part C] exit 1  FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.graphify_semantic.json'
  devin  [Part C] exit 1  FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json'

fixed, with the fast-path block between Part A and Part C
  aider  [Part B fast path] exit 0   [Part C] exit 0  Merged: 4 nodes, 2 edges (4 AST + 0 semantic)
  devin  [Part B fast path] exit 0   [Part C] exit 0  Merged: 4 nodes, 2 edges (4 AST + 0 semantic)

fixed, same sequence without the block
  aider / devin  [Part C] exit 1  FileNotFoundError (same message as above)
```

### Evidence

- **Before:** `tests/test_code_only_update_all_hosts.py` on unfixed v8, 2 failed and 7 passed. The reader's unit tests are the 7; devin and aider fail at the merge:
  - devin: `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json'`
  - aider: `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.graphify_extract.json'`

  **After:** 9 passed. The route the test runs is the one the rendered paragraph names, `['A', 'B', 'C', 'merge']`. After the merge, Step 4 also ran on both skills (`Graph: 5 nodes, 3 edges, 2 communities`, `graph.json` labels `a.py, b.py, f(), f_new(), g()`).
- Commit 2 on its own: with the detect block removed the same test fails on both skills with `the --update section never wrote .graphify_detect.json`; with it, 9 passed.

### Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Instruction text, one new block per skill and one new `gen.py` audit entry per commit. No stored format changes. Reverting is one commit each.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Two skills, aider and devin. Nothing in `graphify/*.py` changes.

- **Cache and ids:** the semantic cache key is unchanged. These skills call `check_semantic_cache(all_files)` and `save_semantic_cache(...)` with no prompt argument, so the key does not derive from the skill text. No node ids, graph format or manifest change.
- **Generated files:** besides the two fragments (`core/aider.md`, `core/devin.md`), each commit regenerates `graphify/skill-aider.md`, `graphify/skill-devin.md` and their two `tools/skillgen/expected/` files with `--bless`. The 14 generated hosts are not touched.
- **`gen.py` audit entries:** `--monolith-roundtrip` compares each monolith with a pinned v8 body and only accepts changes a predicate names. Commit 1 adds `_is_code_only_fast_path_fix_line` and commit 2 adds `_is_update_detect_populate_fix_line`, both registered in `_SANCTIONED_MONOLITH_DIFFS`. The first one lets six generic shell lines of the new block pass once each anywhere in the monoliths (a code fence, `` ```bash ``, `import json`, `from pathlib import Path`, `"`, the unquoted `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "` line). Every content line is matched by specific text.
- **Open PRs, checked with `git merge-tree --write-tree`:**
  - #4353 and the #4344 stack conflict with this branch in `tools/skillgen/gen.py`, at the tail of `_SANCTIONED_MONOLITH_DIFFS`. Both sides append entries; keep all of them (this PR's two, plus `_is_labels_json_fix_line` and `_is_scan_root_fix_line`). The fragments and generated skill files auto-merge.
  - Those two PRs change `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "` to the quoted form in the other blocks. Whoever lands second should quote this PR's new interpreter calls too: the fast-path block and the detect block in each of `core/aider.md` and `core/devin.md`, 4 in total.
  - #4313, #4371, #4434 and #4452 have no overlap with the files here, measured from each branch's merge-base.

### Not covered

- The 14 generated hosts. They are #4313's. The test file keeps the shared anchors and the windows handling, unused, with `# shared hosts: add the params back once #4313 lands`.
- aider's `code_exts` lacks `.lua` and `.toc`, which devin has, so a Lua change makes aider's `code_only` False.
- The transcribe block in aider: Step 2 writes `.graphify_detect.json` in the cwd but the video transcribe block reads `graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json`. Only the video path is affected.
- aider keeps its `.graphify_*.json` in the project root, where `detect_incremental` scans them. A leftover `.graphify_semantic.json` from an interrupted run lands under `new_files.code` and flips `code_only` to False.
- A code-only update that also deletes a file: Step 4's shrink guard (#479) refuses the smaller graph. Separate problem, not touched.
- The "plain build" case needs the agent to run the new block. The "skip Part B entirely and go straight to Part C" sentence is unchanged.
- Part C of every skill has backticks inside a double-quoted `python -c` block, for example ``# `graphify update` deleted it ...``. With `graphify` on PATH, bash runs that text and pastes its output into the Python source. This is why the test keeps `graphify` off PATH. Not fixed here: it touches the shared fragments for all hosts.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: when the code-only paragraph of an aider or devin runbook is followed as written, the merge reads a `.graphify_extract.json` that this run's Part C built from the fresh AST, and a stale `.graphify_semantic.json` or the semantic cache cannot reach the result.

- `tests/test_code_only_update_all_hosts.py` renders the skill, reads the code-only paragraph, runs only the blocks it names (Part A, the Part B fast path if named, Part C if named, then the merge), and checks: the merge exits 0; the printed node count is the baseline plus the new function; where the merge writes the extraction, `f_new()` is in it and a seeded stale semantic label is not; the semantic cache files are byte-identical before and after.
- The paragraph is read by a small reader: first mention of each step counts, code spans and clauses with a negation are dropped, and an unmapped step name raises. It has its own unit cases, including #4313's paragraph verbatim and the issue's second route (the merge builds from the AST file).
- The test does not hard-code the route. A paragraph that names too little fails, which is the bug.
- Generated or persisted state this invalidates: none. `--bless` rewrites only the aider and devin entries in `expected/` (the other 132 are content-identical).

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

Run from `/var/tmp` or the worktree with `PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/wt-4447-fix` and the repo venv's Python, so the code under test is this branch. `graphify.__file__` was checked to be inside the worktree.


items.title: fix(extract): keep a symbol that spells a sibling's file id (#4449)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4449.

When a JS file and a file with another extension share a stem in one folder (`x.mjs` plus `x.sql`) and the `.mjs` declares a variable named like the sibling's extension (`const sql = ...`), the `.mjs` file node ends up labelled `sql`. `graphify explain "x.mjs"` finds nothing.

`extract()` renames each file's old file-level id (its path with the extension: `esquema_x_sql` for `esquema/x.sql`) to the canonical one (`esquema_x`). It did that on every node, edge endpoint and raw call that spells the string, whichever file it belonged to. The JS variable `sql` is minted `{stem}_{name}`, which is also `esquema_x_sql`. So it was renamed too, salted next to the file node, and dedup dropped one of the two.

This PR renames a key only for the file that minted it, and only when another file's own symbol carries the same id. Every other key renames exactly as before.

```diff
 extract.py, the id_remap pass          (key esquema_x_sql -> esquema_x, minted by x.sql)

   node   sql           (x.mjs)  id esquema_x_sql
-    renamed to esquema_x         (its file did not mint the key)
+    kept as esquema_x_sql

   edge   contains  x.mjs -> sql        endpoint esquema_x_sql, source_file x.mjs
-    renamed: now x.mjs -> x.mjs, a self-loop
+    kept: still points at the sql variable

   edge   imports_from  x.mjs -> x.sql  endpoint esquema_x_sql, target_file x.sql
     renamed (x.sql minted the key), then salted onto the x.sql file node

   edge   imports  main.pas -> util.pas   (no target_file, main.pas holds no such node)
     renamed, as before
```

A key is contested only when a node of a different file carries it as one of that file's own symbol ids. For a contested key, an item is renamed if its file minted the key, kept if its file holds a node with that id, and renamed otherwise. Which file an item belongs to: a node, its `source_file`; an edge source, the edge's `source_file`; an edge target, the `target_file` stamp if there is one, else the edge's `source_file`; a `raw_calls` `caller_nid`, the record's `source_file`. Paths are compared resolved. Swift extension `nid`s and Objective-C field-table keys follow the same rule.

The later `ext_id_remap` pass already has an ownership guard (`owned_ids`, from #2231 and #2243). The first pass lacked it.

### Before / after

The issue's repro, `graphify extract . --code-only`:

```text
before:  [graphify] note: node 'esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x' was extracted twice from 'esquema/x.mjs'
         under different labels (keeping 'sql', dropping 'x.mjs').
         5 nodes, 4 edges
         esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x | sql          <- should be the file node "x.mjs"
         esquema_x_prueba        | prueba()
         esquema_x_sql_esquema_x | x.sql
         esquema_x_t             | t

after:   no note.   6 nodes, 5 edges
         esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x | x.mjs
         esquema_x_sql           | sql
         esquema_x_prueba        | prueba()
         esquema_x_sql_esquema_x | x.sql
         esquema_x_t             | t
```

Tests, `tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`:

```text
before fix:  8 failed, 6 passed   (the 6 are guards that must not move)
after fix:   14 passed
```

The same cause hit other pairs. Each is a test:

- `x.ts` + `x.css` (`export const css = ...`): `css` took the file node's id, and nothing was salted because `x.css` has no nodes.
- `x.js` + `x.js.map` (`const js_map`): the variable was renamed to the id of `x.js.map`, a node that does not exist.
- `x.py` + `x.sql` (`def sql()`): the function was lost and its `calls` edge started at the file node.
- `x.swift` + `x.sql` with `struct sql` and `extension sql`: without the Swift hunk the fix would delete both file nodes, so the hunk is required, and a test covers it.

### Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. No stored format changes. Reverting is one commit.

**Blast radius:** narrow. The rename changes only for a key that a node of another file also carries as its own symbol id; every other key takes the old path.

- **Ids:** a corpus with no such clash gets the same ids as before. An affected corpus gets its swallowed symbol back under its own id, with its edges. An unchanged affected file keeps its old state in an existing `graph.json` until it is re-extracted.
- **Caches and skills:** the semantic cache key, the AST cache and the generated skill files do not change. `.mjs`, `.js`, `.ts` and similar are never in the AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`).
- **Cost:** one extra pass over `all_nodes` before the rename loop, dictionary lookups and memoized path resolution.
- **Open PRs:** none of #4344, #4353, #4371 touches `graphify/extract.py`.

### Not covered

- The Objective-C hunk has no test that reaches it. I could not build a case where an Objective-C class node holds a contested id. It runs only when some key is contested (`if contested:`), and the 5 existing objc tests pass with it.
- Unstamped cross-file imports to a same-stem file (for example Pascal `uses util` next to `util.js`) already end on a node that does not exist after salting, with or without this bug. A contested key now behaves like an uncontested one there. That dangling edge is not repaired.
- A symbol named like its own file's extension (`const js` in `x.js`, `def py()` in `z.py`) is lost. The same file owns the key, so this rename fix does not touch it. It needs its own issue.
- Stub nodes: I scanned graphify's own repo and its test fixtures for a node whose file did not mint the key. The one hit is `sample` in `tests/fixtures/sample.lpk`, a Lazarus unit reference minted with `sample.pas`'s old id. Before this fix it collided with the lpk's own file node; now it keeps its own id and its edge follows. Other languages and extractors were not scanned.
- Through `graphify extract .`, only siblings of a supported type (such as `.sql`) trigger the bug. `collect_files` skips `.css` and `.map`, so those two pairs need an explicit `extract([...])` call.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a symbol is never renamed because of a file it does not belong to, and everything that refers to a file node still ends on that file node.

- The issue repro runs with relative and absolute paths: three distinct ids for the file node, the variable and the `x.sql` file node.
- After `build()`, the labels `x.mjs`, `sql` and `x.sql` all exist.
- With `import raw from "./x.sql"` in `x.mjs`: `imports_from` ends on the `x.sql` file node, `contains` and `calls` end on the variable, and there is no self-loop.
- An unstamped Pascal import on a contested key ends exactly where the same edge ends with no clashing variable.
- Controls from the issue (`const db`, `const sql = 1`, no sibling, a sibling with another stem), and a Lazarus stub from a different stem, keep their ids.
- Gating only the node rename, and leaving edge endpoints on the old id-only rule, was tried and does not work: it leaves a `contains x.mjs -> x.mjs` self-loop and a `calls` edge that starts at the file node.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

Run with `PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/wt-4449` and the repo venv's Python, so the code under test is this branch and not an editable install of another checkout. `graphify.__file__` was checked to be inside the worktree.

```text

  before: 5 nodes, 4 edges, "extracted twice ... keeping 'sql', dropping 'x.mjs'"
  after:  6 nodes, 5 edges, no note

python -m pytest tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt-4449 -p no:cacheprovider
  before fix: 8 failed, 6 passed, 12 warnings in 1.61s
  after fix:  14 passed, 12 warnings in 2.31s

python -m pytest tests/test_swift_cross_file_calls.py tests/test_objc_field_table_remap.py -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt-4449b -p no:cacheprovider
  22 passed, 21 warnings in 1.55s

python -m pytest <the 18 covering files> -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt-4449c -p no:cacheprovider
  1183 passed, 295 warnings in 38.41s
  (test_extract, test_incremental, test_js_import_resolution, test_node_id_canonical,
   test_file_node_id_spec, test_astro_import_ids, test_extract_path_memo,
   test_cross_extension_reexport_self_cycle, test_id_normalization_contract,
   test_objc_field_table_remap, test_dotnet, test_languages, test_incomplete_build_guard,
   test_extraction_spec_ids, test_jsconfig_baseurl, test_package_json_subpath_imports,
   test_cjs_module_extension, test_typescript_module_extensions)

python -m pytest -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt-4449-full -p no:cacheprovider
  8011 passed, 14 skipped, 2055 warnings in 541.55s (0:09:01)

ruff check graphify/extract.py tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py
  All checks passed!
pyright graphify/extract.py
  131 errors, same as upstream/v8 (041771be); tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py: 0
```

items.title: fix(extract): give the model each file's real id stem (#4432)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4432. #3103 reported the same thing and was closed without a fix.

The extraction prompts say node ids use "only `[a-z0-9_]`". `graphify/ids.py` keeps Unicode letters. For a path like `docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md` the model cannot follow both, so it invents a stem, and the stem differs between chunks and between runs. `_semantic_id_remap` only strips stems it already knows, so none of them get fixed.

This PR states the real rule and gives the model each file's stem, computed in code.

```diff
 graphify extract (llm.py)
-  <untrusted_source path="docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md" sha256="...">
+  <untrusted_source path="docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md" sha256="..." stem="docs_tz_лз4">

 skill, Part B
   check_semantic_cache(...)
     writes .graphify_uncached.txt              # unchanged
+    writes .graphify_uncached_stems.txt        # path<TAB>stem, same order
   Step B1: FILE_LIST lines
-    /abs/docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md
+    /abs/docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md<TAB>docs_tz_лз4       # falls back to the old file if missing

 rule text (llm.py + both extraction-spec fragments)
-  Node ID format: lowercase, only [a-z0-9_], no dots or slashes.
+  Node ID format: lowercase. Letters and digits of any script are kept as written
+  (never transliterated to ASCII); every run of any other character becomes one _.
+  ...use the given stem character for character as the id prefix.
```

Both paths use one new helper, `file_id_stem(path, root)` in `graphify/extractors/base.py`. It returns `make_id(_file_stem(...))` of the root-relative path. The skill computes the stems in the same Python step that already runs the cache check. No path is pasted into code, and no agent types a stem.

I left `_semantic_id_remap` alone. A made-up stem has no known length, so a repair can't tell where the stem ends and the entity begins. The #4281 prototype also showed that re-keying a node from its `source_file` moves a node that mentions another file under the wrong file.

### Before / after

Same id, two different stems:

```text
before:  ids.py stem      docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог
         model's stem     docs_tz_lz4_obosnovanie_kdog            (from the issue; changes per run)
         remap            {}                                      (nothing reconciled)

after:   prompt carries   stem="docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог"
         page node id     docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог   (same string, tested)
```

Read literally, the old rule turns that path into `docs_tz_4_`. That result comes from running the rule as code, not from a model run.

Tests, `tests/test_unicode_id_rule.py`:

```text
before fix:  43 failed, 2 passed   (the 2 are the host-count guards)
after fix:   45 passed
```

### Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. No stored format changes. The only new file is a temp file that Part B cleans up, and reverting means one commit.

**Blast radius:** medium. Every semantic extraction prompt changes:

- **Cache:** the semantic cache is keyed on the prompt text, so every existing entry misses once. This hits `graphify extract` users and all 14 skill hosts, including ASCII-only repos. Reverting causes one more miss.
- **ASCII paths:** the chunk prompt is byte-identical apart from the added `stem="..."` (tested). File-node ids do not change for any path.
- **Skill hosts:** 14 hosts get the regenerated skill and spec. Aider and devin are not touched. They never stated the `[a-z0-9_]` rule.
- **#4344:** one-line conflict. Both PRs touch the same `check_semantic_cache` line in `core.md`. Whichever merges second changes `root = 'INPUT_PATH'` to `root = read_scan_root()`.

### Not covered

- Nothing enforces the id. The model can still ignore the stem it is given, and then ids drift as before. Enforcing it means having code mint the ids, which is a larger change.
- Nodes with no file stem at all (`concept_*`, `s301_totals` in the issue).
- On the skill path, a symlinked doc whose target is outside the scan root gets no stem and falls back to the rule text.
- The aider and devin monolith skills.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: the stem the model is told to use is the same string the document pass mints for that file's node, whatever script the path is in.

- `test_file_id_stem_is_the_prefix_the_pipeline_mints` runs a Cyrillic and an ASCII document through the real `extract()`. The page-node id equals `file_id_stem`, the chunk prompt carries that stem, and `_semantic_id_remap` leaves a node under it alone.
- `file_id_stem` is tested with an absolute path and root `"."`, with a path outside the root (returns `""`), and with `"`, `<` and `>` in the name. The stem holds only letters, digits and `_`, so it cannot break out of the attribute.
- The Part B step is extracted from the generated `graphify/skill.md` and run. It writes the expected `path<TAB>stem` lines, with `INPUT_PATH` substituted once.
- The rule wording is checked in `llm.py` and in all 14 generated specs, with exact host counts so a dropped host fails the test.
- Generated state this invalidates: the semantic cache (once), plus 14 skill files and 14 specs, which are regenerated with `--bless`.

```text
python repro.py

  before: 43 failed, 2 passed
```

items.title: fix(dedup): keep a dropped-folder doc next to a top-level same-id file (#4281)

labels.name: contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4281. Closes the gap named in the review of #4371: "a bare id that names an actual input file, e.g. a top-level protocol.md next to docs/protocol.md". Stacks cleanly with #4371 in either order.

When the LLM drops the folder, `protocol.md`, `docs/protocol.md` and `docs/firmware/protocol.md` all mint `protocol`. #4362 skips any group whose bare id names an input file, because the id may be a reference to that file. So the collapse ran and one real document was dropped:

```diff
 nodes after build
   docs_protocol            docs/protocol.md
   docs_firmware_protocol   docs/firmware/protocol.md
+  protocol                 protocol.md        (v8: dropped)

 edges
-  docs_firmware_protocol -> docs_protocol
+  docs_firmware_protocol -> protocol
```

The id alone can't tell "my own page with the folder dropped" from "a reference to protocol.md". The rest of the file can: a file that only refers to protocol.md still has its own page node.

```text
for each id shared across files:
  the file whose full stem IS the id (protocol.md) keeps it and counts toward the group
  for each other file with that bare id:
    if the file has no other node spelled with its own full stem:
      the bare id is its page: rename to <full stem> + rest of id
    else:
      it may be a reference: leave it to the collapse, as before

survivor ranking:
  a bare path slice from a file that has its own page ranks as a reference,
  so protocol.md's node survives whatever the labels are
```

```diff
 deduplicate_entities
   _path_qualify_dropped_collisions
+    _own_page_files                         # file has a node spelled with its own full stem
-    skip the group if the bare id names an input file
+    decide per file: no own page -> rename, own page -> collapse
   exact-id collapse
-    mentions = _mentions(...)
+    mentions = _mentions(...) | _slice_references(...)
     _collision_rank(node, root, mentions)
```

### Existing tests this PR changes

| Test | Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_top_level_collision_keeps_todays_result` | 2 nodes; its docstring says "KNOWN LIMITATION, pinned so a change is noticed" | renamed `test_top_level_file_keeps_its_own_node_next_to_dropped_folder_docs`; 3 nodes, the firmware reference ends on `protocol` | this is the fixed case |
| `test_bare_id_naming_an_existing_file_is_not_renamed` | three files, each with a single `protocol`, collapse to 1 node | renamed `test_bare_ids_in_three_files_keep_one_node_per_file`; 3 nodes, no collision warning | none of the three files has another page, so each bare id is that file's page. The collapse was the data loss |

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

One node per real document. A reference must not become a new document, and a real document must not be dropped. The result does not depend on input order or label length.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Code only: no schema, cache or file-format change.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. It changes only groups where an input file is named by the bare id, and survivor choice only for a bare path slice from a file that has its own page. On a rebuild, such a corpus gets one more document node, and a saved query for `protocol` finds the top-level file.

**Limitations**

- If the LLM drops the folder AND emits another node spelled with the file's full stem (`docs_protocol_header`), the file counts as having its own page and gets the collapse it got before. `test_dropped_folder_doc_with_own_stem_entity_falls_back_to_collapse` pins this.
- In R_toplevel one warning still prints: the firmware file's mention of `protocol` collapses into the top-level node. That merge is right, the warning is noise.
- The own-page check reads the nodes the LLM emitted, not the source file.

items.title: fix(dedup): say what an id-collision merge actually drops (#4281)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4281. Fixes the misleading warning the reporter hit.

When two files mint one id, dedup keeps one node and merges the other into it. The warning claimed that "the dropped node is lost" and that the id "does not identify a single entity", for every such collision. On the reporter's corpus that was wrong: none of their 16 remaining warnings was a lost document. They were one entity described in two documents, or a reference to another file, and merging them was correct. This PR rewords the warning to say what the merge did. It does not change which node survives.

```text
_report_id_collision(nid, survivor, loser)        # cross-file branch only
  survivor defines the id, loser does not  -> silent          (unchanged)
  head = "kept <survivor> from <file>, merged <loser> from <file> into it"
  if _defines_id(survivor) or _defines_id(loser)
    "the id comes from a file path: either a reference to the kept file (merge is right)
     or a separate document (its own label and attributes are lost; edges stay)
     -> advise 'graphify extract' per subfolder"
  else
    "the id comes from neither path: probably one entity described in both files"
```

Edges stay on the kept node because both nodes have the same id. What is dropped is the merged node's own label and attributes.

Real stderr, before and after (both from `deduplicate_entities`):

`protocol` in `docs/protocol.md` and `docs/firmware/protocol.md`

```diff
-[graphify] WARNING: node 'protocol' is minted by two different files — keeping 'Protocol' from 'docs/protocol.md', dropping 'protocol (top-level)' from 'docs/firmware/protocol.md'. An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost. To keep them distinct, run 'graphify extract' per subfolder and merge with 'graphify merge-graphs'.
+[graphify] WARNING: node 'protocol' is minted by two different files: kept 'Protocol' from 'docs/protocol.md', merged 'protocol (top-level)' from 'docs/firmware/protocol.md' into it. The id comes from a file path, so the merged node is either a reference to the kept file (then the merge is right) or a separate document (then its own label and attributes are lost; its edges stay on the kept node). To keep separate documents apart, run 'graphify extract' per subfolder and merge with 'graphify merge-graphs'.
```

`sender` in `docs/a.md` and `docs/b.md`

```diff
-[graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files — keeping 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', dropping 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md'. An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost. To keep them distinct, run 'graphify extract' per subfolder and merge with 'graphify merge-graphs'.
+[graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files: kept 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', merged 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md' into it. The id comes from neither path, so this is probably one entity described in both files. The merged node's own label and attributes are not kept; its edges stay on the kept node.
```

Severity is unchanged. `WARNING` and the phrase "minted by two different files" are kept, so `test_issue_3472_source_file_collision.py` and the #1504 test pass without edits.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The warning must not claim more than the merge did. After a collision, one node is kept, the other node's own label and attributes are dropped, and its edges stay on the kept node. Survivor choice is unchanged: it still comes from `_collision_rank`, and the order of the input still does not matter (#1851).

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. The change is stderr text plus a docstring. No persisted state, cache or graph.json field is touched.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Only the text of the cross-file collision warning changes. Anything that greps stderr for the old words ("is lost", "does not identify a single entity", "dropping") will no longer match. In this repo only `dedup.py` contained them; the CHANGELOG line for #1504 describes the older warning and is left as it is.

**Limitations**

- The text cannot tell a reference from a second document when the id comes from a path. It says both are possible. Telling them apart needs edge evidence and is out of scope here (it is the separate fix for the path-qualified id case in #4281).
- "Probably one entity" for an id that comes from neither path is an inference, not a fact. Two real documents can also share such an id; the merged node's label and attributes are then lost.
- Severity stays `WARNING`. The reporter asked for something milder, but `test_issue_3472` asserts `WARNING` for a non-path id, so lowering it would change an existing test.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_dedup.py`:

| Test | Before the fix | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_collision_warning_for_path_slice_id_is_conditional` (`protocol`) | fails | passes |
| `test_collision_warning_for_non_path_id_says_what_is_kept` (`sender`) | fails | passes |
| `test_collision_warning_wording_keeps_the_same_survivor` | passes | passes |
| `test_collision_warning_for_path_derived_id_that_is_not_a_slice` (`x_intro` from `a/x.md` and `b/x.md`) | fails | passes |

The third test pins that the survivor is the same in both input orders; it is a guard, so it is expected to pass before the fix.

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_dedup.py -q -k collision_warning   -> before the fix: 3 failed, 1 passed
uv run pytest tests -q                                       -> 7581 passed, 14 skipped
uv run ruff check .                                          -> All checks passed
uv run pyright                                               -> 626 errors repo-wide, 626 before this change
                                                                dedup.py + test_dedup.py: 5 before, 5 after
git checkout uv.lock                                         (uv run rewrites it)
```

pyright is not clean on this repo. This PR adds no errors: the repo-wide and touched-file counts are unchanged.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no skill fragments touched.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). (Wording only; the survivor test runs both input orders.)
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python). (Labels and paths are interpolated into a stderr message only, as before.)
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

items.title: fix(dedup): path-qualify semantic ids that dropped the directory (#4281)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

labels.name: needs:title
labels.description: PR title should follow the conventional-commit format

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4281. Builds on #4371 (warning wording).

Semantic extraction sometimes drops the folder from an id, so `a/x.md` and `b/x.md` both emit `x`. Dedup then merged them and one real document was lost. This PR gives each file its own path-qualified id (`a_x`, `b_x`), unless the bare id is only a mention of another document.

Three different things produce the same collision:

| Shape | Example | Right result |
|---|---|---|
| two real documents | `a/x.md` and `b/x.md` each emit their own `x` | two nodes, `a_x` and `b_x` |
| a mention of another document | `docs/firmware/protocol.md` emits `protocol` and points at it | one node: the reference ends on `docs/protocol.md` |
| one entity described in two documents | `sender` in `docs/a.md` and `docs/b.md` | one node, both documents point at it |

The id alone can't tell these apart: in all three, two files emit one id. What differs is the graph around it. A mention is a path-slice id that another node of its own file points at. In the entity case the id is not a path slice, and for two real documents the id is a slice but nothing in the file points at it.

### The rule

```text
for each id shared by files with different full path stems:
  candidates = nodes whose id is a SHORTER path slice of their own file
               (not AST-tier, not an absolute source_file)
  drop from candidates every MENTION:
      the node is the target of a `references` edge from another node of its own file
      AND its id is itself a path slice of that file          # names a document
  if 2+ files remain, and no remaining file's full stem equals the id:
      rename each node to <full stem of its own file> + rest of id
      edges and hyperedges follow by their own source_file
      references from OTHER files stay on the bare id, with one warning per id
```

The same mention evidence also makes a mention lose survivor ties in `_collision_rank`, so a real document outranks it whatever the label lengths are.

```diff
 deduplicate_entities
   _disambiguate_defining_collisions        # x.py vs x.html (#4282)
+  _path_qualify_dropped_collisions         # a/x.md vs b/x.md
+    _mentions                              # own-file `references` + path-slice id
   exact-id collapse
+    _mentions
     _collision_rank(node, root, mentions)  # a mention ranks as a reference
```

The path-slice gate matters. Ordinary entity ids such as `x_intro` are also the target of intra-file `references` edges. Without the gate, `x_intro` would be skipped from the rename and two real documents would collapse, and the ranking would change survivors for unrelated collisions. `test_reference_evidence_does_not_change_survivors_of_other_collisions` pins this: v8 and this PR keep `a/x.md`'s `x_intro`; an ungated version flips to `c.md`'s.

### Cases

Seven hand-built semantic fragments, run through `graphify.build.build()` on v8, on the first version of this PR (f8c2451), and now.

| case | correct | v8 | PR before (f8c2451) | PR now | covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D: two real docs | 4 nodes, edges within each file | `b/x.md` dropped | ok | ok | `test_path_dropped_through_build` |
| R: mention of another doc | 2 nodes, firmware doc references `docs/protocol.md` | ok, because the mention's label is shorter | self-link: `docs_firmware_protocol` references itself | ok | `test_reference_to_another_file_does_not_become_a_second_document` |
| R_noedge: same, no edge | same 2 nodes, no edge | ok | ok | ok | `test_mention_without_an_edge_gives_the_same_two_documents` |
| R_toplevel: plus a top-level `protocol.md` | 3 nodes, one per file | top-level document dropped | same | same (known) | `test_top_level_collision_keeps_todays_result` |
| F: reference from a third file | no `x`; `c.md`'s edge not pinned on one file | `c_note` pinned on `a_x` as EXTRACTED, `b/x.md` dropped | ok | ok | `test_path_dropped_foreign_reference_edge_is_dropped_by_build` |
| R_labelswap: R with the labels swapped | same as R | `docs/protocol.md` dropped, self-link | self-link | ok | `test_reference_outcome_does_not_depend_on_label_length` |
| G: one entity in two docs | 3 nodes, `sender` once | ok | ok | ok | `test_entity_described_in_two_documents_collapses_to_one_node` |

Totals: v8 3 of 7 right, first version 4 of 7, now 6 of 7. False facts (a self-link, or an extra node): 1, 2, 0. EXTRACTED edges on the wrong node: 2, 2, 0.

### Existing tests this PR changes

The collapse for these inputs was pinned in #1504 and #4282. This PR reverses it for path-dropped ids, because the maintainer's comment on #4281 says the remaining `a/x.md` vs `b/x.md` case "still needs a path-qualified id".

| Test | Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_cross_chunk_id_collision_emits_warning` (#1504) | id `readme_booking_service` on `module-a/README.md` and `module-b/README.md` | id `booking_service` on both | The old id is a path slice of both files, so it is now renamed. `booking_service` is not, so the collapse and the warning are still covered. Assertions are unchanged. |
| `test_bare_id_across_different_paths_still_collapses_with_warning` | asserted one node and a WARNING | renamed `test_bare_id_across_different_paths_is_path_qualified`; asserts `docs_protocol` and `docs_firmware_protocol`, and no `minted by two different files` | With no `references` edge there is no evidence that either copy is a mention, so both files are renamed. The docstring points to the case where the edge exists (R), which stays one node. |

All other existing `test_path_dropped_*` tests are unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

One id per real entity. A reference must not become a new entity, and a real document must not be dropped. Renames depend only on the input: groups, members and warnings are visited in sorted order, and nothing reads the hash seed or the input order.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Code only: no schema, cache or file-format change. Reverting restores the old collapse for newly extracted bare ids.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. It applies only to semantic nodes whose id is a shorter path slice shared across files. On a rebuild, a corpus with such collisions gets more nodes than before (two documents instead of one), and saved queries or notes that use the bare `x` find `a_x` and `b_x` instead. #4371 is independent: the two PRs merge in either order without conflicts (`git merge-tree`).

**Limitations**

- The mention evidence is inferred from the edges an LLM chose to emit. A missing or reversed `references` edge gives no evidence, so both files are renamed (R_noedge). With a reversed edge, the reference can still end up as a self-link.
- A real document whose own node is linked to its file-level id the same way (an entity named like its file) reads as a mention, and that collision collapses as on v8.
- R_toplevel stays wrong: with a top-level `protocol.md` that also mints `protocol`, one real document is still dropped by the label tiebreak. It is a separate collision, and a test pins today's result.
- If two or more other files also mint the mention's id, the mention stays on the bare id and `build_from_json` folds it into its own file's page, which gives a self-link and no warning. This is the same outcome as the first version of this PR.
- A reference to the bare id from a third file (`c.md -> x`) cannot be attributed to one file. The edge is left on `x`, one warning is printed per id, and `build()` then drops it because no node `x` exists.
- For `imports`, `imports_from` and `re_exports` edges, `build_from_json` mints an external stub node for the missing target. An import-family edge to a renamed bare id leaves a phantom external node `x`. Checked by hand; there is no test.
- Absolute `source_file` values (no root, outside the root, or a Windows path on POSIX) are never qualified, so checkout paths cannot leak into ids (#502, #2197, #2618). Those collisions stay on collapse-and-warn.
- AST-tier nodes are not touched. Hyperedge members given as dicts are not rewritten, as in the #4282 pass.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_dedup.py`: the five cases R, R_labelswap, R_noedge, R_toplevel and G from the table, plus `test_reference_evidence_does_not_change_survivors_of_other_collisions` (the survivor gate). The first version of this PR already added tests for keeping both files, order independence, foreign references, absolute paths, a lone id, the build path, a rebuild, and a bare id that names an existing file. On the rebased branch before the final change, R and R_labelswap fail and the rest pass. With an ungated version of the evidence, only the survivor-gate test fails.

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_dedup.py -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pytest-4281   -> 130 passed
uv run pytest tests -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pytest-4281                 -> 7594 passed, 14 skipped
uv run ruff check .                                                    -> All checks passed
uv run pyright                                                         -> 626 errors repo-wide, 626 on upstream/v8
                                                                          dedup.py + test_dedup.py: 5 before, 5 after
.venv/bin/graphify update .                                            -> graph updated
git checkout uv.lock                                                   (uv run rewrites it)
```

pyright is not clean on this repo. Both counts are the same as on `upstream/v8`, measured the same way.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no skill fragments touched.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

items.title: fix: Step 1 fails loudly instead of leaving empty marker files; readers keep .graphify_root exactly (#4346)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
**Stacked on #4344. Please review that one first.** The first 8 commits here belong to #4344. This PR adds the last 4.

With both applied, Step 1 does two things: it refuses a scan path with a line break (#4344), and it fails loudly when a write fails (this PR). `read_scan_root()` from #4344 now calls `read_root_marker()` from this PR, so one function decides how the marker is read.

> **In short:** on a full disk, Step 1 left `.graphify_python` and `.graphify_root` empty and still exited 0, and six readers trimmed spaces off the saved folder (`proj ` became a sibling `proj`). Now Step 1 writes safely and fails loudly, and every reader keeps the folder name exactly. Fixes #4346.
>
> **To review:** about 180 hand-written lines in 11 files (list below). The other 32 changed files are regenerated by `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`, and `--check` confirms they match the sources.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4346.

Step 1 of the `/graphify` skill saves two files that every later step reads: `.graphify_python` (which Python to run) and `.graphify_root` (which folder to scan).

**1. Step 1 said "done" even when it couldn't save them.** On a full disk it left both files empty and exited 0. The next step failed with `bash: : command not found`, and `graphify update` rebuilt the current folder instead of the project. Now Step 1:

```text
deletes last run's files
writes each file to a temp file, then renames it into place
on any error: cleans up, says which file, exits 1
```

So after Step 1, both files are complete and from this run, or Step 1 failed and said so. The Windows Step 1 does the same.

**2. Six readers used `.strip()` on the saved folder.** A folder named `proj ` (legal on Linux and macOS) came back as `proj`. A new `read_root_marker()` removes only a byte-order mark (#3028) and a final newline, and every reader uses it: `graphify update`, `build.py`, `watch.py`, `reflect.py` and the two git hooks. `graphify update` now also stops on an empty `.graphify_root` instead of guessing.

### How to review

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `tools/skillgen/fragments/shell/posix.md` | Step 1 writes both files in one Python call (35 lines) |
| `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md`, `core/devin.md` | the same Step 1 block, copied |
| `tools/skillgen/fragments/shell/powershell.md` | the Windows Step 1 (23 lines) |
| `graphify/paths.py` | new `read_root_marker()` (11 lines) |
| `graphify/cli.py`, `build.py`, `watch.py`, `reflect.py`, `hooks.py` | each reader switches to it (1–15 lines each) |
| `tools/skillgen/gen.py` | the exact list of changed lines the monolith check allows |
| `tests/test_graphify_root_marker.py`, `tests/test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py` | the tests |

Skip `graphify/skill*.md`, `graphify/skills/**` and `tools/skillgen/expected/**`. They're generated.

### Evidence: before and after

Step 1 with `ulimit -f 0`, so every write fails the way it does on a full disk:

```text
v8:           Step 1 exit code 0, .graphify_python and .graphify_root left empty
this branch:  "could not write graphify-out/.graphify_python (File too large; is the disk full?)",
              exit code 1, no files left behind
```

`graphify update` with the saved folder `proj ` and a sibling `proj`:

```text
v8:           rebuilds proj (the wrong folder)
this branch:  rebuilds proj  (the saved folder)
```

<details>
<summary>Reproduce bug 1</summary>

From a checkout of `v8`:

```bash
python3 - > /tmp/step1.sh <<'EOF'
import re
text = open("graphify/skill.md").read()
print(next(b for b in re.findall(r"```bash\n(.*?)\n```", text, re.S) if "graphify_root" in b))
EOF
mkdir -p "/tmp/s1/my project" && cd /tmp/s1
sed -e "s|^INPUT_PATH\$|/tmp/s1/my project|" \
    -e "s|^mkdir -p graphify-out\$|mkdir -p graphify-out\ntrap '' XFSZ; ulimit -f 0|" /tmp/step1.sh | bash
echo "exit: $?"; wc -c graphify-out/.graphify_*      # exit 0, two empty files
```

</details>

### Commits

```text
d8baf79  tests for both bugs
96aa478  Step 1 saves its files safely and fails loudly (bash, aider, devin, Windows)
2d3e236  graphify update, build.py and the hooks read the folder exactly
378d4b2  watch.py and reflect.py too, plus a test that catches any new .strip() reader
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**The rule:** if `.graphify_python` or `.graphify_root` exists and isn't empty, it holds what this run of Step 1 found, and every reader gets that exact value.

**Enforced by:**

- **Step 1 failing a write:** all three bash copies run under `ulimit -f 0` with old files present. Each must exit non-zero, name the file and leave nothing behind. The Windows Step 1 gets the same test under `pwsh`, with a directory blocking its temp file (`ulimit` stops pwsh itself from starting on CI). That test skips where `pwsh` isn't installed.
- **Readers:** `proj ` and `proj` stay apart in `read_root_marker()`, `build.py`, the hooks and `graphify update`. A guard test fails if any module reads a file as `utf-8-sig` and then calls `.strip()`.

All of these fail on `v8` and pass on this branch.

**What changes for existing setups:**

- Installed git hooks keep the old code until `graphify hook install` is run again.
- `graphify update` with an **empty** `.graphify_root` now exits 1. A **missing** one still falls back to the current folder.

**Limitations:** not tested on Windows PowerShell 5.1. The Windows Step 1 ran under PowerShell 7.4.6 on Linux.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

Linux, Python 3.13, rebased on v8 fe085ced (0.9.90), on top of #4344. No pwsh on this run.

```text
uv run pytest tests/                              # 8205 passed, 71 skipped, 0 failed
uv run ruff check .                               # no issues
uv run pyright                                    # 640 errors, same as v8: none added
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check           # 134 files match
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --monolith-roundtrip, --audit-coverage,
  --schema-singleton, --always-on-roundtrip       # all OK
```

The Step 1, reader and skillgen tests also passed on Python 3.10 and 3.13.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. A revert restores the old Step 1 and readers. The files keep the same format, so nothing is migrated.

**Blast Radius:** every skill's Step 1, plus six small reader changes. Extraction and the graph format are untouched.

- A full disk now stops Step 1 with a clear message instead of a confusing error one step later.
- This PR and #4344 both touch `graphify/paths.py` and `tools/skillgen/gen.py`. I'll rebase whichever lands second.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments.
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). This PR doesn't touch extraction code.
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

AI disclosure: I made these changes with Claude Code (Claude Sonnet and Claude Opus 5.5). Claude Code ran the tests and commands listed above in my local checkout, and I reviewed every change and the results.

items.title: fix(skill): stop pasting agent-supplied values into skill scripts (#4309)
items.body:
> **In short:** the skill told the agent to paste the scan folder, community names and spec path into `python -c "..."` scripts, so a folder named `proj$(touch X)` ran `touch X`. Now the agent writes each value to a file in `graphify-out/` and the script reads the file. Fixes #4309.
>
> **To review:** about 340 hand-written lines in 11 files (list below). The other 172 changed files are regenerated by `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`, and `--check` confirms they match the sources.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4309.

The skill told the agent to paste three values into the Python scripts it runs:

- `INPUT_PATH`, the folder to scan
- `LABELS_DICT`, the community names
- `SPEC_PATH`, the path to the extraction spec

A pasted value becomes code. A folder named `proj$(touch PWNED)` runs `touch PWNED` before Python starts, and a label like `x'}; ...; #` ends the Python string early.

Now the agent writes each value to a file through a quoted heredoc (the shell copies it as plain text), and the script reads the file:

```diff
 Step 1        + save the scan folder to graphify-out/.graphify_root
 later steps   - detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'))
               + detect(read_scan_root())
 Step B0/B3    - prompt_file='SPEC_PATH'
               + prompt_file=<read from graphify-out/.graphify_spec_path>
 Step 5        - labels = LABELS_DICT
               + labels = json.loads(<graphify-out/.graphify_labels_in.json>)
```

It also quotes the interpreter path, `"$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)"`, so an interpreter under `/Users/First Last/` no longer splits in two.

### How to review

Read these, in this order:

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md` | the skill steps: read the saved files instead of pasting |
| `tools/skillgen/fragments/references/shared/update.md`, `references/query/default.md`, and three small `references/shared/*.md` | the same change in the reference pages |
| `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md`, `core/devin.md` | the same changes in the two single-file skills |
| `graphify/paths.py` | new `read_scan_root()` (20 lines) |
| `tools/skillgen/gen.py` | the Windows translator learns the spec-path heredoc; the monolith check ignores the added interpreter quotes |
| `tests/test_skillgen_no_pasted_placeholders.py` | the new test that fails if any script pastes a value again |

Skip `graphify/skill*.md`, `graphify/skills/**` and `tools/skillgen/expected/**`. They're generated.

### Evidence: before and after

The real Step 2 script from `graphify/skill.md`, run on a folder named `proj$(touch PWNED)`:

```text
v8:           PWNED file created, then "could not scan .../proj", Detected 0 files
this branch:  nothing created, Detected 1 files
```

On `v8` the folder name runs as a command **and** the wrong folder gets scanned.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce it</summary>

From a checkout, with graphify installed in `.venv`:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/demo/'proj$(touch PWNED)' /tmp/demo/graphify-out && cd /tmp/demo
echo '# notes' > 'proj$(touch PWNED)/notes.md'
echo "$OLDPWD/.venv/bin/python" > graphify-out/.graphify_python
git -C "$OLDPWD" show upstream/v8:graphify/skill.md \
  | python3 -c "import re,sys; t=sys.stdin.read(); print(next(b for b in re.findall(r'\`\`\`bash\n(.*?)\n\`\`\`', t, re.S) if 'graphify_detect.json' in b))" \
  | sed "s|INPUT_PATH|$PWD/proj\$(touch PWNED)|" | bash
ls    # PWNED is here
```

</details>

### Commits

```text

5f0b6da  read_scan_root() reads the folder Step 1 saved
2b1ef8f  Step 5 reads the community names from a JSON file

```

## Verification & Invariants

**The rule:** a value the agent supplies never becomes part of a script. Scripts read it from a file in `graphify-out/`.

**Enforced by** `tests/test_skillgen_no_pasted_placeholders.py`: it renders every skill and fails if a script contains `INPUT_PATH`, `LABELS_DICT` or `SPEC_PATH`, or runs the interpreter unquoted. It fails on the test commit alone (`7e36f0c`) and passes on the branch. Two more tests run the real heredocs with hostile input (``x $(touch PWNED) `touch PWNED2` $HOME``) and check that nothing runs.

**Limitations:**

- Not tested on Windows PowerShell 5.1. The Windows blocks ran under PowerShell 7.4.6 on Linux.
- Step 1 leaving empty files on a full disk is a separate bug, #4346, fixed in #4353.

Linux, Python 3.13, rebased on v8 fe085ced (0.9.90).
