```text
uv run ruff check .                               # no issues
uv run pyright                                    # 640 errors, same as v8: none added
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check           # 134 files match
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --monolith-roundtrip, --audit-coverage,
  --schema-singleton, --always-on-roundtrip       # all OK
```

Rebased on v8 fe085ced. One new commit: v8 added tests/test_query_fallback_edges.py, which found the query fallback by the unquoted opener. This branch quotes the interpreter path, so the test now matches on -c " and the import lines after it.

The changed test files also passed on Python 3.10 and 3.13. The Windows blocks from `skill-windows.md` ran under PowerShell 7.4.6, and the semantic cache still hits on a second run.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. A revert restores the old skill text. No data is migrated.

**Blast Radius:** every skill. The library gains only `read_scan_root()`.

- A step run by hand without Step 1 now stops with `graphify-out/.graphify_root not found; run Step 1 first`.
- `graphify-out/` gets two small new files: `.graphify_spec_path` and `.graphify_labels_in.json`.
- This PR and #4353 both touch `graphify/paths.py` and `tools/skillgen/gen.py`. I'll rebase whichever lands second.

One new commit, `fix(skill): refuse a scan path with a line break in Step 1`, answers the comment on #4309. A path line could end the heredoc early (or the here-string on PowerShell), and anything after it would run as shell. The agent is now told to refuse such a path, and the Python side rejects input of more than one line.

The agent instruction is the real guard. The shell ends the heredoc before Python runs, so the Python check only catches multi-line input that reaches it.

items.title: fix(dedup): rank a relative source_file against the scan root, not the CWD (#4281)

labels.name: needs:title
labels.description: PR title should follow the conventional-commit format

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4281. Fixes the subdirectory case @gmos found in #4282 ([comment](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/pull/4282#issuecomment-6101831797)), which is still on v8 in 0.9.85. It does not touch the remaining `a/x.md` vs `b/x.md` case.

By dedup time a node's `source_file` is already root-relative, but `_rank_path` still called `.resolve()` on it, which prepends the CWD. When graphify starts from a subdirectory of the root, the renamed `x.html` node gets its own id but none of its edges.

```diff
 _rank_path(source_file, root)
-  if root and normalized:
+  if root and normalized and normalized is absolute:
     return normalized.resolve().relative_to(root)
   return normalized
```

Run from `root/firmware`:

| | node key | edge key | edge lands on |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | `firmware/firmware/lib/portal.html` | `firmware/lib/portal.html` | `firmware_lib_portal` |
| after | `firmware/lib/portal.html` | `firmware/lib/portal.html` | `firmware_lib_portal_html` |

I left `_source_key` in `extractors/resolution.py` alone. At extraction time a relative path is still CWD-relative, so resolving it there is right. The `_rank_path` docstring said it mirrored `_source_key`; it now says how they differ.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

A node and the edges from its file must get the same `_rank_path` key, whatever directory graphify runs from.

The regression test is #4282's absolute-edge-path test plus `monkeypatch.chdir(root / "firmware")`. It is committed before the fix, so checking out `f369742` alone shows it failing.

`_collision_rank` uses the same key, so the winner of a collision between relative paths no longer depends on the CWD either. Nothing persisted changes; the keys exist only inside dedup.

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test**.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_dedup.py                  # test commit only: 1 failed; with fix: 109 passed
uv run --python 3.10 pytest tests/test_dedup.py    # 109 passed
uv run --python 3.13 pytest tests/test_dedup.py    # 109 passed
uv run pytest tests                                # 6956 passed, 167 skipped
uv run ruff check .                                # all checks passed
uv run pyright graphify/dedup.py                   # 5 errors, the same 5 as on v8
```

## Limitations

Reverting the one condition restores the old behavior. Only dedup is affected. A relative path containing `..` is no longer normalized here; nodes are relativized before dedup, so stored paths shouldn't contain one.

items.title: [Bug]: one edited file still costs a full   rebuild, so a warm graphify update goes from 2 s back to 68 s

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

v0.9.96 already skips a run where nothing changed. #4748 put a gate at the top of
`_rebuild_code` (graphify/watch.py:2081) that compares the manifest's per-file
`ast_hash` and a build-state stamp, then returns early.

That gate asks one yes/no question. Edit a file and it declines, so the run takes
the full path: detect, extract, build, cluster, analyze, report, export over the
whole corpus. One edited file costs what a cold build costs.

Same tree, 1,059 scanned files, one process per run:

| run | wall | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| warm, nothing changed (gate) | 1.96 s | 46 MB |
| two files edited | 68.15 s | 1,071 MB |

Nothing derives a change set. The manifest stores a content hash per file, and
`_rebuild_code` already accepts `changed_paths`; the only caller that passes one is
the post-commit hook, which gets it from `git diff`. `graphify update` passes
nothing (graphify/cli.py:2877), which the function documents as "the full code
corpus".

Expected: a run with two changed files re-extracts those two files.


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
### Steps to reproduce


# graphify v8 at dac06345 (0.9.96), from a source checkout
# in a repo of about a thousand files:
graphify update .                      # cold build
graphify update .                      # warm: the gate skips, about 2 s
printf '\n# note\n' >> src/a.py
printf '\n# note\n' >> src/b.py
graphify update .                      # back to the full pipeline, about 68 s


Neither `--force` nor `changed_paths` is passed. `detect()` runs again, `extract()`
is handed the whole corpus, and build, cluster, analyze and report work over every
node. The call site is the `update` command:


# graphify/cli.py:2877
ok = _rebuild_code(watch_path, force=force, no_cluster=no_cluster, block_on_lock=True)
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
### Output

Same tree, 1,059 scanned files, one process per run.


# nothing changed
[graphify watch] No relevant changes; graphify-out left untouched.
1.96 s, peak RSS 46 MB

# two files edited, current v8
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 22025 nodes, 47132 edges, 1031 communities
68.15 s, peak RSS 1,071 MB

# two files edited, with a manifest-derived change set (prototype, not on v8)
[graphify watch] Incremental: re-extracting 2 of 1059 scanned files that changed since the last build.
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 22026 nodes, 47135 edges, 1017 communities
48.72 s, peak RSS 537 MB


19 of the 68 seconds, and half the memory. The rest is the pipeline after
extraction, which still runs over every node.

The one extra node in the third run is the pre-existing `any` residue: v8 with an
explicit `changed_paths` produces it too, so it is not something the change set
introduces.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.96

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

Reproduced on a clean checkout of v8 (`dac06345`, 0.9.96), on a copy of this
repository's tracked files with `worked/` removed: 1,059 scanned files, 583 of them
code. No provider environment variables involved, `update` is AST-only, and every
measurement is one process with no other load.

The warm rows are the second of two consecutive runs in the same tree, so the gate
sees an untouched output fingerprint. Copying a built tree with `cp -r` is not
equivalent: the copy gets new mtimes, the gate declines, and the run looks slow for
a reason that has nothing to do with this issue.


### Additional context

**Why this is separate from #4748.** That PR answers "did anything change?" and
shipped in 0.9.96. The maintainer closed #4769 as superseded by it, because the two
look like the same work. They cover different cases: #4748 returns early only when
every scanned file already matches the manifest. One edited file leaves that early
return, and the whole cost returns with it. That is the 2 s to 68 s above.

**What a change set would be.** Content-addressed, from the manifest: rows whose
`ast_hash` moved, plus rows whose file is gone from disk. A deleted row has to be in
the set, or its nodes survive and the shrink guard refuses the write. The unchanged
corpus's AST nodes go to `extract()` as resolution context, or a call from a changed
file into an unchanged one loses its edge (#2406). A missing or unreadable manifest,
`--force`, and an explicit `changed_paths` all keep the full path.

**What it does not fix.** Extraction is only part of the run. Build, cluster,
analyze, report and export still work over every node, which is why 68 s becomes
49 s rather than seconds. On this corpus the JS/TS resolution pass re-parses the
TypeScript files too, because those suffixes bypass the AST cache on purpose. A
corpus where the graph stages dominate would gain less than this one.

**Related.** #4740 is the umbrella. #4748 shipped the no-change gate. #4769 was the
change-set attempt, closed as superseded. #2543 is why a corpus holding a file that
never extracts can never take the skip.

Found while working through #4740.

items.title: [Bug]: one SQL table becomes one node per file that reads it, and a schema-qualified read never binds to its definition

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

### What happened?

A SQL table that no file defines, read from N files, becomes N nodes. A
schema-qualified read (`dbo.Customers`) never binds to the `CREATE TABLE`
in another file. A plain read (`Invoices`) binds to a Python class of the
same name.

A project with five files:

```text
tables/customers.sql   CREATE TABLE dbo.Customers (Id INT PRIMARY KEY);
views/active.sql       CREATE VIEW dbo.ActiveCustomers AS SELECT Id FROM dbo.Customers;
views/open_orders.sql  CREATE VIEW dbo.OpenOrders AS SELECT Id FROM dbo.Orders;
views/late_orders.sql  CREATE VIEW dbo.LateOrders AS SELECT Id FROM dbo.Orders;
views/recent.sql       CREATE VIEW dbo.Recent AS SELECT Id FROM Invoices;
app/models.py          class Invoices: pass
```

On v8 the `reads_from` edges are:

```text
dbo.ActiveCustomers  reads_from  dbo_customers
dbo.LateOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.OpenOrders       reads_from  views_open_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.Recent           reads_from  app_models_invoices
```

- `dbo_customers` is a stub with no `source_file`. The real table is
  `tables_customers_dbo_customers`, so there are two `dbo.Customers` nodes
  and the view points at the empty one.
- No file defines `dbo.Orders`, so the two views get two nodes,
  `views_open_orders_sql_dbo_orders` and `views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders`.
  A query by either id finds one view. Neither finds both.
- `dbo.Recent` reads `Invoices`, a table no `.sql` file defines, and the
  edge lands on `app_models_invoices`, the Python class in
  `app/models.py`.

Three causes:

1. Stubs with the same id and no `source_file` are salted apart by
   `origin_file` in `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids`
   (graphify/extractors/resolution.py:1060), so each file gets its own
   stub for the same table.
2. `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` (graphify/extract.py:3924, called at
   :10189) only rewires a stub to a definition that
   `_is_type_like_definition` accepts. That check returns False for any
   label with a `.` (graphify/extractors/resolution.py:1201), and a SQL
   table is `schema.name`, so `dbo.Customers` never rewires.
3. `.sql` is not in `_LANG_FAMILY_BY_EXT` (graphify/extract.py:3801), so
   the cross-language guard doesn't apply to SQL nodes and `Invoices`
   binds to the Python class.

Expected: one node per table across the project. A read binds to the
`CREATE TABLE` when exactly one file defines it, and never to a
definition in another language.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
### Steps to reproduce


# graphify v8 at 847a93f3, from a source checkout
# create the five files listed above, then, from that folder:
GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none graphify update .
python -c "
import json
g = json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json'))
nodes = g['nodes']
edges = g.get('links') or g.get('edges')
label = {n['id']: n['label'] for n in nodes}
for k in ('dbo.customers', 'dbo.orders', 'invoices'):
    ms = [n for n in nodes if n['label'].lower() == k]
    print(k, len(ms), [(n['id'], n.get('source_file')) for n in ms])
for e in edges:
    if e['relation'] == 'reads_from':
        print(label[e['source']], e['relation'], e['target'])"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
### Error output or graph output

`graphify update .` prints `Rebuilt: 15 nodes, 10 edges, 5 communities`.
The script above then prints:


dbo.customers 2 [('dbo_customers', ''), ('tables_customers_dbo_customers', 'tables/customers.sql')]
dbo.orders 2 [('views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders', ''), ('views_open_orders_sql_dbo_orders', '')]
invoices 1 [('app_models_invoices', 'app/models.py')]
dbo.ActiveCustomers reads_from dbo_customers
dbo.LateOrders reads_from views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.OpenOrders reads_from views_open_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.Recent reads_from app_models_invoices


The edges into `dbo.Orders`: `views_open_orders_sql_dbo_orders` has one
reader, `dbo.OpenOrders`, and `views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders` has one
reader, `dbo.LateOrders`.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.93

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables involved. Reproduced on a clean checkout
of v8 (847a93f3).


### Additional context

### Additional context

On `microsoft/sql-server-samples` `wide-world-importers/wwi-ssdt` (336
`.sql` files), v8 has 172 table-like nodes for 79 distinct tables, and 25
tables are split across several nodes. `application.cities` has 7 nodes
and `application.deliverymethods` has 10.

The `.` check in `_is_type_like_definition` came in with `e44e6e98`. C#,
Elixir and Julia also produce dotted labels, so a fix should relax the
check only for `.sql` nodes.

Found while fixing #4635.

items.title: [Bug]: a GO line with no `;` before it swallows the next T-SQL statement, so its table, view and edges vanish

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

### What happened?

In a T-SQL script, a `GO` line with no `;` before it hides every
statement after it. The tables and views after the first `GO` get no
node, and their edges are lost or land on the wrong node.

```sql
SET NOCOUNT ON
GO
CREATE TABLE dbo.Customers (Id INT PRIMARY KEY)
GO
CREATE TABLE dbo.Orders (Id INT, CustomerId INT REFERENCES dbo.Customers(Id))
GO
CREATE VIEW dbo.OpenOrders AS SELECT Id FROM dbo.Orders
GO
```

v8 gives two nodes, `schema.sql` and `dbo.Customers`, and one edge,
`dbo.Customers references dbo.Customers`. `dbo.Orders` and
`dbo.OpenOrders` are missing, and the foreign key from `dbo.Orders` is
attached to `dbo.Customers` itself.

`GO` is not SQL. It is a command for sqlcmd and SSMS that means "send the
batch so far". tree-sitter-sql has no rule for it, so it reads `GO` as an
identifier. Without a `;`, the statement doesn't end there. The parser
puts `GO` and everything after it in one ERROR node, and
`extract_sql` (graphify/extractors/sql.py) reads nothing from that node.
The parse happens at `sql.py:317`, and nothing before it knows about `GO`.

Expected: each statement between `GO` lines is read as its own
statement, with or without a `;`.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
### Steps to reproduce


# graphify v8 at 847a93f3, from a source checkout
# save the script above as schema.sql, then:
python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract_sql
r = extract_sql(Path('schema.sql'))
print(sorted(n['label'] for n in r['nodes']))"
# -> ['dbo.Customers', 'schema.sql']


Ending each statement with `;` before the `GO` gives all four nodes.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
### Error output or graph output


v8:
  nodes: dbo.Customers, schema.sql
  dbo.Customers  references  dbo.Customers

with each GO line read as the end of a statement:
  nodes: dbo.Customers, dbo.OpenOrders, dbo.Orders, schema.sql
  dbo.Orders      references  dbo.Customers
  dbo.OpenOrders  reads_from  dbo.Orders
```

### Graphify version

0.9.93

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables involved. Reproduced on a clean checkout
of v8 (847a93f3).


### Additional context

### Additional context

Projects scripted by SSMS or SSDT end most statements with `GO` and no
`;`. SSMS also writes `SET ANSI_NULLS ON` / `GO` and
`SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON` / `GO` before every object, so one script can
lose everything after its first line.

On `microsoft/sql-server-samples` `wide-world-importers/wwi-ssdt` (336
`.sql` files), reading `GO` lines as statement ends adds 29 nodes and 29
non-`contains` edges (739 -> 768 nodes, 146 -> 175 edges).

A `go` on its own line can also be a column or alias:

```sql
SELECT a.id,
 go
FROM dbo.A a
```

That `go` comes right after a comma, so a fix can tell it apart: a `GO`
line is a separator unless a `,` comes right before it or a `,` or `)`
right after it. Keywords don't help: `SET NOCOUNT ON` / `GO` is a real
separator.

Found while fixing #4635.

items.title: [Bug]: install and wheel tests write into the package and the repo build/, so a killed or concurrent run breaks the checkout

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Two test fixtures write into folders that every process shares: the
installed package and the repo's own `build/`. One serial pytest run passes.
A killed run, or two runs on the same checkout, break in ways the suite
doesn't report.

**1. The real `graphify/skills/claude` bundle is moved out of the package.**

The `fake_bundle` fixture in tests/test_install_references.py (lines 31-64),
and `test_hard_fail_when_bundle_dir_present_but_references_missing` (line
180), do this:

```text
shutil.move(graphify/skills/claude -> a mkdtemp() backup)
write a fake bundle in its place
run the test
move the real bundle back      <- in finally
```

`finally` doesn't run when the process gets SIGTERM, which is what `kill`
and `timeout` send. Python has no handler for it, so the process ends where
it is. The fake bundle stays in the package, the real files stay in a
backup under the temp dir, and `git status` shows them as deleted and
modified. Ctrl-C (SIGINT) is fine: Python raises `KeyboardInterrupt`, and
the fixture restores the bundle on the way out.

While the bundle is moved away, any other process that reads the package
fails. That includes a second pytest run on the same checkout.

**2. Wheel builds share the repo's `build/` folder.**

The `wheel_namelist` fixture in tests/test_wheel_packaging.py (lines 55-66)
runs `python -m build --wheel --no-isolation --outdir <tmp> <repo>`. The
wheel lands in `<tmp>`, but setuptools still works in `<repo>/build/`. Two
builds at once on one checkout delete each other's files. The fixture then
calls `pytest.skip` for every dependent test, so the run that lost reports
133 skips and no failure.

Expected: a killed or concurrent test run leaves the checkout unchanged,
and a broken wheel build shows up as a failure, not a skip.


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# graphify v8 at 86c57be8, from a source checkout, serial (no -n)

# 1a. Kill pytest during a fake_bundle test.
#     pause.py pauses inside the test, after the fixture has moved the bundle:
cat > /tmp/pause.py <<'EOF'
import os, time, pytest
@pytest.hookimpl(hookwrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_call(item):
    open("/tmp/paused", "w").write(str(os.getpid()))
    time.sleep(60)
    yield
EOF
rm -f /tmp/paused
PYTHONPATH=/tmp pytest -p pause -p no:randomly \
  "tests/test_install_references.py::test_install_stages_references_sidecar" &
while [ ! -f /tmp/paused ]; do sleep 0.2; done
kill -TERM "$(cat /tmp/paused)"
git status --short graphify/skills/claude     # D and M lines
pytest -p no:randomly tests/test_install_references.py tests/test_install.py
# -> 3 failed, 133 passed, 1 skipped   (intact checkout: 136 passed, 1 skipped)
git checkout -- graphify/skills/claude        # restore

# 1b. Two serial runs on one checkout at the same time.
for i in $(seq 30); do pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/test_install_references.py; done &
for i in $(seq 30); do pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/test_install.py; done

# 2. Two wheel-test runs at the same time.
rm -rf build
pytest -rs -p no:randomly tests/test_wheel_packaging.py --basetemp=/tmp/w1 &
pytest -rs -p no:randomly tests/test_wheel_packaging.py --basetemp=/tmp/w2
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
1a. Stopped while the fake bundle is in place, 3 runs each:
    SIGINT      exit 2    bundle restored
    SIGTERM     exit 143  fake bundle left behind
    SIGKILL     exit 137  fake bundle left behind
    timeout 30  exit 124  fake bundle left behind (1 run)

    git status:  D graphify/skills/claude/references/add-watch.md
                 D graphify/skills/claude/references/exports.md
                 M graphify/skills/claude/references/extraction-spec.md

1b. test_install.py failed in 6, 3 and 6 of 30 iterations with the other loop

2.  5 of 5 times, one run skipped all 133 tests and the other passed:
```

### Graphify version

0.9.92

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables involved. Reproduced on a clean checkout
of v8 with a fresh venv, using an editable install of that checkout.
`graphify.__file__` pointed into the checkout, so the fixture moved the
checkout's own `graphify/skills/claude`.


### Additional context

Each run had a single pytest process, except 1b and 2, where two serial
processes ran at the same time. Under `pytest -n` both problems show up in
one command: install tests fail with the same `shutil.Error`, and about 110
wheel tests are skipped.

A CI job that hits its time limit gets SIGTERM, so it can leave a cached
checkout in the 1a state. A `graphify install` from that checkout would then
copy the fake references, and a wheel built from it ships them
(`test_built_wheel_ships_the_full_skill_payload` fails on that checkout).

Possible fixes:
- Bundle: monkeypatch the package dir the install code reads to a copy
  under `tmp_path`, so nothing in the real package moves.
- Wheel: build from a copy of the repo under `tmp_path`, so `build/` is
  private. Separately, fail instead of skipping when `python -m build` is
  available but the build fails. The `_has_build()` check already covers
  machines without `build`.

items.title: [Bug]: test_the_pool_hands_its_workers_the_overrides never resets _ACTIVE_SCAN_ROOT, so 9 tests fail in a different order

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`test_the_pool_hands_its_workers_the_overrides` in
tests/test_language_overrides.py leaves `_ACTIVE_SCAN_ROOT` set to its own
tmp dir after it finishes. Any test that runs after it and expects
`active_scan_root()` to be None fails: 2 tests in
test_extractor_scan_root_context.py and 7 XAML tests in test_dotnet.py.

The default test order never runs those files right after the leaking test,
so a normal `pytest` run passes. A different order fails in one serial
process, with no xdist.

The test swaps `ProcessPoolExecutor` for a `ThreadPoolExecutor` subclass so
it can record the pool's initializer. The 25 extractions then run as threads
in the test process. Each one goes through `_safe_extract_with_xaml_root`
in graphify/extract.py:

```python
previous_root = set_active_scan_root(root.resolve())
try:
    return _safe_extract(extractor, path, scan_root=root)
finally:
    set_active_scan_root(previous_root)
```

`_ACTIVE_SCAN_ROOT` is one module global in graphify/extractors/base.py, so
the threads share it. When two calls overlap, the second saves the first
one's root as `previous_root` and restores it last:

```text
thread A: previous = None, set root
thread B: previous = root, set root
thread A: restore None
thread B: restore root      <- still set after extract() returns
```

With the pool forced to one thread, the global ends as None (3 of 3 runs).
With the default thread count, it ends as the tmp dir (3 of 3 runs).

Expected: the global is None again after the test, whatever order the
tests run in.


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# graphify v8 at 86c57be8, from a source checkout, serial (no -n)
pytest -p no:randomly \
  "tests/test_language_overrides.py::test_the_pool_hands_its_workers_the_overrides" \
  tests/test_extractor_scan_root_context.py tests/test_dotnet.py
# -> 9 failed, 42 passed   (3 of 3 runs)

pytest -p no:randomly tests/test_extractor_scan_root_context.py tests/test_dotnet.py
# -> 50 passed             (3 of 3 runs)

# Full suite in random order, serial:
pytest -p randomly --randomly-seed=2
# -> 9 failed, 8383 passed, 14 skipped: the same 9 tests
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
FAILED tests/test_extractor_scan_root_context.py::test_active_scan_root_defaults_to_none
FAILED tests/test_extractor_scan_root_context.py::test_active_scan_root_set_get_restore_nested
FAILED tests/test_dotnet.py  (7 XAML tests: viewmodel and DataContext linking,
       the CommunityToolkit link, prune-noise-dirs, non-UTF-8 code-behind)

active_scan_root() after the leaking test:
/var/tmp/.../test_the_pool_hands_its_worker0
```

### Graphify version

0.9.92

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables involved. Reproduced on a clean checkout
of v8 with a fresh venv.


### Additional context

Only the test is affected. Real runs extract through `ProcessPoolExecutor`,
and each worker process has its own copy of the global. I found no thread
pool on that path.

Two ways to fix it:
- In the test, run the pool with `max_workers=1`, or reset `_ACTIVE_SCAN_ROOT`
  afterwards with `monkeypatch`.
- In the code, make the scan root a `contextvars.ContextVar`, so each thread
  has its own value. This also protects any later caller that runs
  `extract()` from several threads.

Found while timing the suite. Under `pytest -n` it shows up on whichever
worker runs these files after the leaking test.

items.title: [Bug]: hooks never rebuild after a clean cherry-pick, a rebase, or git pull --rebase

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

After a clean `git cherry-pick`, a `git rebase` or a `git pull --rebase`, the hooks from `graphify hook install` never launch a rebuild. `graph.json` keeps describing the old code until the next plain commit or branch switch. There are two causes:

1. **Cherry-pick.** `post-commit` exits on `[ -f "$GIT_DIR/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" ] && exit 0` (`graphify/hooks.py:448`). git still has `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` on disk while `post-commit` runs, even when the pick finished cleanly. This is the same pattern as #4463 with `MERGE_HEAD`. For a range (`git cherry-pick A..B`), every pick hits it, the last one included.
2. **Rebase.** During a rebase, `post-checkout` (`hooks.py:538`) and every `post-commit` (`hooks.py:445`) see `rebase-merge/` and exit. That part is intended. But git's hook for "the rebase is finished" is `post-rewrite`, and `install()` never installs one (`hooks.py:1031-1034` installs post-commit, post-checkout and post-merge only). So nothing rebuilds at the end. `git pull --rebase` goes the same way.

- A conflicted single pick works today: when you finish it with `--continue` or `git commit`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` is already gone, so `post-commit` rebuilds. Only the clean pick is broken.
- `git commit --amend` works: `post-commit` rebuilds once.

Expected: every git operation that changes the tree launches one rebuild when it finishes.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
git init -q -b main demo && cd demo
mkdir graphify-out && echo '{}' > graphify-out/graph.json
echo 'def a(): pass' > a.py && git add . && git commit -qm init
graphify hook install

# clean cherry-pick
export GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1
git checkout -qb side && echo 'def b(): pass' > b.py && git add . && git commit -qm b
git checkout -q main
unset GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK
git cherry-pick side 2>&1 | grep -c "launching background rebuild"   # 0

# rebase
export GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1
git checkout -qb feat && echo 'def f(): pass' > f.py && git add . && git commit -qm f
git checkout -q main && echo 'def m(): pass' > m.py && git add . && git commit -qm m
git checkout -q feat
unset GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK
git rebase main 2>&1 | grep -c "launching background rebuild"        # 0

# control
echo 'def z(): pass' > z.py && git add z.py
git commit -qm z 2>&1 | grep -c "launching background rebuild"       # 1
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Rebuild launch lines in git's output, v8 10130e79:

operation              rebuilds launched
plain commit           1
git commit --amend     1
git cherry-pick X      0
git cherry-pick A..B   0
git rebase main        0
git pull --rebase      0

State files on disk while each hook runs (probe hook, git 2.54.0):

operation           hook                       on disk
cherry-pick X       post-commit                CHERRY_PICK_HEAD
cherry-pick A..B    post-commit (every pick)   CHERRY_PICK_HEAD sequencer/
rebase main         post-checkout              rebase-merge/
                    post-commit (every pick)   rebase-merge/ CHERRY_PICK_HEAD
                    post-rewrite, $1=rebase    rebase-merge/
commit --amend      post-commit                none
                    post-rewrite, $1=amend     none
```

### Graphify version

0.9.91

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

git 2.54.0. No provider environment variables needed: the bug is in the shell hooks, before Python runs. Reproduced on a clean worktree of v8 10130e79.

### Additional context

Found while writing #4476 (the #4463 fix).

The probe shows two traps for a fix:
- A new `post-rewrite` hook can't copy the existing `rebase-merge` check, because `rebase-merge/` is still on disk when it runs.
- It must ignore `$1 = amend`, because `post-commit` already rebuilt.

Simply dropping the `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` check is not safe. With a tracked `graphify-out/graph.json`, a rebuild between picks dirties it. A later pick that touches it is then refused with `error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: graphify-out/graph.json`. v8 completes the same sequence.

What I tested locally, with 7 launch-count tests, 12 edge cases and `tests/test_hooks.py`, all passing:
- `post-commit`: skip while `sequencer/todo` has more than one line. On the last pick, diff from `$(cat "$GIT_DIR/sequencer/head")` (the HEAD before the sequence started) instead of `HEAD~1`. A range then gets one rebuild covering every pick, and nothing rebuilds mid-sequence.
- A `post-rewrite` hook that acts only on `$1 = rebase`.
- Results are the same stacked on #4476.

Two gaps remain, on v8 and with the fix: `--skip` on the last pick and `--quit`. git runs no hook when a sequence ends that way.

Side notes:
- `git commit --amend` on a repo's first commit never rebuilds. `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD` has no parent to diff against, and the fallback diff is empty.
- The comment "git exports GIT_DIR to hooks" doesn't hold in a normal repo. `GIT_DIR` was empty in every probe, so the `git rev-parse` fallback runs on every hook.

items.title: [Bug]: backticks in two skill comments make bash run `graphify update` and `changed` mid-merge

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Two skill blocks run Python as `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "..."`. The Python source is in double quotes, and bash still expands backticks inside double quotes. Two comments in that source have backticks:

1. Part C (merge AST + semantic): ``# `graphify update` deleted it along with the re-extracted code file it``. Source: `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md:317`, `core/aider.md:378`, `core/devin.md:442`. It is in 15 generated skills. `skill-windows.md` is not affected: its Part C is a single-quoted PowerShell here-string.
2. The `--update` merge block: ``# Do NOT add `changed` here: ...``. Source: `tools/skillgen/fragments/references/shared/update.md:110`. It is in all 14 `skills/<host>/references/update.md`, windows included.

Bash runs `graphify update` and `changed` before Python starts, in the current folder, and pastes their output into the Python source.

- With `graphify` on PATH (anyone who installed it), a full `graphify update` runs in the middle of Part C and rewrites `graph.json`. Its output has several lines. The first lands in the comment, the rest are pasted into the code, and Part C fails with `SyntaxError`. `.graphify_extract.json` is never written, so the merge cannot run.
- Without `graphify` on PATH, bash prints `command not found` and Python runs normally. That is why this went unnoticed.
- `changed` is usually not a command, so it only prints `command not found`. If a program named `changed` is on PATH, the `--update` merge fails the same way.

Expected: bash runs nothing inside these blocks, and Part C hands Python exactly the code the skill shows.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# Minimal: a fake graphify that logs its call
mkdir -p bin
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "RAN graphify $*" >> log\n' > bin/graphify
chmod +x bin/graphify
PATH=$PWD/bin:$PATH bash -c 'python3 -c "
# `graphify update` deleted it
print(\"python ran\")
"'
cat log    # RAN graphify update

# Real case: in a project with a previous graphify build and one edited .py file,
# with graphify installed, run Part C copied verbatim from graphify/skill.md (lines 377-417 on v8 fe085ced).
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Real graphify on PATH, Part C on v8 fe085ced:

  File "<string>", line 13
    [graphify watch] 3 file(s) not classified (no supported extension or shebang), skipped: ...
     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?

exit 1. graph.json was rewritten by the update bash ran. .graphify_extract.json was not written.

setup                                   command bash ran   Part C exit   result
graphify not on PATH                    none               0             "graphify: command not found", merge OK
fake graphify, prints 1 line            graphify update    0             works by luck, the line lands in the comment
fake graphify, prints 3 lines           graphify update    1             SyntaxError
real graphify on PATH                   graphify update    1             graph.json rewritten, then SyntaxError
fake changed, prints 3 lines (update)   changed            1             SyntaxError, graph.json untouched
```

### Graphify version

0.9.90 

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables needed; the bug is in bash, before Python runs. Reproduced on a clean worktree of v8 fe085ced.


### Additional context

Found while writing the test for #4456: its CI failed because the runner had `graphify` on PATH. That test keeps `graphify` off PATH for now.

The `# Save scan root so \`graphify update\` ...` lines (Step 1, `shell/posix.md`, `shell/powershell.md`) are plain shell comments outside quotes. Bash does not run them; checked with the same fake.

I have a fix ready: drop the backticks on those 4 source lines, regenerate, and add a test that fails on any backtick inside a double-quoted `-c "..."` block. PR to follow.

items.title: [Bug]: /graphify skill "Step 1 - Ensure graphify is installed" exits 0 and leaves empty graphify-out files when a write fails; .graphify_root readers trim folder names

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Step 1 of the `/graphify` skill ("Step 1 - Ensure graphify is installed") saves two files that every later step depends on:

- `graphify-out/.graphify_python`: which Python to run
- `graphify-out/.graphify_root`: which folder is being scanned

There are two bugs around these files.

**Bug 1: Step 1 reports success when it can't write them**

Actual: Step 1 writes each file with `open(path, 'w').write(...)`. Opening the file creates it right away, so when the write fails (for example on a full disk), Python prints `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device`, but the empty file stays behind and Step 1 exits 0. After that:

- Every later step runs `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "..."`, which becomes an empty command. Bash prints `bash: : command not found`, and nothing points back to Step 1 or the full disk.
- `graphify update` with no path reads the empty `.graphify_root` as `Path("")`, which is the current directory, so it rebuilds whatever folder you're in instead of the project, without a warning.

The Windows version of Step 1 does the same: `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` throws, PowerShell prints the error, and the script keeps going.

Expected: if Step 1 can't write a file, it exits non-zero with a message naming the file (for example `could not write graphify-out/.graphify_root (disk full?)`), and it doesn't leave an empty file behind.

**Bug 2: readers trim spaces off the saved folder name**

Actual: Linux and macOS allow a folder name to end with a space, such as `proj `. Step 1 saves the path exactly, but `graphify update` (`cli.py`), `_infer_merge_root` (`build.py`) and both git hook scripts (`hooks.py`) read it back with `.strip()` and get `proj`. If a `proj` folder also exists, they work on that folder instead.

Expected: readers use the path exactly as Step 1 saved it. They only remove a UTF-8 byte-order mark (added by Windows PowerShell 5.1, see #3028) and a trailing newline.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
Linux, from the root of a `v8` checkout (commit `b4e6307`). No root access needed. The full disk is a private 2 MB filesystem that disappears when the command ends.

**Setup (both bugs):** save Step 1 from the skill to a script.


python3 - > /tmp/step1.sh <<'EOF'
import re
text = open("graphify/skill.md").read()
blocks = re.findall(r"\n(.*?)\n", text, re.S)
print(next(b for b in blocks if "graphify_root" in b))
EOF


**Bug 1: run Step 1 on a full disk**


unshare -rm bash -c '
  mkdir -p /tmp/fullfs && mount -t tmpfs -o size=2M tmpfs /tmp/fullfs
  mkdir -p "/tmp/fullfs/work/my project"
  dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/fullfs/fill bs=64k 2>/dev/null   # fill the disk
  cd /tmp/fullfs/work
  sed "s|^INPUT_PATH\$|/tmp/fullfs/work/my project|" /tmp/step1.sh > /dev/shm/step1.sh
  bash /dev/shm/step1.sh; echo "Step 1 exit code: $?"
  stat -c "%s bytes  %n" graphify-out/.graphify_python graphify-out/.graphify_root
  $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "print(1)"; echo "next step exit code: $?"
'


Output:


OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device      (printed twice)
Step 1 exit code: 0
0 bytes  graphify-out/.graphify_python
0 bytes  graphify-out/.graphify_root
bash: line 9: : command not found
next step exit code: 127


**Bug 2: a folder name ending in a space**


mkdir -p /tmp/sp/"proj " /tmp/sp/proj && cd /tmp/sp
sed "s|^INPUT_PATH\$|/tmp/sp/proj |" /tmp/step1.sh | bash
python3 -c "
from pathlib import Path
saved = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig')
print('Step 1 saved:', repr(saved))
print('readers get: ', repr(saved.strip()))
"


Output:


Step 1 saved: '/tmp/sp/proj '
readers get:  '/tmp/sp/proj'


`/tmp/sp/proj` is a different, existing folder, so `graphify update` and the git hooks would work on it instead of `proj `.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
**Bug 1: what Step 1 prints on a full disk**

Python reports both failed writes, but only as "Exception ignored" while shutting down, so neither the command nor Step 1 fails:


Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='graphify-out/.graphify_python' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='/tmp/fullfs/work/graphify-out/.graphify_root' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
Step 1 exit code: 0


What's left on disk, and what the next step prints:


0 bytes  graphify-out/.graphify_python
0 bytes  graphify-out/.graphify_root
bash: line 9: : command not found
next step exit code: 127


How an empty `.graphify_root` is read by `graphify update` (no path):


Path("") -> current directory


**Bug 2: the saved folder vs. what readers get**


Step 1 saved: '/tmp/sp/proj '
readers get:  '/tmp/sp/proj'      <- a different folder that exists


There's no graph output to show: both bugs happen before or around the graph build, by pointing it at the wrong folder or stopping it with an unclear error.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.85 (v8 branch, commit b4e6307)

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

- Provider environment variables: none set (no OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GRAPHIFY_* or similar). Neither bug involves a provider: both happen in Step 1's file writes and in the readers of `.graphify_root`, before any extraction.
- Clean checkout: yes. Both bugs reproduced in a fresh worktree of `upstream/v8` at `b4e6307`, with no local changes.
- OS: Fedora 43 (Linux, x86_64), bash 5.3. Bug 2 also applies to macOS. Windows doesn't allow trailing spaces in folder names, but its Step 1 has the same write problem as Bug 1 (`WriteAllText` throws and the script continues).
- Full disk was simulated with a private 2 MB tmpfs (`unshare -rm`), as in the steps above. I first hit Bug 1 on a real full `/tmp` while running the test suite.


### Additional context

**Where the code is (line numbers on `v8` at `b4e6307`)**

Bug 1, where Step 1 writes the files. The skill text is generated from these fragments, so a fix goes here and then `python -m tools.skillgen --bless`:

- `tools/skillgen/fragments/shell/posix.md` lines 32-40: writes `.graphify_python` and `.graphify_root` with `open(...).write(...)`
- `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md` and `core/devin.md`: their own copies of Step 1 (ending at lines 100 and 113)
- `tools/skillgen/fragments/shell/powershell.md` lines 59 and 68: the Windows Step 1, writing both files with `WriteAllText`

Bug 2, the readers that call `.strip()` on `.graphify_root`:

- `graphify/cli.py` line 2552: `graphify update` with no path
- `graphify/build.py` line 624: `_infer_merge_root`
- `graphify/hooks.py` lines 227 and 302: the post-commit and post-checkout hook scripts. These are templates copied into `.git/hooks`, so hooks that are already installed keep the old code until they're reinstalled.

**How I found it**

While running the test suite for #4309, `/tmp` filled up, because some tests create a ~168 MB home folder each. After that, `test_step1_still_resolves_a_legitimate_path` started failing with the repo folder where the project folder should be.
